```ts
    // retired_at (3e design, section 6.1): set only by a retirement in the ledger, forced null at insert.
    expect(cfg.columns.map((c) => c.name)).toEqual(["handle_lower", "profile_id", "changed_at", "retired_at"]);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "retired_at")?.notNull).toBe(false);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "retired_at")?.hasDefault).toBe(false);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "handle_lower")?.primary).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "profile_id")?.notNull).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "changed_at")?.notNull).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "changed_at")?.hasDefault).toBe(true);
    const fk = cfg.foreignKeys.map((k) => ({ table: getTableConfig(k.reference().foreignTable).name, columns: k.reference().foreignColumns.map((c) => c.name), onDelete: k.onDelete }));
    expect(fk).toEqual([{ table: "profiles", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "cascade" }]);
    expect(cfg.policies.map((p) => [p.name, p.for])).toEqual([["handle_history_api_all", "all"]]);
  });
  test("profiles record when the handle last changed; users record when their purge finished", () => {
    const handleChangedAt = byName.get("profiles")!.columns.find((c) => c.name === "handle_changed_at");
    expect(handleChangedAt).toBeDefined();
    expect(handleChangedAt?.notNull).toBe(false);
    const purgedAt = byName.get("users")!.columns.find((c) => c.name === "purged_at");
    expect(purgedAt).toBeDefined();
    expect(purgedAt?.notNull).toBe(false);
  });
  test("one phone per account: a unique index on phone_hash that leaves out the accounts without one", () => {
    const idx = byName.get("users")!.indexes.find((i) => i.config.name === "users_phone_hash_idx");
    expect(idx?.config.unique).toBe(true);
    expect(idx?.config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name)).toEqual(["phone_hash"]);
    expect(idx?.config.where).toBeDefined();
  });
  test("email codes can be for deleting the account, and every account event of 1b has a type", () => {
    expect(schema.emailCodePurpose.enumValues).toContain("delete_account");
    const values = schema.authEventType.enumValues;
    expect(values.slice(values.indexOf("not_me"), values.indexOf("account_deleted") + 1)).toEqual([
      "not_me",
      "profile_updated",
      "handle_changed",
      "email_changed",
      "badge_verified",
      "badge_removed",
      "export_created",
      "account_deleted",
    ]);
  });
});

describe("passkeys 1c", () => {
  const column = (table: string, name: string) => byName.get(table)!.columns.find((c) => c.name === name);
  /** The foreign keys of one local column: the table and columns they point at and what a delete there does. */
  const foreignKeys = (table: string, name: string) =>
    byName
      .get(table)!
      .foreignKeys.filter((k) => k.reference().columns.some((c) => c.name === name))
      .map((k) => ({ table: getTableConfig(k.reference().foreignTable).name, columns: k.reference().foreignColumns.map((c) => c.name), onDelete: k.onDelete }));

  test("bytea is the bytea SQL type and hands Buffers both ways", () => {
    const table = pgTable("bytea_probe", { value: bytea("value") });
    const probe = getTableConfig(table).columns[0]!;
    expect(probe.getSQLType()).toBe("bytea");
    const bytes = Buffer.from([0, 1, 254, 255]);
    expect(probe.mapToDriverValue(bytes)).toEqual(bytes);
    // postgres.js already parses bytea into a Buffer; a driver that answers a plain Uint8Array gets one too.
    const read = probe.mapFromDriverValue(new Uint8Array([0, 1, 254, 255]));
    expect(Buffer.isBuffer(read)).toBe(true);
    expect(read).toEqual(bytes);
    expect(probe.mapFromDriverValue(bytes)).toEqual(bytes);
  });

  test("users carry an optional WebAuthn user handle in bytea, unique among the accounts that have one", () => {
    const handle = column("users", "webauthn_user_id");
    expect(handle?.getSQLType()).toBe("bytea");
    expect(handle?.notNull).toBe(false);
    expect(handle?.hasDefault).toBe(false);
    const idx = byName.get("users")!.indexes.find((i) => i.config.name === "users_webauthn_user_id_idx");
    expect(idx?.config.unique).toBe(true);
    expect(idx?.config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name)).toEqual(["webauthn_user_id"]);
    expect(idx?.config.where).toBeDefined();
  });

  test("passkeys record the AAGUID, the backup and verification flags, the creating device and a suspected copy", () => {
    expect(column("passkeys", "aaguid")?.getSQLType()).toBe("uuid");
    expect(column("passkeys", "aaguid")?.notNull).toBe(false);
    for (const name of ["backup_eligible", "uv_initialized"]) {
      expect(column("passkeys", name)?.getSQLType(), name).toBe("boolean");
      expect(column("passkeys", name)?.notNull, name).toBe(true);
      expect(column("passkeys", name)?.default, name).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(column("passkeys", "created_device_id")?.getSQLType()).toBe("uuid");
    expect(column("passkeys", "created_device_id")?.notNull).toBe(false);
    expect(foreignKeys("passkeys", "created_device_id")).toEqual([{ table: "devices", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "set null" }]);
    expect(column("passkeys", "suspect_at")?.getSQLType()).toBe("timestamp with time zone");
    expect(column("passkeys", "suspect_at")?.notNull).toBe(false);
    // One row per credential: the index the foundation created stays.
    const idx = byName.get("passkeys")!.indexes.find((i) => i.config.name === "passkeys_credential_idx");
    expect(idx?.config.unique).toBe(true);
    expect(idx?.config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name)).toEqual(["credential_id"]);
  });

  test("sessions carry a random handle that is unique, the factors they proved and the passkey that started them", () => {
    const handle = column("sessions", "handle");
    expect(handle?.getSQLType()).toBe("uuid");
    expect(handle?.notNull).toBe(true);
    expect(handle?.hasDefault).toBe(true);
    const idx = byName.get("sessions")!.indexes.find((i) => i.config.name === "sessions_handle_idx");
    expect(idx?.config.unique).toBe(true);
    expect(idx?.config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name)).toEqual(["handle"]);
    const factors = column("sessions", "factors");
    expect(factors?.getSQLType()).toBe("jsonb");
    expect(factors?.notNull).toBe(true);
    expect(factors?.hasDefault).toBe(true);
    expect(column("sessions", "passkey_id")?.notNull).toBe(false);
    expect(foreignKeys("sessions", "passkey_id")).toEqual([{ table: "passkeys", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "set null" }]);
  });

  test("adding, removing and a counter regression of a passkey are security events", () => {
    const values = schema.authEventType.enumValues;
    // The slice ends at 1c's last value: 3a appends the staff events after it.
    expect(values.slice(values.indexOf("account_deleted"), values.indexOf("passkey_counter_regression") + 1)).toEqual([
      "account_deleted",
      "passkey_added",
      "passkey_removed",
      "passkey_counter_regression",
    ]);
  });
});

describe("explore 2c", () => {
  const column = (table: string, name: string) => byName.get(table)!.columns.find((c) => c.name === name);
  /** Name, SQL type and not-null of every column, in order. */
  const shape = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.columns.map((c) => [c.name, c.getSQLType(), c.notNull]);
  /** Every foreign key of a table by its local column: the table and columns it points at and what a delete there does. */
  const foreignKeys = (table: string) =>
    Object.fromEntries(
      byName.get(table)!.foreignKeys.map((k) => {
        const ref = k.reference();
        return [ref.columns.map((c) => c.name).join(","), { table: getTableConfig(ref.foreignTable).name, columns: ref.foreignColumns.map((c) => c.name), onDelete: k.onDelete }];
      }),
    );
  const indexColumns = (config: { columns: unknown[] }) => config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name);

  test("profiles carry the author's Explore switch, on by default", () => {
    const flag = column("profiles", "show_in_explore");
    expect(flag?.getSQLType()).toBe("boolean");
    expect(flag?.notNull).toBe(true);
    expect(flag?.default).toBe(true);
  });

  test("explore_runs numbers each ranking with an identity and records its time, formula, counts and duration", () => {
    const cfg = byName.get("explore_runs")!;
    expect(cfg.schema).toBeUndefined(); // public
    expect(shape("explore_runs")).toEqual([
      ["generation", "integer", true],
      ["as_of", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["formula", "smallint", true],
      ["candidates", "integer", true],
      ["items", "integer", true],
      ["took_ms", "integer", true],
    ]);
    const generation = column("explore_runs", "generation");
    expect(generation?.primary).toBe(true);
    // Always generated: an insert cannot choose its generation, so the numbers come from the sequence alone.
    expect(generation?.generatedIdentity?.type).toBe("always");
    // The refresh writes every other value itself, the refresh time included, which tests move.
    expect(cfg.columns.filter((c) => c.hasDefault).map((c) => c.name)).toEqual(["generation"]);
    expect(cfg.foreignKeys).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("explore_items holds a ranking's posts by position, each post once, and goes with its ranking, its post or its author", () => {
    const cfg = byName.get("explore_items")!;
    expect(cfg.schema).toBeUndefined(); // public
    // No score or count is stored: the position is the order.
    expect(shape("explore_items")).toEqual([
      ["generation", "integer", true],
      ["position", "integer", true],
      ["post_id", "uuid", true],
      ["author_id", "uuid", true],
    ]);
    expect(cfg.primaryKeys.map((k) => k.columns.map((c) => c.name))).toEqual([["generation", "position"]]);
    expect(cfg.indexes.map((i) => [i.config.name, indexColumns(i.config), i.config.unique])).toEqual([["explore_items_generation_post_idx", ["generation", "post_id"], true]]);
    expect(foreignKeys("explore_items")).toEqual({
      generation: { table: "explore_runs", columns: ["generation"], onDelete: "cascade" },
      post_id: { table: "posts", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "cascade" },
      author_id: { table: "profiles", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "cascade" },
    });
  });

  test("both tables have row level security and one full-access policy for the API role", () => {
    // The loop under "row level security" covers them too; this pins the policy each one has.
    for (const name of ["explore_runs", "explore_items"]) {
      const cfg = byName.get(name)!;
      expect(cfg.enableRLS, name).toBe(true);
      expect(cfg.policies.map((p) => [p.name, p.for, p.to]), name).toEqual([[`${name}_api_all`, "all", apiRole]]);
    }
  });

  test("likes and reposts have a BRIN index on created_at for the refresh's window; bookmarks, which Explore never reads, has none", () => {
    for (const name of ["likes", "reposts"]) {
      const brin = byName.get(name)!.indexes.filter((i) => i.config.method === "brin");
      expect(brin.map((i) => [i.config.name, indexColumns(i.config), i.config.unique, i.config.where]), name).toEqual([[`${name}_created_brin`, ["created_at"], false, undefined]]);
    }
    expect(byName.get("bookmarks")!.indexes.filter((i) => i.config.method === "brin")).toEqual([]);
    // The factory's other indexes stay the same on all three tables.
    for (const name of ["likes", "reposts", "bookmarks"]) {
      const others = byName.get(name)!.indexes.filter((i) => i.config.method !== "brin");
      expect(others.map((i) => [i.config.name, i.config.method]).sort(), name).toEqual([
        [`${name}_post_idx`, "btree"],
        [`${name}_user_created_idx`, "btree"],
      ]);
    }
  });
});

describe("staff console 3a", () => {
  const column = (table: string, name: string) => byName.get(table)!.columns.find((c) => c.name === name);
  /** Name, SQL type and not-null of every column, in order. */
  const shape = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.columns.map((c) => [c.name, c.getSQLType(), c.notNull]);
  /** Every foreign key of a table by its local columns: the table and columns it points at and what a delete there does. */
  const foreignKeys = (table: string) =>
    Object.fromEntries(
      byName.get(table)!.foreignKeys.map((k) => {
        const ref = k.reference();
        return [ref.columns.map((c) => c.name).join(","), { table: getTableConfig(ref.foreignTable).name, columns: ref.foreignColumns.map((c) => c.name), onDelete: k.onDelete }];
      }),
    );
  /** Every index as its name, its columns and whether it is unique, by name. */
  const indexes = (table: string) =>
    byName
      .get(table)!
      .indexes.map((i) => [i.config.name, i.config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name), i.config.unique])
      .sort((a, b) => String(a[0]).localeCompare(String(b[0])));
  const uniques = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.uniqueConstraints.map((u) => [u.getName(), u.columns.map((c) => c.name)]);
  const checks = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.checks.map((c) => c.name).sort();
  const policies = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.policies.map((p) => [p.name, p.for, p.to]);

  test("the seven staff events close the auth event type, after 1c's passkey events", () => {
    const values = schema.authEventType.enumValues;
    expect(values.slice(values.indexOf("passkey_counter_regression") + 1)).toEqual([
      "staff_enrollment_issued",
      "staff_key_added",
      "staff_key_revoked",
      "staff_key_counter_regression",
      "staff_sign_in",
      "staff_signed_out",
      "staff_session_revoked",
    ]);
  });

  test("the three staff tables live in the auth schema, with row level security and one policy for the auth role", () => {
    for (const name of ["staff_keys", "staff_enrollments", "staff_sessions"]) {
      const cfg = byName.get(name)!;
      expect(cfg.schema, name).toBe("auth");
      expect(cfg.enableRLS, name).toBe(true);
      expect(policies(name), name).toEqual([[`${name}_auth_all`, "all", authRole]]);
    }
  });

  test("a staff key records its credential, its origin and relying party ID, its dates and whether it was revoked or suspect", () => {
    expect(shape("staff_keys")).toEqual([
      ["id", "uuid", true],
      ["user_id", "uuid", true],
      ["credential_id", "text", true],
      ["public_key", "text", true],
      ["counter", "bigint", true],
      ["transports", "text[]", true],
      ["name", "text", true],
      ["aaguid", "uuid", false],
      ["origin", "text", true],
      ["rp_id", "text", true],
      ["created_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["last_used_at", "timestamp with time zone", false],
      ["revoked_at", "timestamp with time zone", false],
      ["suspect_at", "timestamp with time zone", false],
    ]);
    // No user handle of its own: staff registrations use the account's webauthn_user_id.
    expect(column("staff_keys", "user_handle")).toBeUndefined();
    // The development cleaner deletes accounts as the superuser; a key must stop that delete, never go with it.
    expect(foreignKeys("staff_keys")).toEqual({ user_id: { table: "users", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "restrict" } });
    expect(indexes("staff_keys")).toEqual([
      ["staff_keys_credential_idx", ["credential_id"], true],
      ["staff_keys_user_idx", ["user_id"], false],
    ]);
    // The pair the staff sessions' foreign key names.
    expect(uniques("staff_keys")).toEqual([["staff_keys_id_user_id_unique", ["id", "user_id"]]]);
    expect(checks("staff_keys")).toEqual(["staff_keys_suspect_is_revoked"]);
  });

  test("an enrolment keeps only its token's hash, the console it was issued for, its expiry and when it was used", () => {
    expect(shape("staff_enrollments")).toEqual([
      ["id", "uuid", true],
      ["user_id", "uuid", true],
      ["token_hash", "text", true],
      ["origin", "text", true],
      ["rp_id", "text", true],
      ["created_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["expires_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["used_at", "timestamp with time zone", false],
    ]);
    expect(foreignKeys("staff_enrollments")).toEqual({ user_id: { table: "users", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "cascade" } });
    expect(indexes("staff_enrollments")).toEqual([
      ["staff_enrollments_token_hash_idx", ["token_hash"], true],
      ["staff_enrollments_user_idx", ["user_id"], false],
    ]);
  });

  test("a staff session keeps its token's hash, a unique handle, its key and account together, both expiries and the browser label", () => {
    expect(shape("staff_sessions")).toEqual([
      ["id", "text", true],
      ["handle", "uuid", true],
      ["user_id", "uuid", true],
      ["key_id", "uuid", true],
      ["created_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["last_used_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["idle_expires_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["absolute_expires_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      ["revoked_at", "timestamp with time zone", false],
      ["browser", "text", true],
    ]);
    expect(column("staff_sessions", "id")?.primary).toBe(true);
    expect(column("staff_sessions", "handle")?.hasDefault).toBe(true);
    // The key's foreign key names the account as well, so a session's key always belongs to its account.
    expect(foreignKeys("staff_sessions")).toEqual({
      user_id: { table: "users", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "cascade" },
      "key_id,user_id": { table: "staff_keys", columns: ["id", "user_id"], onDelete: "cascade" },
    });
    expect(indexes("staff_sessions")).toEqual([
      ["staff_sessions_handle_idx", ["handle"], true],
      ["staff_sessions_user_idx", ["user_id"], false],
    ]);
    expect(checks("staff_sessions")).toEqual(["staff_sessions_lifetime"]);
  });

  test("audit_log gains the staff session's handle, the key, the action's hash and the step-up, all optional", () => {
    const added = [
      ["staff_session", "uuid"],
      ["key_id", "uuid"],
      ["action_hash", "text"],
      ["step_up", "jsonb"],
    ] as const;
    for (const [name, type] of added) {
      expect(column("audit_log", name)?.getSQLType(), name).toBe(type);
      expect(column("audit_log", name)?.notNull, name).toBe(false);
      expect(column("audit_log", name)?.hasDefault, name).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(checks("audit_log")).toEqual(["audit_log_step_up_complete"]);
  });

  test("audit_log's chain columns are not null, with placeholder defaults that the trigger always overwrites", () => {
    const chain = [
      ["chain_version", "smallint", 0],
      ["chain_seq", "bigint", 0],
      ["prev_hash", "text", ""],
      ["hash", "text", ""],
    ] as const;
    for (const [name, type, placeholder] of chain) {
      expect(column("audit_log", name)?.getSQLType(), name).toBe(type);
      expect(column("audit_log", name)?.notNull, name).toBe(true);
      expect(column("audit_log", name)?.default, name).toBe(placeholder);
    }
    // One index serves the viewer and audit-verify; there is none on (created_at, id).
    expect(indexes("audit_log")).toEqual([["audit_log_chain_seq_idx", ["chain_seq"], true]]);
  });

  test("audit_head holds one row, the newest place and hash, which the API role may only read", () => {
    const cfg = byName.get("audit_head")!;
    expect(cfg.schema).toBeUndefined(); // public
    expect(shape("audit_head")).toEqual([
      ["id", "smallint", true],
      ["seq", "bigint", true],
      ["hash", "text", true],
    ]);
    expect(column("audit_head", "id")?.primary).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.columns.filter((c) => c.hasDefault)).toEqual([]);
    expect(checks("audit_head")).toEqual(["audit_head_single_row"]);
    expect(cfg.enableRLS).toBe(true);
    expect(policies("audit_head")).toEqual([["audit_head_api_select", "select", apiRole]]);
  });
});

describe("moderation cases 3c", () => {
  const column = (table: string, name: string) => byName.get(table)!.columns.find((c) => c.name === name);
  /** Name, SQL type and not-null of every column, in order. */
  const shape = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.columns.map((c) => [c.name, c.getSQLType(), c.notNull]);
  const checks = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.checks.map((c) => c.name).sort();
  const policies = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.policies.map((p) => [p.name, p.for, p.to]);
  const index = (table: string, name: string) => byName.get(table)!.indexes.find((i) => i.config.name === name)?.config;
  const indexColumns = (config: { columns: unknown[] } | undefined) => config?.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name);
  /** An index's predicate as the SQL the migration holds. */
  const predicate = (config: { where?: SQL } | undefined) => (config?.where ? new PgDialect().sqlToQuery(config.where).sql : undefined);
  /** Every foreign key of a table by its local columns: the table and columns it points at and what a delete there does. */
  const foreignKeys = (table: string) =>
    Object.fromEntries(
      byName.get(table)!.foreignKeys.map((k) => {
        const ref = k.reference();
        return [ref.columns.map((c) => c.name).join(","), { table: getTableConfig(ref.foreignTable).name, columns: ref.foreignColumns.map((c) => c.name), onDelete: k.onDelete }];
      }),
    );
  /** The columns declared unique by themselves, each with the name of its constraint. */
  const uniques = (table: string) =>
    byName
      .get(table)!
      .columns.filter((c) => c.isUnique)
      .map((c) => [c.uniqueName, [c.name]])
      .sort();

  /** A check's expression as the migration holds it. */
  const checkSql = (table: string, name: string) => new PgDialect().sqlToQuery(byName.get(table)!.checks.find((c) => c.name === name)!.value).sql;

  const MODERATION_TABLES = ["cases", "intakes", "intake_items", "decisions", "decision_actions", "seal_posts", "appeals", "staff_texts", "evidence_snapshots", "case_access_log", "moderation_limits", "media_holds"];
  const AUTH_TABLES = ["notifier_contacts", "notifier_confirmations", "notifier_suppressions", "staff_personal_accounts"];

  test("the twelve moderation tables are public, with row level security and one policy for the API role", () => {
    for (const name of MODERATION_TABLES) {
      const cfg = byName.get(name);
      expect(cfg, name).toBeDefined();
      expect(cfg!.schema, name).toBeUndefined(); // public
      expect(cfg!.enableRLS, name).toBe(true);
      // The grants do the restricting (migration 0015); moderation_limits is read only, so its one policy is a SELECT one.
      expect(policies(name), name).toEqual(name === "moderation_limits" ? [["moderation_limits_api_select", "select", apiRole]] : [[`${name}_api_all`, "all", apiRole]]);
    }
  });

  test("no moderation table has a column named like an email or an address", () => {
    for (const name of MODERATION_TABLES) {
      for (const c of byName.get(name)!.columns) expect(c.name, `${name}.${c.name}`).not.toMatch(/email|address/i);
    }
  });

  test("xid8 is the xid8 SQL type and hands the transaction id over as a string", () => {
    const table = pgTable("xid8_probe", { value: xid8("value") });
    const probe = getTableConfig(table).columns[0]!;
    expect(probe.getSQLType()).toBe("xid8");
    // A 64-bit counter: a string keeps every digit, where a JavaScript number would not.
    expect(probe.mapFromDriverValue("18446744073709551615")).toBe("18446744073709551615");
    expect(probe.mapToDriverValue("773")).toBe("773");
  });

  test("one open case a target: the partial unique index, the queue's index and the target's index", () => {
    const open = index("cases", "cases_one_open_per_target");
    expect(open?.unique).toBe(true);
    expect(indexColumns(open)).toEqual(["target_type", "target_id"]);
    expect(predicate(open)).toBe("closed_at is null");
    const queue = index("cases", "cases_queue_idx");
    expect(queue?.unique).toBe(false);
    expect(indexColumns(queue)).toEqual(["lane", "oldest_open_at"]);
    expect(predicate(queue)).toBe("closed_at is null");
    expect(indexColumns(index("cases", "cases_target_idx"))).toEqual(["target_type", "target_id", "opened_at"]);
    expect(checks("cases")).toEqual(["cases_closed_answered", "cases_lane", "cases_seq_order"]);
    expect(column("cases", "id")?.hasDefault).toBe(true);
    // No foreign key on the target: it names two tables.

  test("no check lets a row through on a null: a statement always has its digest, a salt its form, and the two comparisons with a nullable value are null-safe", () => {
    // A CHECK passes when its expression is null, so `digest = encode(...)` alone would accept a statement with no digest.
    for (const [table, name] of [
      ["intake_items", "intake_items_statement"],
      ["appeals", "appeals_statement"],
    ] as const) {
      expect(checkSql(table, name), name).toContain(`"${table}"."statement_digest" is not null and "${table}"."statement_digest" = encode(sha256(`);
      expect(checkSql(table, name), name).toContain(`"${table}"."statement_salt" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'`);
    }
    expect(checkSql("staff_texts", "staff_texts_digest")).toContain(`"staff_texts"."salt" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' and "staff_texts"."digest" = encode(sha256(`);
    expect(checkSql("intake_items", "intake_items_case")).toBe(
      `("intake_items"."case_id" is null) = ("intake_items"."seq" is null) and ("intake_items"."case_id" is not null or "intake_items"."outcome" is not distinct from 'not_available')`,
    );
    expect(checkSql("decisions", "decisions_keyword")).toBe(`"decisions"."category_keyword" is null or "decisions"."ground" is not distinct from 'illegal'`);
  });

  test("the columns of decisions that the database forces: their types, and which carry a default", () => {
    // [name, SQL type, not null, default]; undefined where the column has none and the trigger of 0016 alone fills it.

  test("the ledger: a measure once a decision, lifted at most once, and the columns the database forces", () => {
    expect(shape("decision_actions")).toEqual([
      ["id", "uuid", true],
      ["decision_id", "uuid", true],
      ["kind", "action_kind", true],
      ["media_id", "uuid", false],
      ["subject_account_id", "uuid", true],
      ["post_id", "uuid", false],
      ["reverses_action_id", "uuid", false],
      ["no_effect", "text", false],
      ["created_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],
      // 3e (design, section 6.1): three the key signs, four the trigger forces.
      ["days", "smallint", false],
      ["announced", "boolean", false],
      ["basis", "text", false],
      ["rests_on", "uuid[]", false],
      ["starts_at", "timestamp with time zone", false],
      ["ends_at", "timestamp with time zone", false],
      ["replaced", "boolean", false],
      // 3f (design, section 6.2): one the trigger forces from the order, one the key signs on a reinstatement.
      ["withhold_author", "boolean", false],
      ["order_ground", "text", false],
    ]);
    // None of the forced columns has a default: the triggers of 0016 and 0021 alone fill them.
    for (const name of ["subject_account_id", "post_id", "reverses_action_id", "no_effect", "created_at", "days", "announced", "basis", "rests_on", "starts_at", "ends_at", "replaced", "withhold_author", "order_ground"]) {
      expect(column("decision_actions", name)?.hasDefault, name).toBe(false);
    }
    const once = byName.get("decision_actions")!.uniqueConstraints.map((u) => [u.getName(), u.columns.map((c) => c.name), u.nullsNotDistinct]);
    expect(once).toEqual([["decision_actions_once", ["decision_id", "kind", "media_id"], true]]);
    const reversed = index("decision_actions", "decision_actions_reversed_once");
    expect(reversed?.unique).toBe(true);
    expect(indexColumns(reversed)).toEqual(["reverses_action_id"]);
    expect(predicate(reversed)).toBe("reverses_action_id is not null");
    expect(checks("decision_actions")).toEqual(["decision_actions_announced", "decision_actions_basis", "decision_actions_days", "decision_actions_no_effect", "decision_actions_order_ground"]);
    expect(checkSql("decision_actions", "decision_actions_order_ground")).toBe(`"decision_actions"."order_ground" in ('withdrawn', 'annulled', 'scrutiny', 'not_authentic', 'wrong_item')`);
    // Each check names columns only: no value of action_kind, which a check may not name in the migration that adds it.
    expect(checkSql("decision_actions", "decision_actions_days")).toBe(`"decision_actions"."days" between 1 and 30`);
    expect(checkSql("decision_actions", "decision_actions_basis")).toBe(
      `"decision_actions"."basis" in ('strikes', 'threat', 'terrorist', 'flood', 'protective', 'threat_repeat', 'ladder_end', 'reports')`,
    );
    expect(checkSql("decision_actions", "decision_actions_announced")).toBe(`"decision_actions"."announced" is null or "decision_actions"."basis" is not null`);
    expect(foreignKeys("decision_actions")).toEqual({
      decision_id: { table: "decisions", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "restrict" },
      reverses_action_id: { table: "decision_actions", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "no action" },
    });
    // 3c's seven measures and five reversals, then 3e's six measures and four reversals, in the order the migration adds them.
    expect(schema.actionKind.enumValues).toEqual([
      "withhold",
      "remove",
      "seal_media",
      "withhold_media",
      "remove_media",
      "reset_display_name",
      "reset_bio",
      "restore",
      "unseal_media",
      "restore_media",
      "restore_display_name",
      "restore_bio",
      "strike",
      "suspend",
      "terminate",
      "retire_handle",
      "warn_reporting",
      "restrict_reporting",
      "overrule",
      "lift_suspension",
      "unretire_handle",
      "lift_reporting",
      // 3f: the measure of an order decision and its reversal.
      "disable_by_order",
      "reinstate_by_order",
    ]);
  });

      ["forget_after", "timestamp with time zone", true],
    ]);
    // The moderation module chooses the id: the public intake row names it before the contact is stored.
    expect(column("notifier_contacts", "id")?.primary).toBe(true);
    expect(column("notifier_contacts", "id")?.hasDefault).toBe(false);
    expect(shape("notifier_confirmations")).toEqual([

  test("a staff link pairs a staff account with a personal account that is not the same one, and stops either from being deleted", () => {
    expect(shape("staff_personal_accounts")).toEqual([

      ["personal_user_id", "uuid", true],
      ["linked_at", "timestamp with time zone", true],

    expect(foreignKeys("staff_personal_accounts")).toEqual({
      staff_user_id: { table: "users", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "restrict" },
      personal_user_id: { table: "users", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "restrict" },
    });

});

  const policies = (table: string) => byName.get(table)!.policies.map((p) => [p.name, p.for, p.to]);

  const indexes = (table: string) =>

      .get(table)!
      .indexes.map((i) => [i.config.name, i.config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name), i.config.where ? new PgDialect().sqlToQuery(i.config.where).sql : null])
      .sort((a, b) => String(a[0]).localeCompare(String(b[0])));

    expect(checkSql("alert_outbox", "alert_outbox_kind")).toContain("'contact_mail', 'contact_mail_escalated', 'order_due'");

    expect(checkSql("alert_outbox", "alert_outbox_scope")).toBe(`"alert_outbox"."scope" in ('on_call', 'all')`);
```

### Create `apps/api/src/transparency/head.ts`

```ts
import { createHash } from "node:crypto";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import { HEAD_RULES, type HeadKind, type HeadWitness, type PublicHead } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { KeeperMailResult, KeeperMessage } from "../auth";
import type { TransparencyRepo } from "./repo";
import type { WitnessAdapter } from "./witness";

/**
 * The audit head's daily value (3d design, sections 2 row 9, 6.5, 7.7 and 10.6; Task 5). Once a day after the dispatch
 * hour the transparency job inserts the day's row of head_publications, whose insert trigger forces the day, the place
 * and the value from audit_head, so the API's role cannot publish a value of its own making; asks the witness for a token
 * while one is on; sets published_at from null; and mails the keeper, once, from the round whose update published it,
 * the day, the value, the place and the hash, from which the keeper computes the value again. A later round of the same
 * day asks the witness again while the token is null. The day's first round alerts head_missed when the day before has
 * no published value. The publication writes no audit row: it would move the head it publishes (section 15, 3a).
 */

/** The line feed between the digest's four parts. */
const LF = String.fromCharCode(10);

/**
 * head_value() of the database, in the API's own code: the hex SHA-256 of the tag, the day (yyyy-mm-dd, UTC), the place
 * in decimal and the hash, each after a line feed. What the keeper computes from the mail; a test holds the two equal.
 */
export function headValue(day: string, seq: number, hash: string): string {
  return createHash("sha256").update([HEAD_RULES.tag, day, String(seq), hash].join(LF), "utf8").digest("hex");
}

/** The day's head row as the job reads it after its insert. */
export interface HeadToday {
  /** Whether this round's insert wrote it. */
  inserted: boolean;
  day: string;
  value: string;
  witness: HeadWitness;
  witnessed: boolean;
  published: boolean;
}

/** One published row as the public route reads it: never its place. */
export interface HeadDayRow {
  day: string;
  kind: HeadKind;
  value: string;
  witness: HeadWitness;
  token: Uint8Array | null;
  retiredOn: string | null;
  lastDay: string | null;
}

/** The statements of the head's day, which repo.ts writes. */
export type HeadRepo = Pick<TransparencyRepo, "headInsert" | "headWitnessed" | "headPublish" | "headPlace" | "headMissed" | "headAlert">;

/** What one round's pass did with the day's value. */
export interface HeadPass {
  /** The database's UTC day, whose row the pass read. */
  day: string;
  inserted: boolean;
  /** stored: a token came this round; unanswered: the witness was asked and gave none; null: nobody was asked. */
  witnessed: "stored" | "unanswered" | null;
  /** Whether this round's update published the value. */
  published: boolean;
  /** The keeper's mail, from the round that published: as mailKeeper answered, or unverified when no hash gave the value. */
  mailed: KeeperMailResult | "unverified" | null;
  /** The alerts this round wrote (each under F's daily rule, so a second in 24 hours is not written). */
  alerts: ("head_unwitnessed" | "head_missed")[];
  /** Nothing more to do today: published, and witnessed or never to be. */
  done: boolean;
}

export interface HeadDeps {
  repo: HeadRepo;
  witness: WitnessAdapter;
  /** The auth module's mail to HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL, which answers "off" while the setting is empty. */
  mailKeeper: (message: KeeperMessage) => Promise<KeeperMailResult>;
  log: Logger;
}

/** One round's pass over the day's value (7.7 steps 2 to 6). */
export async function publishHead(deps: HeadDeps, options: { firstOfDay: boolean }): Promise<HeadPass> {
  const { repo, witness, log } = deps;
  const alerts: HeadPass["alerts"] = [];
  // 2. The row: the trigger forces everything but the witness's name; a day holds one head row.
  const today = await repo.headInsert(witness.name);
  // 6. A missed day: the day before has no published value, while an earlier day has one (the head's first day misses
  // nothing). A missed day is never written afterwards: the page shows the hole.
  if (options.firstOfDay) {
    const missed = await repo.headMissed();
    if (missed !== null && (await repo.headAlert("head_missed", missed))) alerts.push("head_missed");
  }
  // 3. The witness, while one is on and the row was born under it: a row named none was asked of nobody, and the CHECK
  // keeps a token off it. Asked again in each round while the token is null; a later token proves the value from then on.
  let witnessed: HeadPass["witnessed"] = null;
  let hasToken = today.witnessed;
  if (witness.mode !== "off" && today.witness === witness.name && !today.witnessed) {
    const token = await witness.witness(today.value);
    if (token !== null) {
      // Set from null alone: the update finds nothing when the row has its token already.
      await repo.headWitnessed(today.day, token);
      witnessed = "stored";
      hasToken = true;
    } else {
      witnessed = "unanswered";
      if (await repo.headAlert("head_unwitnessed", today.day)) alerts.push("head_unwitnessed");
      log.warn({ job: "transparency", day: today.day }, "transparency: the head's witness gave no token; the value is published without one");
    }
  }
  // 4. Published, from null, once.
  let published = false;
  let mailed: HeadPass["mailed"] = null;
  if (!today.published) {
    const set = await repo.headPublish(today.day);
    if (set !== null) {
      published = true;
      // 5. The keeper's mail, from this round alone. The place's hash is read again and must give the stored value, so the
      // keeper is never sent a place and a hash that do not check.
      const place = await repo.headPlace(today.day);
      if (place === null) {
        mailed = "unverified";
        log.error({ job: "transparency", day: today.day }, "transparency: no hash of the audit log gives the head's stored value; the keeper is not mailed");
      } else {
        mailed = await deps.mailKeeper({ template: "head_published", day: today.day, value: today.value, seq: place.seq, hash: place.hash, witnessed: set.witnessed });
      }
      log.info({ job: "transparency", day: today.day, mailed }, "transparency: the head's daily value was published");
    }
  }
  const unwitnessable = witness.mode === "off" || today.witness !== witness.name;
  return { day: today.day, inserted: today.inserted, witnessed, published, mailed, alerts, done: (today.published || published) && (unwitnessable || hasToken) };
}

/** A token as the public answer carries it. */
const base64 = (token: Uint8Array) => Buffer.from(token).toString("base64");

/**
 * GET /api/public/head's answer (10.6): the rows as the route read them, newest first, a row without a token read as
 * witnessed by nobody whatever was asked, the token as base64. It holds no place and no hash.
 */
export function publicHead(rows: readonly HeadDayRow[]): PublicHead {
  return {
    days: rows.map((row) => ({
      day: row.day,
      kind: row.kind,
      value: row.value,
      witness: row.token === null ? "none" : row.witness,
      token: row.token === null ? null : base64(row.token),
      retiredOn: row.retiredOn,
      lastDay: row.lastDay,
    })),
  };
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/transparency/witness.ts`

```ts
import { HEAD_RULES, type HeadWitness } from "@korbat/contracts";

/**
 * The head's witness adapter (3d design, sections 2 row 9, 5 "The adapters" and 7.7; Task 5), chosen by HEAD_WITNESS when
 * the process starts. It is given one value, the day's 64 hexadecimal characters, and nothing else, and it imports
 * nothing of the transparency module: the job (head.ts) hands it the value and stores what it answers. An architecture
 * test holds it to that.
 *
 *   - `off` (the default): asks nobody; the value stands on korbat's page and in the keeper's mail only.
 *   - `test`: answers TEST_TOKEN, a fixed token that proves nothing, for any value; it is built only while the app's site
 *     is closed, in the process as at start.
 *   - `rfc3161`: one POST of the fixed RFC 3161 request below to HEAD_WITNESS_URL, bounded at HEAD_RULES.witnessTimeoutMs.
 *     The answer, a TimeStampResp, is read no further than its status: granted (0) or granted with modifications (1),
 *     with a token after it, is kept whole and as received, at most HEAD_RULES.tokenMaxBytes; anything else, a timeout or
 *     no connection answers null, and nothing is thrown. The whole answer is what `openssl ts -verify -in <day>.tsr`
 *     reads, which the page's [tr.verify] says how to run.
 */

export type WitnessMode = "off" | "test" | "rfc3161";

export interface WitnessAdapter {
  readonly mode: WitnessMode;
  /** What head_publications.witness records of a row the job writes while this adapter is built: none while it is off. */
  readonly name: HeadWitness;
  /** The authority's token for the value, or null when it gave none. */
  witness(value: string): Promise<Uint8Array | null>;
}

/** The settings the adapter is built from: the configuration's own members of the same names. */
export interface WitnessSettings {
  HEAD_WITNESS: WitnessMode;
  APP_SITE: "open" | "closed";
  HEAD_WITNESS_URL?: string | undefined;
}

/** What a test may give in place of the authority: its address (fakeWitness(), which is no https one), a fetch, a shorter wait. */
export interface WitnessOptions {
  url?: string;
  fetch?: typeof fetch;
  timeoutMs?: number;
}

/**
 * The fixed TimeStampReq (RFC 3161, section 2.4.1), 59 bytes in DER around the value's own 32 bytes:
 *
 *   30 39                        TimeStampReq, a SEQUENCE of 57 bytes
 *     02 01 01                   version 1
 *     30 31                      messageImprint, a SEQUENCE of 49 bytes
 *       30 0d                    hashAlgorithm
 *         06 09 60 86 48 01 65 03 04 02 01    the OID of SHA-256, 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.2.1
 *         05 00                  its NULL parameters
 *       04 20 <32 bytes>         hashedMessage: the value read as the 32 bytes its hex spells
 *     01 01 ff                   certReq TRUE: the token carries the authority's certificate
 *
 * The imprint is the value itself, not a digest of its text, so `openssl ts -verify -digest <value>` compares the proof
 * with the value the page shows. No nonce and no policy: the request is the same for everyone but for its 32 bytes.
 */
const REQUEST_HEAD = Uint8Array.of(0x30, 0x39, 0x02, 0x01, 0x01, 0x30, 0x31, 0x30, 0x0d, 0x06, 0x09, 0x60, 0x86, 0x48, 0x01, 0x65, 0x03, 0x04, 0x02, 0x01, 0x05, 0x00, 0x04, 0x20);
const REQUEST_TAIL = Uint8Array.of(0x01, 0x01, 0xff);

/** A head's value: the hex SHA-256 that head_value() computes. */
const VALUE = /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/;

/** The request for one value, as `timestampRequest` writes it into the template. */
export function timestampRequest(value: string): Uint8Array {
  if (!VALUE.test(value)) throw new Error("head witness: a value is 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters");
  const request = new Uint8Array(REQUEST_HEAD.length + 32 + REQUEST_TAIL.length);
  request.set(REQUEST_HEAD, 0);
  request.set(Buffer.from(value, "hex"), REQUEST_HEAD.length);
  request.set(REQUEST_TAIL, REQUEST_HEAD.length + 32);
  return request;
}

/**
 * The `test` adapter's token: a TimeStampResp of status granted whose token is the OCTET STRING "test" in place of a
 * signed structure. It proves nothing and says so to whoever parses it; it is stored and offered like a real one.
 */
export const TEST_TOKEN = Uint8Array.of(0x30, 0x0b, 0x30, 0x03, 0x02, 0x01, 0x00, 0x04, 0x04, 0x74, 0x65, 0x73, 0x74);

/** A DER element's tag at `at`: where its content starts and ends, or null when it is not that tag or overruns `end`. */
function element(bytes: Uint8Array, at: number, end: number, tag: number): { start: number; end: number } | null {
  if (at + 2 > end || bytes[at] !== tag) return null;
  const first = bytes[at + 1]!;
  let length: number;
  let start: number;
  if (first < 0x80) {
    length = first;
    start = at + 2;
  } else if (first === 0x81 && at + 3 <= end) {
    length = bytes[at + 2]!;
    start = at + 3;
  } else if (first === 0x82 && at + 4 <= end) {
    length = (bytes[at + 2]! << 8) | bytes[at + 3]!;
    start = at + 4;
  } else {
    // A longer form would hold more than tokenMaxBytes; an indefinite one is no DER.
    return null;
  }
  return start + length <= end ? { start, end: start + length } : null;
}

/**
 * Whether a TimeStampResp grants a token: the SEQUENCE spans the whole answer, its PKIStatusInfo opens with the status
 * 0 or 1, and something follows the status info, which is the token. Nothing else of the answer is read.
 */
export function grantsToken(bytes: Uint8Array): boolean {
  const response = element(bytes, 0, bytes.length, 0x30);
  if (response === null || response.end !== bytes.length) return false;
  const info = element(bytes, response.start, response.end, 0x30);
  if (info === null) return false;
  const status = element(bytes, info.start, info.end, 0x02);
  if (status === null || status.end - status.start !== 1) return false;
  const granted = bytes[status.start] === 0 || bytes[status.start] === 1;
  return granted && info.end < response.end;
}

/** The body of an answer, read until it would pass `max` bytes; null when it does. */
async function readAtMost(res: Response, max: number): Promise<Uint8Array | null> {
  const declared = Number(res.headers.get("content-length") ?? "0");
  if (declared > max) {
    await res.body?.cancel();
    return null;
  }
  if (res.body === null) return new Uint8Array(0);
  const reader = res.body.getReader();
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  let size = 0;
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    size += value.length;
    if (size > max) {
      await reader.cancel();
      return null;
    }
    chunks.push(value);
  }
  return Uint8Array.from(Buffer.concat(chunks));
}

export function witnessFrom(settings: WitnessSettings, options: WitnessOptions = {}): WitnessAdapter {
  switch (settings.HEAD_WITNESS) {
    case "off":
      return {
        mode: "off",
        name: "none",
        witness: async () => {
          throw new Error("head witness: the adapter is off, and nothing is asked");
        },
      };
    case "test":
      // The same rule as the configuration's, so a test adapter built in the process answers only on a closed site too.
      if (settings.APP_SITE !== "closed") throw new Error("head witness: HEAD_WITNESS=test is refused while APP_SITE is open");
      return {
        mode: "test",
        name: "test",
        async witness(value) {
          timestampRequest(value);
          return Uint8Array.from(TEST_TOKEN);
        },
      };
    case "rfc3161": {
      if (!settings.HEAD_WITNESS_URL) throw new Error("head witness: HEAD_WITNESS_URL is required when HEAD_WITNESS is rfc3161");
      const url = options.url ?? settings.HEAD_WITNESS_URL;
      const send = options.fetch ?? fetch;
      const timeoutMs = options.timeoutMs ?? HEAD_RULES.witnessTimeoutMs;
      return {
        mode: "rfc3161",
        name: "rfc3161",
        async witness(value) {
          const body = timestampRequest(value);
          try {
            // One signal bounds the whole exchange, the body's reading included.
            const signal = AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs);
            const res = await send(url, {
              method: "POST",
              headers: { "content-type": "application/timestamp-query", accept: "application/timestamp-reply" },
              body,
              signal,
              redirect: "error",
            });
            if (!res.ok) {
              await res.body?.cancel();
              return null;
            }
            const answer = await readAtMost(res, HEAD_RULES.tokenMaxBytes);
            return answer !== null && grantsToken(answer) ? answer : null;
          } catch {
            // A refused connection, a timeout, a redirect or a broken body: no token. The error is dropped whole.
            return null;
          }
        },
      };
    }
  }
}
```

```sql
CREATE TABLE "head_publications" (
	"day" date NOT NULL,
	"kind" text NOT NULL,
	"chain_seq" bigint,
	"value" text NOT NULL,
	"witness" text NOT NULL,
	"token" "bytea",
	"witnessed_at" timestamp with time zone,
	"published_at" timestamp with time zone,
	"retired_at" timestamp with time zone,
	"last_day" date,
	CONSTRAINT "head_publications_day_kind_pk" PRIMARY KEY("day","kind"),
	CONSTRAINT "head_publications_kind" CHECK ("head_publications"."kind" in ('head', 'restore')),
	CONSTRAINT "head_publications_witness" CHECK ("head_publications"."witness" in ('none', 'rfc3161', 'test')),
	CONSTRAINT "head_publications_value" CHECK ("head_publications"."value" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'),
	CONSTRAINT "head_publications_token" CHECK (("head_publications"."token" is null) = ("head_publications"."witnessed_at" is null) and ("head_publications"."token" is null or ("head_publications"."witness" <> 'none' and octet_length("head_publications"."token") between 1 and 16384))),
	CONSTRAINT "head_publications_place" CHECK (("head_publications"."chain_seq" is not null and "head_publications"."chain_seq" >= 0) or ("head_publications"."chain_seq" is null and "head_publications"."kind" = 'head' and "head_publications"."retired_at" is not null)),
	CONSTRAINT "head_publications_last_day" CHECK ("head_publications"."last_day" is null or "head_publications"."kind" = 'restore')
);

ALTER TABLE "head_publications" ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;--> statement-breakpoint
ALTER TABLE "alert_outbox" DROP CONSTRAINT "alert_outbox_kind";--> statement-breakpoint
ALTER TABLE "alert_outbox" ADD CONSTRAINT "alert_outbox_kind" CHECK ("alert_outbox"."kind" in ('contact_mail', 'contact_mail_escalated', 'order_due', 'order_opened', 'order_corrected', 'order_effected', 'order_reinstated', 'order_unverified', 'hold_ending', 'report_owed', 'handover_undestroyed', 'copy_overdue', 'copy_taken', 'alert_channel_down', 'mailbox_unreachable', 'alert_test', 'moderation_urgent', 'moderation_waiting', 'moderation_burst', 'moderation_reads', 'moderation_reveal', 'moderation_csam_lifted', 'quarantine_due', 'quarantine_lost', 'release_undestroyed', 'seal_released', 'edge_purge_failed', 'head_unwitnessed', 'head_missed'));--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE POLICY "head_publications_api_all" ON "head_publications" AS PERMISSIVE FOR ALL TO "korbat_api" USING (true) WITH CHECK (true);--> statement-breakpoint
-- Everything below is written by hand (3d design, sections 6 and 6.5; Task 5). As in 0016 to 0036: every function is
-- owned by the migrator, pins its search path to public and pg_temp, names every object schema-qualified and has EXECUTE
-- taken from PUBLIC; a guard's refusal is moderation_column under SQLSTATE 42501, as 3c's guards answer.
--
-- 1. The grants. 0001's default privileges gave the API role every right on a new public table; head_publications loses
-- them all, then gets what section 6.5 lists: it reads the rows, inserts the day's row (whose every column but the
-- witness's name the trigger below forces), and sets the token with its time and the time of publication, each once. No
-- DELETE: a published value is public record, and the retention job erases none (7.14).
REVOKE ALL ON "public"."head_publications" FROM korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON "public"."head_publications" TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT UPDATE ("token", "witnessed_at", "published_at") ON "public"."head_publications" TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 2. head_value(day, seq, hash): the hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 text "korbat.head.v2", a line feed, the day as YYYY-MM-DD,
-- a line feed, the place in decimal, a line feed and the hash (section 2, row 9). It shows neither the place nor a row's
-- hash, so nobody counts staff actions or tests a guessed row from it; and the day is in it, so the value differs every
-- day, also over days on which no audit row was written. The keeper, who holds the day, the place and the hash, computes
-- it again. to_char with an explicit pattern prints the day whatever DateStyle says; chr(10) is the line feed.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."head_value"(day date, seq bigint, hash text) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT encode(sha256(convert_to('korbat.head.v2' || chr(10) || to_char($1, 'YYYY-MM-DD') || chr(10) || $2::text || chr(10) || $3, 'UTF8')), 'hex')
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."head_value"(date, bigint, text) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."head_value"(date, bigint, text) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 3. head_publications_insert, plain, BEFORE INSERT, for every role but the migrator: the row is a head of today in UTC,
-- its place and value come from audit_head as it stands in this statement, and nothing else is set but the witness's
-- name. So the API's role cannot publish a value of its own making, nor one of another day. The daily publication writes
-- no audit row: it would move the head it publishes (section 15, 3a). The migrator keeps what it supplied: a restore's
-- rows and a test's past days.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."head_publications_insert"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  v_seq bigint;
  v_hash text;
BEGIN
  IF current_user = 'korbat_migrate' THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  SELECT a.seq, a.hash INTO v_seq, v_hash FROM public.audit_head a WHERE a.id = 1;
  NEW.kind := 'head';
  NEW.day := (now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date;
  NEW.chain_seq := v_seq;
  NEW.value := public.head_value(NEW.day, v_seq, v_hash);
  NEW.token := NULL;
  NEW.witnessed_at := NULL;
  NEW.published_at := NULL;
  NEW.retired_at := NULL;
  NEW.last_day := NULL;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."head_publications_insert"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER "head_publications_insert" BEFORE INSERT ON "public"."head_publications" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."head_publications_insert"();--> statement-breakpoint

-- 4. head_publications_guard, plain, BEFORE UPDATE, for every role but the migrator: the token, its time and the time of
-- publication each change only from null, and nothing else changes; a time set from null is the clock's, whatever the
-- update supplied, so no token and no publication is dated before it happened. The column grants already keep the API's
-- role off every other column; the guard says the same for every role but the migrator, whose updates are a restore's.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."head_publications_guard"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  IF current_user = 'korbat_migrate' THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF NEW.day IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.day OR NEW.kind IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.kind OR NEW.chain_seq IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.chain_seq
     OR NEW.value IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.value OR NEW.witness IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.witness OR NEW.retired_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.retired_at
     OR NEW.last_day IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.last_day
     OR (OLD.token IS NOT NULL AND NEW.token IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.token)
     OR (OLD.witnessed_at IS NOT NULL AND NEW.witnessed_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.witnessed_at)
     OR (OLD.published_at IS NOT NULL AND NEW.published_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.published_at) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'moderation_column' USING ERRCODE = '42501';
  END IF;
  IF OLD.witnessed_at IS NULL AND NEW.witnessed_at IS NOT NULL THEN
    NEW.witnessed_at := now();
  END IF;
  IF OLD.published_at IS NULL AND NEW.published_at IS NOT NULL THEN
    NEW.published_at := now();
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."head_publications_guard"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER "head_publications_guard" BEFORE UPDATE ON "public"."head_publications" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."head_publications_guard"();
```

```json
          "name": "decisions_rule_id",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"rule_id\" in ('R1', 'R2', 'R3', 'R4', 'R5', 'R6')"
        },
        "decisions_category": {
          "name": "decisions_category",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category\" in ('STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE')"
        },
        "decisions_category_keyword": {
          "name": "decisions_category_keyword",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" in ('KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT')"
        },
        "decisions_automated_decision": {
          "name": "decisions_automated_decision",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"automated_decision\" in ('fully', 'partially', 'not_automated')"
        },
        "decisions_territorial_scope": {
          "name": "decisions_territorial_scope",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"territorial_scope\" = 'worldwide'"
        },
        "decisions_review_target": {
          "name": "decisions_review_target",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"kind\" in ('review', 'correction')) = (\"decisions\".\"reviews_decision_id\" is not null) and (\"decisions\".\"kind\" = 'review') = (\"decisions\".\"appeal_id\" is not null)"
        },
        "decisions_interim": {
          "name": "decisions_interim",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"kind\" <> 'interim' or \"decisions\".\"through_seq\" = 0"
        },
        "decisions_ground_rule": {
          "name": "decisions_ground_rule",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'incompatible' or \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is not null"
        },
        "decisions_ground_law": {
          "name": "decisions_ground_law",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'illegal' or \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is not null or \"decisions\".\"kind\"::text = 'order'"
        },
        "decisions_restricted": {
          "name": "decisions_restricted",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"outcome\" <> 'restricted' or (\"decisions\".\"ground\" is not null and \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is not null and \"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" is not null) or \"decisions\".\"kind\"::text = 'order'"
        },
        "decisions_informed": {
          "name": "decisions_informed",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"informed_at\" is not null or \"decisions\".\"author_mail\"::text = 'none'"
        },
        "decisions_digests": {
          "name": "decisions_digests",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$') and (\"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$') and (\"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$')"
        },
        "decisions_keyword": {
          "name": "decisions_keyword",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" is null or \"decisions\".\"ground\" is not distinct from 'illegal'"
        },
        "decisions_law_no_rule": {
          "name": "decisions_law_no_rule",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'illegal' or \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is null"
        },
        "decisions_reversal_plain": {
          "name": "decisions_reversal_plain",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"kind\" not in ('review', 'correction') or (\"decisions\".\"ground\" is null and \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is null and \"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" is null and \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is null and \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is null)"
        }
      },
      "isRLSEnabled": true
    },

        }

      "checkConstraints": {
        "intakes_ref": {
          "name": "intakes_ref",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"ref\" ~ '^N-[A-Z2-7]{10}$'"
        },
        "intakes_rule_id": {
          "name": "intakes_rule_id",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" in ('R1', 'R2', 'R3', 'R4', 'R5', 'R6')"
        },
        "intakes_category": {
          "name": "intakes_category",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"category\" in ('STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE')"
        },
        "intakes_category_keyword": {
          "name": "intakes_category_keyword",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"category_keyword\" in ('KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL', 'KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL_DEEPFAKE', 'KEYWORD_GROOMING_SEXUAL_ENTICEMENT_MINORS')"
        },
        "intakes_cited_law_len": {
          "name": "intakes_cited_law_len",
          "value": "char_length(\"intakes\".\"cited_law\") <= 300"
        },
        "intakes_explanation_len": {
          "name": "intakes_explanation_len",
          "value": "char_length(\"intakes\".\"explanation\") <= 2000"
        },
        "intakes_has_ground": {
          "name": "intakes_has_ground",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" is not null or \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"csam\""
        },
        "intakes_illegal_elements": {
          "name": "intakes_illegal_elements",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"kind\" <> 'user' or not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"csam\" or (\"intakes\".\"bona_fide\" and (\"intakes\".\"explanation\" is not null or \"intakes\".\"erased_at\" is not null))"
        },
        "intakes_finding_legal": {
          "name": "intakes_finding_legal",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"kind\" <> 'finding' or not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\""
        },
        "intakes_illegal_not_tc": {
          "name": "intakes_illegal_not_tc",
          "value": "not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"category\" <> 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC'"
        },
        "intakes_csam": {
          "name": "intakes_csam",
          "value": "not \"intakes\".\"csam\" or (\"intakes\".\"category\" = 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS' and \"intakes\".\"reporter_id\" is null and \"intakes\".\"contact_id\" is null)"
        },
        "intakes_contact_signed_out": {
          "name": "intakes_contact_signed_out",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"contact_id\" is null or \"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_out'"
        },
        "intakes_reporter_signed_in": {
          "name": "intakes_reporter_signed_in",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"reporter_id\" is null or \"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_in'"
        },
        "intakes_finding": {
          "name": "intakes_finding",
          "value": "(\"intakes\".\"kind\" = 'finding') = (\"intakes\".\"finding_by\" is not null) and (\"intakes\".\"kind\" = 'finding') = (\"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'staff')"
        },
        "intakes_lookup": {
          "name": "intakes_lookup",
          "value": "(\"intakes\".\"lookup_hash\" is not null) = (\"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_out' or \"intakes\".\"csam\")"
        },
        "intakes_erased": {
          "name": "intakes_erased",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"erased_at\" is null or (\"intakes\".\"explanation\" is null and \"intakes\".\"cited_law\" is null)"
        },
        "intakes_r2_finding_only": {
          "name": "intakes_r2_finding_only",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" is distinct from 'R2' or \"intakes\".\"kind\" = 'finding'"
        }
      },
      "isRLSEnabled": true
    },

          ]
        }

      "policies": {
        "legal_orders_api_all": {
          "name": "legal_orders_api_all",
          "as": "PERMISSIVE",
          "for": "ALL",
          "to": [
            "korbat_api"
          ],
          "using": "true",
          "withCheck": "true"
        }
      },
      "checkConstraints": {
        "legal_orders_kind": {
          "name": "legal_orders_kind",
          "value": "\"legal_orders\".\"kind\" in ('tco_removal', 'dsa_art9', 'dsa_art10')"
        },
        "legal_orders_member_state": {
          "name": "legal_orders_member_state",
          "value": "\"legal_orders\".\"member_state\" ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'"
        },
        "legal_orders_names": {
          "name": "legal_orders_names",
          "value": "char_length(\"legal_orders\".\"authority\") between 1 and 200 and char_length(\"legal_orders\".\"reference\") between 1 and 200"
        },
        "legal_orders_channel": {
          "name": "legal_orders_channel",
          "value": "\"legal_orders\".\"channel\" in ('mailbox', 'portal', 'post', 'other')"
        },
        "legal_orders_opened_via": {
          "name": "legal_orders_opened_via",
          "value": "\"legal_orders\".\"opened_via\" in ('console', 'cli')"
        },
        "legal_orders_received": {
          "name": "legal_orders_received",
          "value": "\"legal_orders\".\"received_at\" <= \"legal_orders\".\"opened_at\" and \"legal_orders\".\"sent_at\" <= \"legal_orders\".\"opened_at\""
        },
        "legal_orders_issued": {
          "name": "legal_orders_issued",
          "value": "\"legal_orders\".\"issued_at\" <= coalesce(\"legal_orders\".\"received_at\", \"legal_orders\".\"opened_at\")"
        },
        "legal_orders_tco": {
          "name": "legal_orders_tco",
          "value": "((\"legal_orders\".\"kind\" <> 'tco_removal' and not \"legal_orders\".\"section_c\") or \"legal_orders\".\"withhold_from_author\") and (\"legal_orders\".\"kind\" <> 'tco_removal' or \"legal_orders\".\"preserve\")"
        },
        "legal_orders_tell": {
          "name": "legal_orders_tell",
          "value": "(\"legal_orders\".\"tell_person\" is null or (\"legal_orders\".\"tell_person\" in ('at_effect', 'at_instant', 'never') and \"legal_orders\".\"kind\" = 'dsa_art10')) and (\"legal_orders\".\"tell_person_at\" is not null) = (\"legal_orders\".\"tell_person\" is not distinct from 'at_instant')"
        },
        "legal_orders_hold_end": {
          "name": "legal_orders_hold_end",
          "value": "(\"legal_orders\".\"hold_ended_at\" is null) = (\"legal_orders\".\"hold_end_reason\" is null) and \"legal_orders\".\"hold_end_reason\" in ('not_authentic', 'annulled', 'released_by_authority', 'not_ordered')"
        },
        "legal_orders_texts_len": {
          "name": "legal_orders_texts_len",
          "value": "char_length(\"legal_orders\".\"verified_how\") <= 500 and char_length(\"legal_orders\".\"hold_basis\") <= 500 and char_length(\"legal_orders\".\"scope\") <= 500 and char_length(\"legal_orders\".\"reasons\") <= 4000 and char_length(\"legal_orders\".\"redress\") <= 4000"
        },
        "legal_orders_document": {
          "name": "legal_orders_document",
          "value": "\"legal_orders\".\"document_sha256\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' and \"legal_orders\".\"document_bytes\" >= 0"
        }
      },
      "isRLSEnabled": true
    },
```

### Replace `README.md` (whole file)

````markdown
# korbat

Pseudonymous social platform with a narrow public rulebook and transparent moderation. Self-hosted.

- Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-korbat-design.md`
- Accounts and sessions (sub-project 1a): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-identity-auth-1a-design.md`
- Posting and feed (sub-project 2a): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-17-posting-feed-2a-design.md`
- Plans: `docs/superpowers/plans/`

## Dev quick start
```bash
pnpm install
node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs                # creates or completes infra/.env, apps/api/.env, apps/app/.env and apps/worker/.env, and derives apps/api/.env.test; values are random and never printed
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml up -d postgres redis mailpit   # dev host ports 55432, 56379, 51025, 58025 (movable: DEV_*_PORT in infra/.env)
pnpm --filter @korbat/api dev               # http://localhost:3000/api/health; reads apps/api/.env
pnpm --filter @korbat/worker dev            # the image worker; reads apps/worker/.env and works on .data/media
pnpm --filter @korbat/app web               # http://localhost:8081
pnpm --filter @korbat/admin dev             # the staff console at http://localhost:8090 (never 127.0.0.1); forwards /api/staff/* to the API above
```

Emails sent in development (sign-in codes, new-device alerts, lockout notices) land in Mailpit at http://localhost:58025. Locally the web app uses Cloudflare's always-pass Turnstile test key, so the human check never blocks you.

The data services are PostgreSQL 18 and Valkey (the BSD-licensed fork of Redis, still under the service name `redis`, on its own volume `valkeydata`: Valkey 9 cannot read the RDB format 12 that Redis 7.4 wrote into the old `redisdata` volume, which held only transient state and can be removed with `docker volume rm`). Valkey needs the password from `infra/.env`; `gen-dev-env` writes it into the API's `REDIS_URL` too, so an older `.env` is fixed by running it again.

korbat once ran MinIO and never used it. Images live on two Docker volumes instead, `media-uploads` and `media-store`. If an old stack left a `korbat_miniodata` volume behind, `docker volume rm korbat_miniodata` removes it.

## Tests
```bash
pnpm test                                     # unit tests of every package
node scripts/test-db.mjs                      # creates or migrates the korbat_test database; run it again after adding a migration
pnpm --filter @korbat/api test:integration    # needs postgres, redis and mailpit up
```

Integration tests have their own database, `korbat_test`, and their own Redis database, 15. Both are named in `apps/api/.env.test`, which `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` derives from `apps/api/.env`. Every run starts by emptying them, and refuses to start if a URL points anywhere else, so tests never touch development data.

Before they had their own database, the integration suites left accounts, profiles and posts in the development database, and the smoke test still leaves its first account per run, by then a moderator, with one open moderation case on that account's post. To see and remove them:

```bash
node scripts/clean-dev-fixtures.mjs          # lists test accounts and profiles without an account; deletes nothing
node scripts/clean-dev-fixtures.mjs --yes    # deletes them with everything they made
```

It only matches emails of the tests' shape, `<word>-<uuid>@korbat.local`, recomputes the counters of kept profiles and posts they touched, and refuses to run unless `API_APP_ORIGIN` in `infra/.env` is a localhost origin. It keeps an account that holds a staff key or that the moderation record names (one that decided anything, one on either side of a staff link, the subject of a case that a decision or a reveal names), and counts it as kept; every other case about a deleted account or one of its posts is deleted with it, the smoke test's open case included.

## Full stack
```bash
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml up -d --build   # http://localhost:8080, and the staff console at http://localhost:8090
node scripts/smoke-auth-stack.mjs --base http://localhost:8080 --console http://localhost:8090 --mailpit http://localhost:58025 --terms draft-2026-09 -- docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml
```

The smoke test first checks the staff console's site: its page carries the console's own policy and is never stored, and the staff API answers there (401 without a session) and nowhere else (Caddy's own 404 on the app's site); the console's case routes (the overview, the queue, a case, the appeals) answer the same two ways, and the console's site refuses the app's own moderation routes with a 404 of its own. It then signs up a throwaway account through Caddy, reads its code from Mailpit, posts and reads the post back from the public Latest timeline. It uploads a JPEG carrying a GPS position, posts it, and checks that the served file is a fresh WebP without metadata, that a symlink planted in the store from inside the worker gets a 404, and that deleting the post removes the image from disk. It checks the worker's isolation, then grants the account a staff role with the CLI and checks that its session was revoked. A second throwaway account edits its bio, changes its handle, reports the first account's post under a rule, finds that report undecided in its own list and as the last member, `moderation`, of its export, and deletes itself. Last, signed out, a notice that the same post is illegal is taken with the human check: it answers a reference and a token, the status page opens with that token, the receipt arrives in Mailpit, and the token in the receipt's link opens the same page. Nothing in it decides the case, since a decision needs a staff key: every run leaves one open case in lane 2 on the first account's post. One network can run it five times an hour and twenty times a day, since its two sign-ups count against the hourly sign-up limit and its signed-out notice against the limits of reports sent without an account.

After every sharp upgrade, add `--worst-case`: it also uploads flat-colour files at the pixel caps (48 MP 16-bit interlaced PNG, 48 MP progressive JPEG, 48 MP GIF, 16 MP AVIF), expects each to be ready without the worker being OOM-killed or restarted, and prints the worker's memory peak.

Caddy listens on 8080 inside its container as its own user, proxies `/api` to the API and serves the web app with the page's security headers; `index.html` is revalidated on every load and the hashed bundles are cached for a year. On 8090 it serves the staff console under the console's own policy and proxies only `/api/staff/*`, which the app's site refuses. On 8091 it serves the phones' push site: only the two alert topics' subscriptions reach ntfy, and every other path is Caddy's own 404. The compose file keeps cloudflared, Caddy, the API and the data services on separate networks, so cloudflared reaches only Caddy and Caddy only the API and ntfy. Under the Compose profile `notify`, the contact point's watcher (`notify`) and the push server (ntfy) join two networks of their own: `push`, which has no route out and whose clients the app's and the console's sites refuse with 403, and `watch`, which holds the watcher and PostgreSQL and nothing else. With the profile on, add `--push http://localhost:8091` to the smoke test: it checks that the push site answers ntfy's own API with 404 and hands a subscription to ntfy, and that from the push network the app's and the console's sites answer 403.

## Upgrading PostgreSQL

The stack runs PostgreSQL 18 on the `pgdata18` volume. A database from the earlier PostgreSQL 16 volume (`pgdata`) is moved by:

```bash
node scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs -- docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml
```

It dumps the old cluster with the old image in a throwaway container, starts the new server, restores the dump with every owner kept, and compares the row counts. The old volume stays until you remove it; the test database is created again by `node scripts/test-db.mjs`. Run `staff.js audit-verify` with every kept place before and after a major upgrade; Before going public says why.

## Upgrading

Authorities' orders and the alert channel (sub-project 3f) add a database role for the contact point's watcher, two services under a Compose profile, the hand-over's service under another, the report hold, and two arguments of the web build.

- On a database that exists, give the role its password and create it, with its USAGE on the schema `public`, once, as the superuser and against korbat's own database, before the first 3f migration: set `KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD` in `infra/.env` (`node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` does in development), run `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d postgres`, which passes it to the database's container, then the command below. Run twice, it changes nothing. The grant cannot be made by the migration: the migrator does not own the schema, and its grant would be a warning and nothing more. The migration checks both and stops with "create the role korbat_notify first" when either is missing, so a half-done upgrade stops there and not at a watcher that cannot read a row. A new data directory gets both from `infra/postgres/init/01-roles.sh`.

```bash
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml exec -T postgres sh -c 'psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" -v pw="$KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD"' <<'SQL'
SET korbat.notify_pw = :'pw';
DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'korbat_notify') THEN
  IF current_setting('korbat.notify_pw') = '' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD is empty in the postgres container: set it in infra/.env, then up -d postgres'; END IF;
  EXECUTE format('CREATE ROLE korbat_notify LOGIN PASSWORD %L', current_setting('korbat.notify_pw'));
END IF; END $$;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO korbat_notify;
SQL
```

- `notify` and ntfy run under the Compose profile `notify`. Switch it on in one place, `COMPOSE_PROFILES=notify` in `infra/.env`, which Compose reads for every command: the README's commands stay as they are, and an upgrade then recreates the two services with the rest. Without that line they are never started, or keep running an old image against a migrated database.
- Until the contact-point mailbox exists, leave the profile off and set `API_NOTIFY=off`: korbat then says on the console's home screen that phone alerts are switched off on this server, and mails no "Phone alerts are down". No setting of `notify`, ntfy or the hand-over is needed for the stack to start.
- The quarantine's service (`quarantine`, sub-project 3d) runs under the Compose profile `quarantine`, which stays off: the operator starts it by hand with the steps under Quarantine. Its volume `media-quarantine` is created by its first run, owned by the API image's user; the hand-over's service now mounts it too, read-only. It needs no setting, and nothing of it is backed up.
- The hand-over's service (`handover`) runs under the Compose profile `handover`, which stays off: the operator starts it by hand for one hand-over, with the directory on its command line (Authorities' orders, Notifications and hand-overs). It needs no setting.
- The report hold is on from the upgrade: while a report of sealed images to the authorities is owed, the deletion of the account keeps its address, and nothing else, for at most 7 days. `API_REPORT_HOLD=off` in `infra/.env` ends the practice for everyone and deletes as before; set it only on counsel's advice.
- The web build takes `WEB_CONTACT_POINT` and `WEB_HOME_STATE` from `infra/.env` for the terms (the contact point for authorities and korbat's Member State). Neither is required, and both stay empty, or the state alone set, until the last step of Before going public; `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` adds the two lines to an existing file without changing a value. Rebuild the caddy image after a change of either.

## Backups

The backup of `media-store` is deleted 30 days after it was taken (`RETENTION.backupDays`, which the terms publish), without exception but an authority's written demand. `media-quarantine` is never backed up (Quarantine, step 4).

## Restoring

Restore the database and the `media-store` volume from the same moment.
````
