```ts
import { RETENTION, type AlertFacts, type ReleaseNoticeView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { MailRefused, type MailMessage, type NoticeUpdateLine } from "../../mail/mailer";
import type { DecisionMailSubject } from "../../mail/templates";
import type { AuthDeps } from "../context";
import { decrypt, encrypt, randomToken, safeEqual } from "../crypto";
import { emailHash } from "../identifiers";
import { HOUR } from "../limits";
import { noticeTime } from "./notify";

/**
 * The auth module's side of reports and notices (3c design, section 5): a signed-out notifier's name and address, which
 * live here, encrypted, where the API's role cannot reach them, and every mail of the moderation module, which never
 * sees an address or a mail token. The moderation module names a contact by an id it chose, names an account by its id,
 * and passes typed messages: no caller passes free text, and this module builds every link itself.
 */

const DAY = 24 * HOUR;

/** An address that is not confirmed gets at most one receipt in this long; further ones are folded into the next daily mail. */
export const RECEIPT_CAP_MS = DAY;

/** The receipt of a report or a notice: its reference, when it was received, and the korbat links it named, in the order named. */
export interface NoticeReceivedMessage {
  template: "notice_received";
  ref: string;
  receivedAt: Date;
  items: readonly string[];
}

/** The daily update of decisions on the reports an account sent: its lines, as the moderation module composed them. */
export interface AccountUpdateMessage {
  template: "notice_update";
  lines: readonly NoticeUpdateLine[];
}

/**
 * The statement of reasons to the author of what a decision restricts or lifts: the subject by its key, and the
 * statement's paragraphs exactly as they were rendered for the author's screen. 3e (design, sections 7.15 and 18, W.6):
 * a suspension or termination taken at once, and the lift of one (or its end when a reversal broke its basis), are
 * mailed under a subject and a lead of their own, with the same paragraphs; the moderation module picks the template
 * (mailTemplateOf). Times are instants, printed here as the notices print them.
 */
export type DecisionMessage =
  | { template: "moderation_decision"; subject: DecisionMailSubject; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  // 3e Task 4: an announced measure, with its days (null for a termination), the reply window in hours and the earliest start.
  | { template: "suspension_announced"; measure: "suspend" | "terminate"; days: number | null; window: number; earliestStart: string; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  | { template: "suspension_started_at_once"; measure: "suspend" | "terminate"; days: number | null; endsAt: string | null; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  // 3e Task 4: the answer to the person's reply, which kept the measure in force or reversed it.
  | { template: "reply_answered"; outcome: "kept" | "reversed"; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  | { template: "suspension_lifted"; measure: "suspend" | "terminate"; why: "lifted" | "basis"; period: "not_started" | "running" | "ended"; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  // 3e Task 4: a withdrawal signed `replaced`, with the withdrawn decision's time and whether the person had replied to it.
  | { template: "suspension_lifted"; measure: "suspend" | "terminate"; why: "replaced"; decidedAt: string; replied: boolean; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  // 3e Task 5: a warning about the account's reports; a restriction of them, with its days and its end.
  | { template: "reporting_warned"; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  | { template: "reporting_restricted"; days: number; endsAt: string; paragraphs: readonly string[] }
  // 3f Task 3 (design, W.5): an order's notice, a reinstatement after one, and the authority's words added to a notice
  // already told. Each says only that a notice is there or has grown: its paragraphs are not mailed, and are empty.
  | { template: "order_notice" | "order_reinstated_notice" | "order_notice_added"; paragraphs: readonly string[] };

/** The templates of a decision's statement mail: a stop of the address never holds one back. */
const DECISION_TEMPLATES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  "moderation_decision",
  "suspension_announced",
  "suspension_started_at_once",
  "reply_answered",
  "suspension_lifted",
  "reporting_warned",
  "reporting_restricted",
  "order_notice",
  "order_reinstated_notice",
  "order_notice_added",
]);

/** Whether an account's message is a decision's statement. */
const isDecisionMessage = (message: { template: string }): message is DecisionMessage => DECISION_TEMPLATES.has(message.template);

/** What the statement's paragraphs are joined with in a mail's data: one paragraph per line. */
const LINE_BREAK = String.fromCharCode(10);

/** A decision's message as its template's flat data: one data value for the statement, one paragraph per line, exactly as it was rendered. */
function decisionData(message: DecisionMessage): Record<string, string> {
  const statement = message.paragraphs.join(LINE_BREAK);
  switch (message.template) {
    case "moderation_decision":
      return { subject: message.subject, statement };
    case "suspension_announced":
      return { measure: message.measure, statement, window: String(message.window), earliestStart: noticeTime(new Date(message.earliestStart)), ...(message.days === null ? {} : { days: String(message.days) }) };
    case "suspension_started_at_once":
      return { measure: message.measure, statement, ...(message.days === null ? {} : { days: String(message.days) }), ...(message.endsAt === null ? {} : { endsAt: noticeTime(new Date(message.endsAt)) }) };
    case "reply_answered":
      return { outcome: message.outcome, statement };
    case "suspension_lifted":
      return message.why === "replaced"
        ? { measure: message.measure, why: message.why, decidedAt: noticeTime(new Date(message.decidedAt)), replied: String(message.replied), statement }
        : { measure: message.measure, why: message.why, period: message.period, statement };
    case "reporting_warned":
      return { statement };
    case "reporting_restricted":
      return { statement, days: String(message.days), endsAt: noticeTime(new Date(message.endsAt)) };
    case "order_notice":
    case "order_reinstated_notice":
    case "order_notice_added":
      // A fixed body: nothing of the notice goes by mail.
      return {};
  }
}

/** What may be sent to a signed-out notifier's contact by itself: the receipt. Its updates go by address, through mailNotifierUpdates. */
export type NotifierMessage = NoticeReceivedMessage;
/**
 * 3d (design, sections 7.1 and 7.15; W.8): the notice that korbat lost the files of an image of the account's post while
 * they were kept apart in the quarantine, with the post's creation time. No stop of the address holds it back: it is no
 * mail about the account's reports.
 */
export interface ImageLostMessage {
  template: "image_lost";
  postCreatedAt: Date;
}

/**
 * 3d Task 2 (design, sections 7.2 and 7.15; W.6 and W.8): the author's notice of a release of sealed images of their
 * posts, with the view its paragraphs are rendered from: the ground, the times, the posts' times and the counts, never an
 * authority, a reference or an assessment. No stop of the address holds it back: it is about the account's own posts.

  template: "release_notice";

}

/** One contact's share of the daily update: the lines of its notice, and its receipt when the 24-hour cap folded it. */
export interface NotifierUpdatePart {
  contactId: string;

  ref: string;

}

/** What became of one contact's share: as a mail's result, or "unavailable" when the relay could not take that address's mail or the contact could not be read. */
export type NotifierUpdateResult = "sent" | "suppressed" | "no_address" | "forgotten" | "refused" | "unavailable";

/**
 * The staff alerts: counts, times and a staff account's public handle, never a link or content. The urgent lane's alert;
 * the cases that wait longer than their lane's response time, and those that hold a measure taken while deciding for
 * more than a day; the staff account that confirmed many decisions in a short time; the one that reached its daily case
 * limit; every reveal of who sent a report, with the day's count; and every decision that lifted the protection of
 * images reported as child sexual abuse material.
 */
export type StaffMessage =
  | StaffAlertMessage
  // 3f's review (people4): `phones`, whether the phone alerts are on (NOTIFY), so the mail never says a push went to a
  // phone when nothing publishes one, and says instead that it is the only alert.
  | { template: "moderation_urgent"; count: number; oldest: Date; phones: boolean }
  | { template: "moderation_waiting"; lanes: readonly { lane: 0 | 1 | 2; count: number; oldest: Date }[]; interim: number; replies?: { count: number; oldest: Date } | null; phones: boolean }
  | { template: "moderation_burst"; handle: string; count: number }
  | { template: "moderation_reads"; handle: string; limit: number }
  | { template: "moderation_reveal"; handle: string; at: Date; count: number; limit: number }
  | { template: "moderation_csam_lifted"; handle: string; at: Date; what: "unsealed" | "dismissed" };

/**
 * 3f (design, sections 7.2, 7.19 and 18, W.4): the staff alerts whose mail is their push's sentence, which the alert tick
 * mails from a row of alert_outbox: the row's facts, counts and times only, and nothing else. Later tasks of 3f add their
 * kinds here as they first write them.
 */
export type StaffAlertKind =
  | "contact_mail"
  | "contact_mail_escalated"
  | "order_due"
  | "mailbox_unreachable"
  | "alert_channel_down"
  | "order_opened"
  | "order_corrected"
  | "order_unverified"
  // Task 3: an order given effect, an order's measure lifted, and a held notice about to be released.
  | "order_effected"
  | "order_reinstated"
  | "hold_ending"
  // Task 6: the copy of the audit log's tail is overdue, and someone who did not take the last copy took one.
  | "copy_overdue"
  | "copy_taken"
  // Task 5's two daily kinds, joined in 3f's review: a report to an authority owed, a hand-over's copy not destroyed.
  | "report_owed"
  | "handover_undestroyed"
  // 3d Task 1: a move of sealed files that is due, which alert_steps() writes daily, and files the quarantine's record
  // says are lost, which staff.js quarantine-record writes with its record.
  | "quarantine_due"
  | "quarantine_lost"
  // 3d Task 2: a released file still recorded in the quarantine, which alert_steps() writes daily, and an admin's release

  | "release_undestroyed"
  | "seal_released"
  // 3d Task 3: the edge's job gave up on purges, which it writes as its own row of the outbox.
  | "edge_purge_failed"
  // 3d Task 5: the transparency job published a day's value without an outside timestamp, or found the day before
  // without a published value, each written as the job's own row of the outbox.
  | "head_unwitnessed"
  | "head_missed";
export interface StaffAlertMessage {
  template: StaffAlertKind;
  facts: AlertFacts;
}

/**
 * A staff alert's template data: every member as the text the template prints. A 3f alert's facts go as they are, each
 * count as its digits, with the time it is sent: the template prints a time with its day only when that is not today's.
 */
function staffData(message: StaffMessage, now: Date): Record<string, string> {
  switch (message.template) {
    case "contact_mail":
    case "contact_mail_escalated":
    case "order_due":
    case "mailbox_unreachable":
    case "alert_channel_down":
    case "order_opened":
    case "order_corrected":
    case "order_unverified":
    case "order_effected":
    case "order_reinstated":
    case "hold_ending":
    case "copy_overdue":
    case "copy_taken":
    case "report_owed":
    case "handover_undestroyed":
    case "quarantine_due":
    case "quarantine_lost":
    case "release_undestroyed":
    case "seal_released":
    case "edge_purge_failed":
    case "head_unwitnessed":
    case "head_missed":
      return { ...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(message.facts).map(([name, value]) => [name, String(value)])), now: now.toISOString() };
    case "moderation_urgent":
      return { count: String(message.count), oldest: noticeTime(message.oldest), phones: message.phones ? "on" : "off" };
    case "moderation_waiting": {
      // A lane's pair only for a lane with a case past its time, and the measures' count only when it is not 0.
      const data: Record<string, string> = { phones: message.phones ? "on" : "off" };
      for (const lane of message.lanes) {
        if (lane.count <= 0) continue;
        data[`lane${lane.lane}Count`] = String(lane.count);
        data[`lane${lane.lane}Oldest`] = noticeTime(lane.oldest);
      }
      if (message.interim > 0) data.interimCount = String(message.interim);
      // 3e Task 4: the replies unanswered for longer than korbat's aim, only when there are any.
      if (message.replies && message.replies.count > 0) {
        data.replyCount = String(message.replies.count);
        data.replyOldest = noticeTime(message.replies.oldest);
      }
      return data;
    }
    case "moderation_burst":
      return { handle: message.handle, count: String(message.count) };
    case "moderation_csam_lifted":
      return { handle: message.handle, time: noticeTime(message.at), what: message.what };
    case "moderation_reads":
      return { handle: message.handle, limit: String(message.limit) };
    case "moderation_reveal":
      return { handle: message.handle, time: noticeTime(message.at), count: String(message.count), limit: String(message.limit) };
  }
}

export type NotifierMailResult = "sent" | "folded" | "suppressed" | "no_address" | "forgotten" | "refused";
export type AccountMailResult = "sent" | "suppressed" | "no_address" | "refused";

/** What staff may know of a signed-out notifier without a reveal: never the name or the address themselves. */
export interface NotifierFacts {
  /** False for an id no contact has: it was never stored, or the janitor has forgotten it. Then the other four are false too. */
  found: boolean;
  named: boolean;
  contactGiven: boolean;
  confirmed: boolean;
  suppressed: boolean;
}

/** A contact's ciphertexts open under the key, or under a key it replaced. Nothing read is ever written back under the newer key. */
const open = (deps: Pick<AuthDeps, "config">, payload: string): string => decrypt(payload, [deps.config.notifierKey, ...deps.config.notifierPreviousKeys]).toString("utf8");
const seal = (deps: AuthDeps, plain: string): string => encrypt(Buffer.from(plain, "utf8"), deps.config.notifierKey);

/** The same day `months` calendar months later in UTC; a day the target month lacks becomes that month's last day. */
function monthsLater(at: Date, months: number): Date {
  const month = at.getUTCMonth() + months;
  const lastDay = new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), month + 1, 0)).getUTCDate();
  return new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), month, Math.min(at.getUTCDate(), lastDay), at.getUTCHours(), at.getUTCMinutes(), at.getUTCSeconds(), at.getUTCMilliseconds()));
}

/** The cap's marker for an address, by its keyed hash: set when a receipt goes to it unconfirmed, gone a day later. */
const receiptCapKey = (hash: string) => `notifier-receipt:${hash}`;

/** The receipt's template data. The page link is this module's: the status page's address with the contact's mail token in the fragment, which no server log sees. */
function receiptData(deps: AuthDeps, message: NoticeReceivedMessage, pageUrl?: string): Record<string, string> {
  return {
    ref: message.ref,
    time: noticeTime(message.receivedAt),
    items: message.items.join(", "),
    ...(pageUrl === undefined ? {} : { pageUrl }),
    termsUrl: `${deps.config.appOrigin}/terms`,
  };
}

/** Sends one mail. "refused" when the relay refused the recipient for good; any other failure is thrown, for the caller to try again. */
async function deliver(deps: AuthDeps, message: MailMessage): Promise<"sent" | "refused"> {
  try {
    await deps.mailer.send(message);
    return "sent";
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof MailRefused) return "refused";
    throw err;
  }
}

/**
 * Stores a signed-out notifier's contact under the id the moderation module wrote on the notice: the name and the
 * address normalised and encrypted under the notifier key, the address's keyed hash for the cap and for stops, and, with
 * an address, a fresh mail token encrypted beside it. A disposable address is taken: a notifier may want one. The contact
 * is forgotten 13 months on unless the notice is still owed something by then.
 */
export async function storeNotifierContact(deps: AuthDeps, contactId: string, contact: { name?: string; email?: string }): Promise<void> {
  const name = contact.name?.trim() || null;
  const email = contact.email?.trim().toLowerCase() || null;
  await deps.repo.createNotifierContact({
    id: contactId,
    nameEnc: name === null ? null : seal(deps, name),
    emailEnc: email === null ? null : seal(deps, email),
    emailHash: email === null ? null : emailHash(deps.config.authHmacKey, email),
    // The token of the mails' link: it alone confirms or stops the address, so whoever typed someone else's address cannot.
    mailTokenEnc: email === null ? null : seal(deps, randomToken()),
    forgetAfter: monthsLater(deps.now(), RETENTION.contactMaxMonths),
  });
}

/**
 * Sends a signed-out notifier's receipt, under three rules. A stopped address gets nothing ("suppressed"). An address
 * that is not confirmed gets one receipt in 24 hours, and a further one is "folded": it rides in the next daily mail, so
 * typing someone's address into the form many times sends them one mail. A confirmed address has no cap. "forgotten"
 * when no contact has the id, "no_address" when the contact left none. A failure of the relay that is not about the
 * address is thrown, and gives the day's one receipt back first, so the retry is sent rather than folded.
 */
export async function mailNotifier(deps: AuthDeps, contactId: string, message: NotifierMessage): Promise<NotifierMailResult> {
  const contact = await deps.repo.findNotifierContact(contactId);
  if (!contact) return "forgotten";
  if (!contact.emailEnc || !contact.emailHash || !contact.mailTokenEnc) return "no_address";
  const hash = contact.emailHash;
  if ((await deps.repo.suppressedNotifierHashes([hash])).has(hash)) return "suppressed";
  // Opened before the cap is taken: a ciphertext no configured key opens throws here and spends nothing.
  const to = open(deps, contact.emailEnc);
  const pageUrl = `${deps.config.appOrigin}/notice/${message.ref}#t=${open(deps, contact.mailTokenEnc)}`;
  const confirmed = (await deps.repo.confirmedNotifierHashes([hash], deps.now())).has(hash);
  if (!confirmed && !(await deps.kv.setIfAbsent(receiptCapKey(hash), "1", RECEIPT_CAP_MS))) return "folded";
  try {
    return await deliver(deps, { to, template: "notice_received", data: receiptData(deps, message, pageUrl) });
  } catch (err) {
    if (!confirmed) await deps.kv.del(receiptCapKey(hash)).catch((failure: unknown) => deps.log.warn({ err: failure }, "notifier receipt: the day's one receipt could not be given back after a failed send"));
    throw err;
  }
}

/**
 * Sends a mail to an account's own address, which its sign-in code confirmed: no cap and no confirmation. A stop of
 * that address applies to the two report mails, the receipt and the daily update, and never to a statement of reasons.
 * The update of an account is signed in: it carries its lines and neither a receipt nor a page link, since an account
 * follows its reports in the app. "no_address" for an account that is deleted or was never there.
 */
export async function mailAccount(deps: AuthDeps, userId: string, message: AccountMessage): Promise<AccountMailResult> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(userId);
  if (!user) return "no_address";
  if (isDecisionMessage(message)) {
    // A statement is never held back by a stop of the address.
    return deliver(deps, { to: user.email, template: message.template, data: decisionData(message) });
  }
  // 3d: nor is the notice of a lost image, which is about the account's own post and not about its reports.
  if (message.template === "image_lost") return deliver(deps, { to: user.email, template: "image_lost", data: { createdAt: noticeTime(message.postCreatedAt) } });
  // 3d Task 2: nor is the notice of a release. Its paragraphs are rendered from these flat members by the template, from
  // the same function as the app's notice screen; the times go as ISO text and are printed as korbat's mails print them.
  if (message.template === "release_notice") {
    const view = message.view;
    return deliver(deps, {
      to: user.email,
      template: "release_notice",
      data: {
        basis: view.basis,
        releasedAt: view.releasedAt,
        backupsClearAt: view.backupsClearAt,
        upload: view.upload ? "yes" : "no",
        postCount: String(view.postCount),
        images: String(view.images),
        createdAt: view.posts[0]?.createdAt ?? "",
      },
    });
  }
  const hash = emailHash(deps.config.authHmacKey, user.email);
  if ((await deps.repo.suppressedNotifierHashes([hash])).has(hash)) return "suppressed";
  if (message.template === "notice_update") return deliver(deps, { to: user.email, template: "notice_update", data: { signedIn: true, lines: [...message.lines], receipts: [], pages: [] } });
  return deliver(deps, { to: user.email, template: "notice_received", data: receiptData(deps, message) });
}

/**
 * The daily update to signed-out notifiers (3c design, sections 5 and 7.8): the parts are grouped by their contacts'
 * address, which only this module can see, and each address gets one notice_update with every part's lines, every
 * carried receipt with its page link, and the page link of each other notice it has a line for. A page link is the
 * status page's address with that contact's own mail token in the fragment, the same link its receipt carried.
 *
 * It applies a stop of the address, and neither the confirmation nor the 24-hour cap: nothing is withheld for want of a
 * confirmed address. It answers for each contact, and throws for none: an address whose mail the relay could not take is
 * "unavailable", so its lines stay pending while every other address's update is still sent. Each contact is read in a
 * try of its own: one that cannot be read (a ciphertext no configured key opens) is logged with its id, never an
 * address, and answered "unavailable" too.
 */
export async function mailNotifierUpdates(deps: AuthDeps, parts: readonly NotifierUpdatePart[]): Promise<Map<string, NotifierUpdateResult>> {
  const results = new Map<string, NotifierUpdateResult>();
  /** The readable parts, by their address's keyed hash, in the order given. */
  const byAddress = new Map<string, { to: string; parts: { part: NotifierUpdatePart; pageUrl: string }[] }>();
  for (const part of parts) {
    try {
      const contact = await deps.repo.findNotifierContact(part.contactId);
      if (!contact) {
        results.set(part.contactId, "forgotten");
        continue;
      }
      if (!contact.emailEnc || !contact.emailHash || !contact.mailTokenEnc) {
        results.set(part.contactId, "no_address");
        continue;
      }
      if ((await deps.repo.suppressedNotifierHashes([contact.emailHash])).has(contact.emailHash)) {
        results.set(part.contactId, "suppressed");
        continue;
      }
      const to = open(deps, contact.emailEnc);
      const pageUrl = `${deps.config.appOrigin}/notice/${part.ref}#t=${open(deps, contact.mailTokenEnc)}`;
      const group = byAddress.get(contact.emailHash) ?? { to, parts: [] };
      group.parts.push({ part, pageUrl });
      byAddress.set(contact.emailHash, group);
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.error({ err, contactId: part.contactId }, "notifier update: the contact could not be read; its lines stay pending");
      results.set(part.contactId, "unavailable");
    }
  }
  for (const group of byAddress.values()) {
    const receipts = group.parts.flatMap(({ part, pageUrl }) => (part.receipt ? [{ ref: part.receipt.ref, time: noticeTime(part.receipt.receivedAt), items: part.receipt.items.join(", "), pageUrl }] : []));
    // A notice whose receipt rides in this update has its page with the receipt; every other notice with a line gets a page paragraph.
    const pages = group.parts.flatMap(({ part, pageUrl }) => (part.receipt || part.lines.length === 0 ? [] : [{ ref: part.ref, pageUrl }]));
    const lines = group.parts.flatMap(({ part }) => [...part.lines]);
    let result: NotifierUpdateResult;
    try {
      result = await deliver(deps, {
        to: group.to,
        template: "notice_update",
        data: { signedIn: false, lines, receipts, pages, ...(receipts.length > 0 ? { termsUrl: `${deps.config.appOrigin}/terms` } : {}) },
      });
    } catch (err) {
      // The relay could not take this address's mail: the other addresses' mails still go. The contacts' ids, never the address.
      deps.log.warn({ err, contactIds: group.parts.map(({ part }) => part.contactId) }, "notifier update: not sent; its lines stay pending for the next round");
      result = "unavailable";
    }
    for (const { part } of group.parts) results.set(part.contactId, result);
  }
  // In the order the parts were given, whatever order the addresses were mailed in.
  return new Map(parts.map((part) => [part.contactId, results.get(part.contactId) ?? "unavailable"]));
}

/**
 * Sends a staff alert to every live staff account's address, best effort: a failed send is logged and never thrown, and
 * the answer is the number of addresses the relay took, 0 when it took none or there is no live staff account. It
 * applies no throttle: the moderation module keeps every throttle, as a key in the shared limit store.
 */
export async function mailStaff(deps: AuthDeps, message: StaffMessage): Promise<number> {
  const data = staffData(message, deps.now());
  let addresses: string[];
  try {
    addresses = await deps.repo.liveStaffAddresses();
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.error({ err, template: message.template }, "staff alert: the staff accounts could not be read");
    return 0;
  }
  let accepted = 0;
  for (const to of addresses) {
    try {
      await deps.mailer.send({ to, template: message.template, data });
      accepted++;
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.error({ err, template: message.template }, "staff alert email failed");
    }
  }
  return accepted;
}

/**
 * 3d Task 5 (design, sections 5, 7.7 and 18, W.8): the audit head's daily mail to the keeper, the copy that is not on
 * korbat's server: the day, the value, the place and the hash, from which the keeper computes the value again, and whether
 * an outside timestamp is stored. Typed like every message, so no caller passes free text.
 */
export interface KeeperMessage {
  template: "head_published";
  day: string;
  value: string;
  seq: number;
  hash: string;
  witnessed: boolean;
}

/** What became of the keeper's mail: sent, not sent while HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL is empty, refused by the relay, or failed. */
export type KeeperMailResult = "sent" | "off" | "refused" | "failed";

/**
 * Sends the keeper's daily mail to HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL and to nobody else: the caller names no address, and none is read from
 * an account or a staff list. While the setting is empty it sends nothing ("off"). A failure is logged, without the
 * address, and answered, never thrown: the day's value stands published either way, and nothing retries the mail.
 */
export async function mailKeeper(deps: AuthDeps, message: KeeperMessage): Promise<KeeperMailResult> {
  const to = deps.config.keeperMail;
  if (to === null) return "off";
  try {
    await deps.mailer.send({
      to,
      template: "head_published",
      data: { day: message.day, value: message.value, seq: String(message.seq), hash: message.hash, witnessed: message.witnessed ? "stored" : "none" },
    });
    return "sent";
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.error({ err, template: "head_published", day: message.day }, "keeper's mail: not sent");
    return err instanceof MailRefused ? "refused" : "failed";
  }
}

/** For each id: whether a contact has it, whether a name and an address were given, and whether the address is confirmed or stopped now. */
export async function notifierFacts(deps: AuthDeps, contactIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, NotifierFacts>> {
  const rows = await deps.repo.notifierContactFacts(contactIds);
  const hashes = rows.flatMap((row) => (row.emailHash === null ? [] : [row.emailHash]));
  const [confirmed, suppressed] = await Promise.all([deps.repo.confirmedNotifierHashes(hashes, deps.now()), deps.repo.suppressedNotifierHashes(hashes)]);
  const byId = new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.id, row]));
  return new Map(
    contactIds.map((id): [string, NotifierFacts] => {
      const row = byId.get(id);
      if (!row) return [id, { found: false, named: false, contactGiven: false, confirmed: false, suppressed: false }];
      return [id, { found: true, named: row.named, contactGiven: row.contactGiven, confirmed: row.emailHash !== null && confirmed.has(row.emailHash), suppressed: row.emailHash !== null && suppressed.has(row.emailHash) }];
    }),
  );
}

/** The name a notifier gave, or null: for a confirmed reveal only. The address is never handed out. */
export async function notifierName(deps: AuthDeps, contactId: string): Promise<string | null> {
  const contact = await deps.repo.findNotifierContact(contactId);
  return contact?.nameEnc ? open(deps, contact.nameEnc) : null;
}

/** The contact's address hash when the token is its mail token, compared in constant time; null for anything else. */
async function addressOfToken(deps: AuthDeps, contactId: string, token: string): Promise<string | null> {
  const contact = await deps.repo.findNotifierContact(contactId);
  if (!contact?.mailTokenEnc || !contact.emailHash) return null;
  let mailToken: string;
  try {
    mailToken = open(deps, contact.mailTokenEnc);
  } catch (err) {
    // A contact no configured key opens matches nothing; the fault is the operator's to see, with the contact's id and no address.
    deps.log.error({ err, contactId }, "notifier contact: its mail token could not be decrypted");
    return null;
  }
  return safeEqual(mailToken, token) ? contact.emailHash : null;
}

/** Whether the token is the contact's mail token; false when the contact has none. */
export async function notifierMailTokenMatches(deps: AuthDeps, contactId: string, token: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return (await addressOfToken(deps, contactId, token)) !== null;
}

/**
 * "I sent this": with the contact's mail token, records the address as confirmed for 30 days and lifts any stop of it.
 * False, and nothing done, for any other token: typing someone's address proves nothing about it.
 */
export async function confirmNotifier(deps: AuthDeps, contactId: string, token: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const hash = await addressOfToken(deps, contactId, token);
  if (hash === null) return false;
  const now = deps.now();
  await deps.repo.confirmNotifierAddress(hash, now, new Date(now.getTime() + RETENTION.confirmationDays * DAY));
  return true;
}

/** "Stop": with the contact's mail token, korbat sends this address no more mails about reports. Its notices are still processed. */
export async function stopNotifier(deps: AuthDeps, contactId: string, token: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const hash = await addressOfToken(deps, contactId, token);
  if (hash === null) return false;
  await deps.repo.suppressNotifierAddress(hash);
  return true;
}

/** Whether the account's address asked korbat to stop its report mails. */
export async function accountReportMailStopped(deps: AuthDeps, userId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(userId);
  if (!user) return false;
  const hash = emailHash(deps.config.authHmacKey, user.email);
  return (await deps.repo.suppressedNotifierHashes([hash])).has(hash);
}

/** Lifts a stop of the account's address, for the account's own Settings: the session proves the address. True when there was one. */
export async function resumeAccountReportMail(deps: AuthDeps, userId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(userId);
  if (!user) return false;
  return deps.repo.liftNotifierSuppression(emailHash(deps.config.authHmacKey, user.email));
}

/** Moves the day these contacts are forgotten. */
export function forgetNotifierAfter(deps: AuthDeps, contactIds: readonly string[], at: Date): Promise<void> {
  return deps.repo.setNotifierForgetAfter(contactIds, at);
}

/** The contacts that gave this address, with the names they gave: for an access request from a signed-out notifier, from the command line only. */
export async function findNotifierContacts(deps: Pick<AuthDeps, "repo" | "config">, email: string): Promise<{ id: string; name: string | null }[]> {
  const rows = await deps.repo.notifierContactsByEmailHash(emailHash(deps.config.authHmacKey, email));
  return rows.map((row) => ({ id: row.id, name: row.nameEnc ? open(deps, row.nameEnc) : null }));
}

/** How many contacts and confirmations the janitor should have removed more than a day ago: a count only, for the console's overview. */
export function overdueContacts(deps: AuthDeps): Promise<number> {
  return deps.repo.countNotifierRowsDue(new Date(deps.now().getTime() - DAY));
}
```

```ts
export interface AuthForStaff {
  /** Registration options for the key an enrolment link's holder is about to create. */
  enrollOptions(input: StaffEnrollOptionsRequest): Promise<StaffEnrollOptions>;
  /** Checks the browser's answer and stores the staff key, spending the link; the owner is mailed. */
  enrollVerify(input: StaffEnrollVerifyRequest, ctx: StaffRequestContext): Promise<StaffEnrollVerifyResponse>;
  /** Discoverable-credential options for a staff sign-in. */
  signInOptions(): Promise<{ options: PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON }>;
  /** Checks a staff key's assertion and opens a staff session; the route sets its cookies with setStaffCookies. */
  signInVerify(input: StaffSignInVerifyRequest, ctx: StaffRequestContext): Promise<StaffSignedIn>;
  /** Stands before every staff route that needs a session: reads it and sets `staffSession` on the context. */
  requireStaff: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The session's account and both its ends, with the seconds left. */
  me(session: ActiveStaffSession): Promise<StaffMe>;
  /** The person's own live staff sessions. */
  sessions(session: ActiveStaffSession): Promise<StaffSessionsResponse>;
  /** The person's own live staff keys. */
  keys(session: ActiveStaffSession): Promise<StaffKeysResponse>;
  /** Ends the session, on the record; the route clears its cookies with clearStaffCookies. */
  signOut(session: ActiveStaffSession, ctx: StaffRequestContext): Promise<void>;
  /** Options for confirming one action with the session's key: a challenge bound to the session and to exactly that action. */
  stepUpOptions(session: ActiveStaffSession, request: StaffStepUpOptionsRequest): Promise<{ options: PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON }>;
  /**
   * Stands before every staff route that changes something, behind requireStaff: verifies the body's `stepUp` against the
   * action, the target `target` reads from the request and the body's params, and sets `staffStepUp` on the context.
   */
  requireStaffStepUp(action: StaffStepUpAction, target: (c: Context<AppEnv>) => string | undefined): MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** Revokes one of the person's own live staff sessions, on the record with its confirmation; false when the handle names none. */
  revokeSession(session: ActiveStaffSession, confirmed: StaffStepUpConfirmed, ctx: StaffRequestContext): Promise<boolean>;
}

/**
 * What the moderation module needs from this one (3c design, section 5): the human check of a signed-out notice, a
 * signed-out notifier's contact, which is stored here, encrypted, out of the API role's reach, and every mail to an
 * account, a notifier or staff. The moderation module names a contact by the id it chose and an account by its id; it
 * never sees an address or a mail token, and a message is a typed union over the templates, so no caller passes free
 * text. `mailNotifier` and `mailAccount` answer "refused" when the relay refused the recipient for good and throw
 * MailUnavailable for any other failure, so the caller records the one and tries the other again.
 */
export interface AuthForModeration {
  /** Turnstile's answer for the token of a signed-out notice; every failure is false. */
  verifyHuman(token: string): Promise<boolean>;
  /** Stores a signed-out notifier's name and address under the id the notice carries, with a fresh mail token when an address is given. */
  storeNotifierContact(contactId: string, contact: { name?: string; email?: string }): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * Sends a signed-out notifier's receipt, with its page link. "suppressed" for a stopped address, "folded" for a
   * second receipt in 24 hours to an address that is not confirmed, "no_address" for a contact without one, "forgotten"
   * for an id no contact has (it was never stored, or the janitor has deleted it).
   */
  mailNotifier(contactId: string, message: NotifierMessage): Promise<NotifierMailResult>;
  /**
   * Sends a mail to an account's own address, with neither the cap nor a confirmation: the receipt and the daily update
   * of its reports, which a stop of that address holds back ("suppressed"), and the statement of a decision about it,
   * which nothing holds back. "no_address" for a deleted account.
   */
  mailAccount(userId: string, message: AccountMessage): Promise<AccountMailResult>;
  /**
   * The daily update to signed-out notifiers: one notice_update for each address the parts' contacts gave, with every
   * part's lines, every carried receipt and the page link of each other notice. It applies a stop of the address and
   * neither the confirmation nor the cap, answers for each contact, and throws for none: "unavailable" when the relay
   * could not take that address's mail or the contact could not be read.
   */
  mailNotifierUpdates(parts: readonly NotifierUpdatePart[]): Promise<Map<string, NotifierUpdateResult>>;
  /** Sends a staff alert to every live staff account, best effort; answers how many addresses the relay took, and never throws for a failed send. */
  mailStaff(message: StaffMessage): Promise<number>;
  /** For each id, whether a contact has it, whether a name and an address were given, and whether the address is confirmed or stopped. */
  notifierFacts(contactIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, NotifierFacts>>;
  /** The name a notifier gave, or null: for a confirmed reveal only. */
  notifierName(contactId: string): Promise<string | null>;
  /** Whether the token is the contact's mail token, compared in constant time; false when it has none. */
  notifierMailTokenMatches(contactId: string, token: string): Promise<boolean>;
  /** With the contact's mail token: the address is confirmed for 30 days and any stop of it lifted. False for any other token. */
  confirmNotifier(contactId: string, token: string): Promise<boolean>;
  /** With the contact's mail token: no more report mails to the address. False for any other token. */
  stopNotifier(contactId: string, token: string): Promise<boolean>;
  /** Whether the account's own address said stop. */
  accountReportMailStopped(userId: string): Promise<boolean>;
  /** Lifts a stop of the account's own address; true when there was one. */
  resumeAccountReportMail(userId: string): Promise<boolean>;
  /** Sets the day each of these contacts is forgotten. */
  forgetNotifierAfter(contactIds: readonly string[], at: Date): Promise<void>;
  /** Command line only: the contacts that gave an address, with the names they gave, for an access request. */
  findNotifierContacts(email: string): Promise<{ id: string; name: string | null }[]>;
  /** How many contacts and confirmations should have been removed more than a day ago: a count only. */
  overdueContacts(): Promise<number>;
}

/**
 * What the transparency module needs from this one (3d design, sections 5 and 7.7): the keeper's daily mail of the audit
 * head. It takes the message and no address: the one address is HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL, which this module holds, and no
 * account and no staff list receives that mail. "off" while the setting is empty; a failure is answered, never thrown.
 */
export interface AuthForTransparency {
  mailKeeper(message: KeeperMessage): Promise<KeeperMailResult>;
}

export interface CreateAuthOptions {
  config: Config;
  logger: Logger;
  /** The korbat_auth pool. The auth module never receives the API pool. */
  authDb: Db;
  mailer: Mailer;
  profiles: ProfileStore;
  /** Either a Redis client or a ready key-value store (tests use an in-memory store). */
  redis?: Redis;
  kv?: KeyValueStore;
  turnstile?: TurnstileVerifier;
  breachChecker?: BreachChecker;
  /**
   * The phone verification provider behind the verified badge. Absent or null, the badge routes answer
   * badge_unavailable; the server passes verificationProviderFrom(config), tests the development provider.
   */
  verify?: VerificationProvider | null;
  now?: () => Date;
}

/**
 * The provider VERIFY_PROVIDER names: none for `off` (the badge is hidden), the fixed-code one for `dev`,
 * Vonage Verify with the configured credentials and brand for `vonage`. `fetchFn` is for tests only.
 */
export function verificationProviderFrom(config: Config, fetchFn?: typeof fetch): VerificationProvider | null {
  switch (config.VERIFY_PROVIDER) {
    case "off":
      return null;
    case "dev":
      return devProvider();
    case "vonage":
      // Production refuses this configuration in config.ts; development gets the same refusal here, at start-up, rather than a failing first request.
      if (!config.VONAGE_API_KEY || !config.VONAGE_API_SECRET) throw new Error("VERIFY_PROVIDER=vonage needs VONAGE_API_KEY and VONAGE_API_SECRET");
      return vonageProvider({ apiKey: config.VONAGE_API_KEY, apiSecret: config.VONAGE_API_SECRET, brand: config.VERIFY_BRAND, fetch: fetchFn });
  }
}

export function createAuth(options: CreateAuthOptions) {
  const kv = options.kv ?? (options.redis ? redisKv(options.redis) : undefined);
  if (!kv) throw new Error("createAuth needs a Redis client or a key-value store");
  const now = options.now ?? (() => new Date());
  const repo = createAuthRepo(options.authDb);
  const sessions = createSessions({ repo, kv, now });
  const deps: AuthDeps = {
    repo,
    kv,
    sessions,
    lockout: createLockout({ repo, kv, now }),
    mailer: options.mailer,
    turnstile: options.turnstile ?? cloudflareTurnstile(options.config.TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY),
    breachChecker: options.breachChecker ?? hibpChecker(),
    profiles: options.profiles,
    verify: options.verify ?? null,
    config: authConfigFrom(options.config),
    log: options.logger,
    now,
  };
  /** A security event about an account, for the modules that own no auth table (the social module's profile and handle changes, the account module's export). */
  const appendEvent = (userId: string, type: AuthEventType, metadata?: Record<string, unknown>) => repo.appendEvent({ userId, type, metadata });
  const forAccount: AuthForAccount = {
    startDeletion: (session, ctx) => startDeletion(deps, session, ctx),
    confirmDeletion: (session, input) => confirmDeletion(deps, session, input),
    pendingPurges: () => repo.pendingPurges(),
    finishPurge: (userId) => finishPurge(deps, userId),
    takeDownTerminated: (userId, facts) => takeDownTerminated(deps, userId, facts),
    exportAccount: (userId) => exportAccount(deps, userId),
    appendEvent,
  };
  // 3d (design, sections 5 and 7.5): the recipients' count, which the transparency module keeps. This module is built
  // first, so the wiring hands it the handler once both exist (onSeen); until then resolveSession counts nothing.
  let seenBy: TransparencyForAuth | null = null;
  const staffGuard = requireStaff(deps);
  const forStaff: AuthForStaff = {
    enrollOptions: (input) => enrollOptions(deps, input),
    enrollVerify: (input, ctx) => enrollVerify(deps, input, ctx),
    signInOptions: () => signInOptions(deps),
    signInVerify: (input, ctx) => signInVerify(deps, input, ctx),
    requireStaff: staffGuard,
    me: (session) => staffMe(deps, session),
    sessions: (session) => listStaffSessions(deps, session),
    keys: (session) => listStaffKeys(deps, session),
    signOut: (session, ctx) => signOutStaff(deps, session, ctx),
    stepUpOptions: (session, request) => stepUpOptions(deps, session, request),
    requireStaffStepUp: (action, target) => requireStaffStepUp(deps, action, target),
    revokeSession: (session, confirmed, ctx) => revokeStaffSession(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
  };
  const forModeration: AuthForModeration = {
    verifyHuman: (token) => deps.turnstile.verify(token),
    storeNotifierContact: (contactId, contact) => storeNotifierContact(deps, contactId, contact),
    mailNotifier: (contactId, message) => mailNotifier(deps, contactId, message),
    mailAccount: (userId, message) => mailAccount(deps, userId, message),
    mailNotifierUpdates: (parts) => mailNotifierUpdates(deps, parts),
    mailStaff: (message) => mailStaff(deps, message),
    notifierFacts: (contactIds) => notifierFacts(deps, contactIds),
    notifierName: (contactId) => notifierName(deps, contactId),
    notifierMailTokenMatches: (contactId, token) => notifierMailTokenMatches(deps, contactId, token),
    confirmNotifier: (contactId, token) => confirmNotifier(deps, contactId, token),
    stopNotifier: (contactId, token) => stopNotifier(deps, contactId, token),
    accountReportMailStopped: (userId) => accountReportMailStopped(deps, userId),
    resumeAccountReportMail: (userId) => resumeAccountReportMail(deps, userId),
    forgetNotifierAfter: (contactIds, at) => forgetNotifierAfter(deps, contactIds, at),
    findNotifierContacts: (email) => findNotifierContacts(deps, email),
    overdueContacts: () => overdueContacts(deps),
  };
  const forTransparency: AuthForTransparency = {
    mailKeeper: (message) => mailKeeper(deps, message),
  };
  return {
    deps,
    routes: authRoutes(deps),
    me: meHandler(deps),
    /** 3e (design, section 7.12): /api/me's answer without the standing, which the app adds from the moderation module. */
    meFor: (session: Session) => me(deps, session),
    appendEvent,
    /** The interface the account module uses. */
    forAccount,
    /** The interface the staff module uses. */
    forStaff,
    /** The interface the moderation module uses. */
    forModeration,
    /** 3d Task 5: the interface the transparency module uses, the keeper's daily mail alone. */
    forTransparency,
    /** Runs first on every request: resolves the client address the way TRUST_PROXY says and hashes it, and its network with it. */
    clientIdentity: clientIdentity({ trust: deps.config.trustProxy, ipHashKey: deps.config.ipHashKey }),
    resolveSession: resolveSession(deps, () => seenBy),
    /** 3d: registers the transparency module's count, which resolveSession calls from then on (index.ts, once both exist). */
    onSeen: (handler: TransparencyForAuth) => {
      seenBy = handler;
    },
    requireSession,
    requireOnboarding,
    requireFreshAuth: (maxAgeSeconds?: number) => requireFreshAuth(deps, maxAgeSeconds),
    /** Level 2 within the window on an account with TOTP, level 1 otherwise: for the routes of the 1c design's section 10. */
    requireStrongFreshAuth: (maxAgeSeconds?: number) => requireStrongFreshAuth(deps, maxAgeSeconds),
    /** A staff session from the staff cookie, read from the database at every request (3a design, section 7). */
    requireStaff: staffGuard,
    /** A fresh confirmation by the staff session's key, bound to the action a route is about to execute (3a design, section 7). */
    requireStaffStepUp: forStaff.requireStaffStepUp,
    /** Starts the retention pass (dead codes, old sessions and staff sessions, spent enrolment links, device address hashes, old events, forgotten notifier contacts and their confirmations) and returns the function that stops it. */
    startJanitor: (lock: JobLock) => createJanitor(deps, lock).start(),
  };
}

export type Auth = ReturnType<typeof createAuth>;
```

```ts
/**
 * The public figures' commands (3d design, sections 7.5, 7.6 and 8.10, "The public figures and the head"), as the
 * migrator in the migrate service:
 *
 *   docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm migrate node dist/staff.js recipients [--months 6]
 *   docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm migrate node dist/staff.js edition <year> [--correct]
 *   docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js head-restore-mark [<day>:<value> ...]
 *
 * recipients prints the figure of DSA Art. 24(2) and (3) exactly, for the authority that asks: the stored months of the
 * full months before today, and their average as two bounds, accounts alone and accounts plus the sum of each day's
 * signed-out readers, or "at least" while signed-out readers were not counted. It reads only.
 *
 * edition prints the newest stored version of a year's edition as its page prints it, a line a figure, and reads only.
 * With --correct it computes every table of the year again, as of the same due day, and stores the result as the next
 * version with the reason correction (edition_publish, which only the migrator may ask for that): the one way a table is
 * computed a second time. The older versions stay, and the transaction ends with the edition's audit row.
 *
 * head-restore-mark (Task 5; sections 6.5, 7.3 step 4 and 7.7 step 7), after a restore: it stores the values the keeper's
 * mails hold for the days the restored database lacks, each as a retired row without a place (the mail's day and value
 * are what the command is given); retires every stored value whose place and hash the restored chain no longer holds,
 * and deletes none; and writes today's public restore row from the restored head, naming the newest published value that
 * still fits. The transaction ends with the system's audit row head_restore_marked.
 *
 * No command here sends anything to anyone. This file has no entry point of its own, so both bundles can include it
 * (build.mjs says why that matters).
 */
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { RECIPIENT_RULES, TRANSPARENCY_RULES, type OrderFigures, type TransparencyFigures } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Db, DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID } from "../auth";
import { appendAuditRow } from "../staff";
import { describeTcoCounts } from "./counts";
import { Refusal, refuse, rows, type OrderDone } from "./orders";

/** The public figures' commands, each with its first lines of STAFF_USAGE. */
export const FIGURE_COMMANDS = ["recipients", "edition", "head-restore-mark"] as const;
export type FigureCommandName = (typeof FIGURE_COMMANDS)[number];

export const FIGURE_USAGE = [
  `${"  recipients [--months 6]".padEnd(41)}print the average monthly active recipients of the full months before today, exactly, for an`,
  `${"".padEnd(41)}authority that asks (DSA Art. 24(3)), a line a month; read-only; run it in the migrate service`,
  `${"  edition <year> [--correct]".padEnd(41)}print the newest stored version of that year's edition, a line a figure; read-only. With`,
  `${"".padEnd(41)}--correct, compute every table again and store it as the next version; run it in the migrate service`,
  `${"  head-restore-mark [<day>:<value> ...]".padEnd(41)}after a restore: store the keeper's values of the days the restored database lacks,`,
  `${"".padEnd(41)}retire every published value that no longer fits, and record the restore; run it in the migrate service`,
];

/** A keeper's value as the command is given it: the day of the mail and the value it holds. */
export interface KeeperValue {
  day: string;
  value: string;
}

export type FigureCommand =
  | { command: "recipients"; months: number }
  | { command: "edition"; year: number; correct: boolean }
  | { command: "head-restore-mark"; values: KeeperValue[] };

/** A calendar year as the operator types it: four digits, never with a leading zero. */
const YEAR = /^[1-9][0-9]{3}$/;
/** How many full months recipients may average: one to five years of them. */
const MONTHS = /^[1-9][0-9]?$/;

/** A keeper's value as the operator types it: the day, a colon and the value's 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters. */
const KEEPER_VALUE = /^([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}):([0-9a-f]{64})$/;
/** Whether a yyyy-mm-dd is a day of the calendar. */
const isDay = (day: string) => !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(`${day}T00:00:00.000Z`)) && new Date(`${day}T00:00:00.000Z`).toISOString().slice(0, 10) === day;

/** Reads a figure command's words. */
export function parseFigureArgs(command: FigureCommandName, rest: readonly string[]): FigureCommand {
  if (command === "head-restore-mark") {
    const usage = "head-restore-mark: takes the keeper's values as <day>:<value>, a day as 2026-10-18 and a value of 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters, each day once, or nothing";
    const values = rest.map((word) => {
      const found = KEEPER_VALUE.exec(word);
      if (found === null || !isDay(found[1]!)) throw new Error(usage);
      return { day: found[1]!, value: found[2]! };
    });
    if (new Set(values.map((entry) => entry.day)).size !== values.length) throw new Error(usage);
    return { command, values };
  }
  if (command === "recipients") {
    if (rest.length === 0) return { command, months: RECIPIENT_RULES.months };
    if (rest.length === 2 && rest[0] === "--months" && MONTHS.test(rest[1]!) && Number(rest[1]) <= 60) return { command, months: Number(rest[1]) };
    throw new Error("recipients: takes nothing, or --months and a number of full months from 1 to 60");
  }
  const [year, ...flags] = rest;
  if (year === undefined || !YEAR.test(year) || flags.length > 1 || (flags.length === 1 && flags[0] !== "--correct")) {
    throw new Error("edition: takes one calendar year of four digits, as 2026, and optionally --correct");
  }
  return { command, year: Number(year), correct: flags.length === 1 };
}

/** The first day of the month `back` months before the instant's own, as yyyy-mm. */
const monthBefore = (at: Date, back: number) => new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), at.getUTCMonth() - back, 1)).toISOString().slice(0, 7);

/** The day a year's edition is due, as the pages print a day. */
const dueDay = (year: number) => new Date(Date.UTC(year + 1, TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueMonth - 1, TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueDay)).toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** One stored month as the command reads it. */
interface MonthRow {
  month: string;
  signed_in: number;
  signed_out_days: number | null;
}

/** What recipients prints of the stored months among the `months` full months before `now` (7.5 step 4). */
export function describeRecipients(stored: readonly MonthRow[], months: number, now: Date): string[] {
  const line = (text: string) => `recipients: ${text}`;
  const wanted = Array.from({ length: months }, (_, at) => monthBefore(now, months - at));
  const byMonth = new Map(stored.map((row) => [row.month, row]));
  const found = wanted.flatMap((month) => (byMonth.has(month) ? [byMonth.get(month)!] : []));
  const lines = [line(`method ${RECIPIENT_RULES.method}; the ${months} full months to ${wanted.at(-1)}.`)];
  for (const month of wanted) {
    const row = byMonth.get(month);
    lines.push(line(row === undefined ? `${month}: not recorded` : `${month}: signed in ${row.signed_in}; signed out, summed by day, ${row.signed_out_days ?? "not counted"}`));
  }
  if (found.length < months) lines.push(line(`only ${found.length} full months are recorded.`));
  if (found.length === 0) return [...lines, line("average monthly active recipients: not recorded.")];
  const average = (values: number[]) => values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0) / values.length;
  const signedIn = average(found.map((row) => row.signed_in));
  const counted = found.every((row) => row.signed_out_days !== null);
  lines.push(
    counted
      ? line(`average monthly active recipients: between ${Math.round(signedIn)} and ${Math.round(signedIn + average(found.map((row) => row.signed_out_days!)))}.`)
      : line(`average monthly active recipients: at least ${Math.round(signedIn)}; signed-out readers are not counted.`),
  );
  return lines;
}

/** The words of a table's labels on the command line: a rule, the law, the kinds and the results as the ledger names them. */
const LABEL_WORDS: Record<string, string> = {
  law: "the law",
  other: "other",
  rules: "reports under the rules",
  illegal: "notices of illegal content",
  finding: "findings by korbat's moderators",
  automated: "findings by a program",
  action: "action taken",
  no_action: "no action again",
};
const labelOf = (label: string) => LABEL_WORDS[label] ?? label;
const REASON_WORDS = { first: "first", hold_ended: "hold ended", correction: "correction" } as const;

/** One stored version as edition prints it: a line a figure, each starting with the command's name. */
export function describeEdition(year: number, version: { version: number; published_on: string; reason: keyof typeof REASON_WORDS; figures: TransparencyFigures }): string[] {
  const line = (text: string) => `edition: ${text}`;
  const f = version.figures;
  const table = (title: string, rowsOf: readonly { label: string; count: string }[]) =>
    rowsOf.length === 0 ? [line(`${title}: none`)] : rowsOf.map((row) => line(`${title}, ${labelOf(row.label)}: ${row.count}`));
  const lines = [
    line(`${year}, version ${version.version} of ${version.published_on}, ${REASON_WORDS[version.reason]}.`),
    ...table("restrictions by ground", f.restrictions.byGround),
    line(`restrictions, all: ${f.restrictions.total}`),
    ...table("restrictions by kind of measure", f.restrictions.byMeasure),
    line(`decisions that found no breach: ${f.noBreach}`),
    ...table("reports and notices received", f.intakes),
    ...table("appeals answered", f.appeals),
    ...table("re-examinations answered", f.reexaminations),
    ...table("measures on accounts", f.accountMeasures),
    ...table("findings by a program", f.automated.findings),
    ...table("measures a program took", f.automated.measures),
    ...(f.automated.r1 ? [line(`of ${f.automated.r1.base} findings by a program under rule R1, a person then restricted ${f.automated.r1.restricted}`)] : []),
    ...(f.uploads ? table("uploads not accepted", f.uploads) : []),
    ...(f.orders ? orderLines(year, f.orders) : []),
    line(
      `recipients: ${
        f.recipients === "not recorded" ? "not recorded" : f.recipients.high === undefined ? `at least ${f.recipients.low}; signed-out readers are not counted` : `between ${f.recipients.low} and ${f.recipients.high}`
      }`,
    ),
  ];
  return lines;
}

/** The order section as tco-counts prints its figures, without the issuing state, which the edition does not hold. */
function orderLines(year: number, orders: OrderFigures): string[] {
  const counts = { year, ...orders, received: orders.received === null ? null : { ...orders.received, byState: [] as [string, number][] } };
  return describeTcoCounts(counts).map((text) => text.replace(/^tco-counts: /, "edition: authorities' orders, "));
}

/** A P0001 code a database function raised, or null. */
function raisedCode(err: unknown): string | null {
  let current: unknown = err;
  for (let depth = 0; depth < 5 && current; depth++) {
    const found = current as { code?: unknown; message?: unknown; cause?: unknown };
    if (found.code === "P0001" && typeof found.message === "string") return found.message;
    current = found.cause;
  }
  return null;
}

type VersionRow = { version: number; published_on: string; reason: keyof typeof REASON_WORDS; figures: TransparencyFigures };

/** The newest stored version of a year, or null. */
async function newestVersion(tx: DbTx, year: number): Promise<VersionRow | null> {
  const [row] = await rows<VersionRow>(
    tx,
    sql`select version, to_char(published_at at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD') as published_on, reason, figures
          from public.transparency_editions where year = ${year} order by version desc limit 1`,
  );
  return row ?? null;
}

/**
 * recipients and edition on the migrator's own connection, with the command line's 10-second lock timeout: the reads in
 * one read-only transaction at one snapshot; the correction in a transaction whose last statement is the edition's audit
 * row, which edition_publish writes. A refusal prints `edition: <code>: ...` and changes nothing.
 */
export async function figureCommand(migrateDb: Db, cmd: FigureCommand, now: Date = new Date()): Promise<OrderDone> {
  try {
    if (cmd.command === "head-restore-mark") return { ok: true, lines: await headRestoreMark(migrateDb, cmd.values) };
    if (cmd.command === "recipients") {
      const from = `${monthBefore(now, cmd.months)}-01`;
      const to = `${monthBefore(now, 0)}-01`;
      const stored = await migrateDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx.execute(sql`set transaction isolation level repeatable read, read only`);
        await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
        return rows<MonthRow>(tx, sql`select to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') as month, signed_in, signed_out_days from public.recipient_months where month >= ${from}::date and month < ${to}::date order by month`);
      });
      return { ok: true, lines: describeRecipients(stored, cmd.months, now) };
    }
    if (!cmd.correct) {
      const newest = await migrateDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx.execute(sql`set transaction isolation level repeatable read, read only`);
        await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
        return newestVersion(tx, cmd.year);
      });
      return { ok: true, lines: newest === null ? [`edition: none stored for ${cmd.year}.`] : describeEdition(cmd.year, newest) };
    }
    await migrateDb
      .transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
        // A correction is stored or refused, never null; its audit row is the transaction's last statement.
        await tx.execute(sql`select public.edition_publish(${cmd.year}::int, 'correction')`);
      })
      .catch((err: unknown) => {
        const code = raisedCode(err);
        if (code === "edition_not_due") throw new Refusal(`edition: edition_not_due: the edition of ${cmd.year} is due on ${dueDay(cmd.year)}; nothing changed`);
        if (code === "invalid_edition") return refuse("edition", `invalid_edition: no edition of ${cmd.year} is stored yet; the job publishes its first version on or after ${dueDay(cmd.year)}`);
        throw err;
      });
    // The version just stored is the year's newest.
    const stored = await migrateDb.transaction((tx) => newestVersion(tx, cmd.year));
    return {
      ok: true,
      lines: [`edition: ${cmd.year}, version ${stored!.version} stored, every table computed again. The page lists version ${stored!.version - 1} as replaced on ${stored!.published_on}.`],
    };
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof Refusal) return { ok: false, problem: err.message };
    throw err;
  }
}

/**
 * head-restore-mark (3d design, sections 6.5, 7.3 step 4 and 7.7 step 7), in one transaction as the migrator, whose
 * inserts and updates the head's two triggers leave as written. Every refusal comes before the first write: one restore
 * a day (the restore row's key is the day), no keeper's day after today, and no keeper's value that differs from the one
 * the restored database holds for that day. Then:
 *
 *   1. each keeper's value of a day the database lacks is stored as that day's head row, published and retired at once,
 *      with no place (the mail's place is not asked for: no check needs it, and a value of a day after the backup fits
 *      no restored log anyway); a value the database holds already is counted and left;
 *   2. every stored value, of either kind, whose place and hash the restored chain no longer holds is retired, never
 *      deleted: a place above the restored head, or a place whose hash does not give the value;
 *   3. today's restore row from the restored head, published, naming the newest published head value that still fits,
 *      or none (last_day, which the page prints as [tr.restore]'s day);
 *   4. last, the system's audit row head_restore_marked with the day and the count of values retired.
 */
async function headRestoreMark(migrateDb: Db, values: readonly KeeperValue[]): Promise<string[]> {
  const c = "head-restore-mark";
  return migrateDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
    await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
    const [state] = await rows<{ today: string; seq: number; hash: string }>(
      tx,
      sql`select to_char((now() at time zone 'UTC')::date, 'YYYY-MM-DD') as today, a.seq::int as seq, a.hash from public.audit_head a where a.id = 1`,
    );
    const { today, seq, hash } = state!;
    const [marked] = await rows<{ one: number }>(tx, sql`select 1 as one from public.head_publications where kind = 'restore' and day = ${today}::date`);
    if (marked !== undefined) refuse(c, `restore_marked: a restore is recorded for ${today} already`);
    const held: string[] = [];
    for (const { day, value } of values) {
      if (day > today) refuse(c, `invalid_day: ${day} is after today`);
      const [row] = await rows<{ value: string }>(tx, sql`select value from public.head_publications where kind = 'head' and day = ${day}::date`);
      if (row !== undefined && row.value !== value) refuse(c, `head_mismatch: the value of ${day} differs from the one the database holds`);
      if (row !== undefined) held.push(day);
    }
    let stored = 0;
    for (const { day, value } of values) {
      if (held.includes(day)) continue;
      await tx.execute(sql`
        insert into public.head_publications (day, kind, chain_seq, value, witness, published_at, retired_at)
        values (${day}::date, 'head', null, ${value}, 'none', now(), now())`);
      stored++;
    }
    // A value fits while the restored chain holds its place with a hash that gives it: at the head itself, or at a row of
    // the log. A place above the restored head has neither.
    const retired = await tx.execute(sql`
      update public.head_publications h set retired_at = now()
       where h.retired_at is null and h.chain_seq is not null
         and not exists (
           select 1 from public.audit_head a where a.id = 1 and a.seq = h.chain_seq and public.head_value(h.day, a.seq, a.hash) = h.value
           union all
           select 1 from public.audit_log l where l.chain_seq = h.chain_seq and public.head_value(h.day, l.chain_seq, l.hash) = h.value)
      returning 1`);
    const [last] = await rows<{ day: string | null }>(
      tx,
      sql`select to_char(max(h.day), 'YYYY-MM-DD') as day from public.head_publications h where h.kind = 'head' and h.published_at is not null and h.retired_at is null`,
    );
    const lastDay = last?.day ?? null;
    await tx.execute(sql`
      insert into public.head_publications (day, kind, chain_seq, value, witness, published_at, last_day)
      values (${today}::date, 'restore', ${seq}, public.head_value(${today}::date, ${seq}::bigint, ${hash}), 'none', now(), ${lastDay}::date)`);
    const count = stored + retired.length;
    await appendAuditRow(tx, { actorId: SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, action: "head_restore_marked", targetType: null, targetId: null, requestId: null, metadata: { day: today, retired: count } });
    return [
      ...(values.length > 0 ? [`${c}: ${stored} values of the keeper's mails stored, retired; ${held.length} already held.`] : []),
      `${c}: restore recorded for ${today}. ${lastDay === null ? "No published value still verifies." : `The last published value that still verifies is of ${lastDay}.`} ${count} later values are shown as retired.`,
    ];
  });
}
```

```ts
import { Email, STAFF_STEP_UP_ACTIONS, STAFF_STEP_UP_CHALLENGE, StaffStoredAssertion, stepUpActionHash, stepUpBindingText } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { auditHead, auditLog, authEvents, closeDb, createDb, profiles, staffEnrollments, staffKeys, users, type Db, type DbTx } from "@korbat/db";

import { consoleHostOf, consoleOriginSetting, consoleRpIdSetting, databaseUrl, loadConfig, mailFrom, smtpUrl } from "../config";

  ...RESTORE_USAGE,
  // 3f Task 7 (design, sections 7.18 and 8.11): the yearly counts, read-only, as the migrator in the migrate service.

/** A place in the chain and the hash it had when someone kept it, as audit-head printed it. */
export interface KeptPlace {
  seq: number;
  hash: string;
}

export type StaffCommand =
  | { command: "enroll"; email: string }
  | { command: "keys"; email: string | null }
  | { command: "audit-head" }
  | { command: "audit-verify"; kept: KeptPlace[] }
  | { command: "revoke"; email: string; key: string | "all" }
  | { command: "text-verify" }
  | { command: "access-request"; who: { handle: string } | { email: string } }

  | { command: "unlink"; email: string; handle: string }

  | { command: "record"; record: RecordCommand }
```
