```ts
import { Hono } from "hono";
import type { PublicFacts } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Config } from "../config";
import type { AppEnv } from "../env";
import { publicTransparency } from "./editions";
import { publicHead } from "./head";
import type { TransparencyRepo } from "./repo";

/**
 * The public answers (3d design, sections 9.1 and 10.6), mounted at /api after the global rate limit and before the
 * session's resolution (app.ts), as the page status is: neither reads a session, a cookie or a table of a person.
 *
 *   GET /api/public/facts         what is switched on now, read from memory, Cache-Control: no-cache, so /rules prints
 *                                 what runs now, also in the minute after a restart;
 *   GET /api/public/transparency  every year's editions from transparency_editions, Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600:
 *                                 nothing in it changes within a day;
 *   GET /api/public/head          the audit head's published values of the last HEAD_RULES.shownDays days (Task 5), public
 *                                 for an hour too: a day gains its value once, after the dispatch hour, and never the place.
 */

/**
 * The facts of the running server (10.6): booleans, names, days and numbers, never a token, a zone, a host or an address.
 * The R1 check and the comparison with known material are built by later tasks and print off until then; the edge
 * prints its adapter (Task 3), and the head's witness its own (Task 5), never its authority's address. A test adapter
 * prints "on" and says it is one.
 */
export function publicFacts(config: Pick<Config, "EDGE_PURGE" | "RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT" | "HEAD_WITNESS">): PublicFacts {
  return {
    r1: { state: "off", test: false, model: null, digest: null, threshold: null, thresholdVersion: null, publisherClaim: null, dpia: null, dpiaActs: null },
    match: { state: "off", test: false, source: null, dpia: null, dpiaActs: null },
    edge: { on: config.EDGE_PURGE !== "off", test: config.EDGE_PURGE === "test" },
    witness: { on: config.HEAD_WITNESS !== "off", test: config.HEAD_WITNESS === "test" },
    recipientsSignedOut: config.RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT === "on",
  };
}

export function transparencyRoutes(deps: { repo: Pick<TransparencyRepo, "editions" | "headDays">; facts: PublicFacts }) {
  const r = new Hono<AppEnv>();
  r.get("/public/facts", (c) => {
    c.header("Cache-Control", "no-cache");
    return c.json(deps.facts);
  });
  r.get("/public/transparency", async (c) => {
    const answer = publicTransparency(await deps.repo.editions());
    c.header("Cache-Control", "public, max-age=3600");
    return c.json(answer);
  });
  r.get("/public/head", async (c) => {
    const answer = publicHead(await deps.repo.headDays());
    c.header("Cache-Control", "public, max-age=3600");
    return c.json(answer);
  });
  return r;
}
```

```tsx
import { ANNEX3_GROUNDS, ORDER_GROUNDS, PublicHead, PublicTransparency, type OrderFigures, type TransparencyFigures } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { AppShell } from "@/components/AppShell";
import { TextLink } from "@/components/ui";
import { api } from "@/lib/api";
import { saveBlob } from "@/lib/download";
import { PAGE_DOWN, TRANSPARENCY_PAGE, recipientsMonth } from "@/lib/public-pages";

const T = TRANSPARENCY_PAGE;
type Edition = PublicTransparency["editions"][number];
type Row = { label: string; count: string };

/** A heading of the page: level 2 a year or a fixed section, level 3 a table inside a year. */
function Heading({ level, children }: { level: 2 | 3; children: string }) {
  return (
    <Text accessibilityRole="header" aria-level={level} className={level === 2 ? "mt-8 text-lg font-semibold text-zinc-100" : "mt-5 text-base font-semibold text-zinc-100"}>
      {children}
    </Text>
  );
}
const Paragraph = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => <Text className="mt-2 text-base leading-7 text-zinc-300">{children}</Text>;

/**
 * One table: its heading and its rows, each read as "label: value" and laid out as a block, never a chart (9.1); a table
 * with no row is its "none" sentence.
 */
function Table({ title, rows }: { title: string; rows: Row[] }) {
  return (
    <View>
      <Heading level={3}>{title}</Heading>
      {rows.length === 0 ? (
        <Paragraph>{T.tableNone}</Paragraph>
      ) : (
        <View role="list" aria-label={title}>
          {rows.map((row) => (
            <Text key={row.label} role="listitem" className="mt-1 text-base leading-6 text-zinc-300">
              {`${row.label}: ${row.count}`}
            </Text>
          ))}
        </View>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}

/** A table's stored rows with the page's labels: `other` by the table's own word. */
const labelled = (rows: readonly { label: string; count: string }[], label: (key: string) => string, other: string): Row[] =>
  rows.map((row) => ({ label: row.label === "other" ? other : label(row.label), count: row.count }));

/** An order figure as the page prints it: a number, or "not recorded", never 0, for a figure the rows can no longer give. */
const figure = (n: number | null) => (n === null ? T.notRecorded : String(n));
const byGround = (grounds: readonly string[], counts: Record<string, number> | null) =>
  counts === null ? T.notRecorded : grounds.map((ground) => `${T.grounds[ground] ?? ground} ${counts[ground]}`).join(", ");

/**
 * The section on authorities' orders (9.3 item 4): [tr.orders], then the yearly report's headings with tco-counts'
 * figures as numbers, without the issuing state. It stands only in a year that has the section.
 */
function OrdersSection({ orders }: { orders: OrderFigures }) {
  const L = T.orderLines;
  const minutes = orders.minutes;
  const minutesList = minutes === null ? T.notRecorded : minutes.list.length === 0 ? "none" : minutes.list.map((n) => figure(n)).join(", ");
  return (
    <View>
      <Heading level={3}>{T.ordersHeading}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>{T.orders}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.received}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{orders.received === null ? L.received(T.notRecorded, T.notRecorded) : L.received(String(orders.received.total), String(orders.received.crossBorder))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.disabled}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.itemsDisabled(figure(orders.itemsDisabled))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.minutes(minutesList)}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.late}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.outside(minutes === null || minutes.withoutReceipt > 0 ? T.notRecorded : String(minutes.outside))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.open(minutes === null ? T.notRecorded : String(minutes.open))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.annex3(byGround(ANNEX3_GROUNDS, orders.annex3))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.scrutiny}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{orders.scrutiny === null ? L.scrutiny(T.notRecorded, T.notRecorded, T.notRecorded) : L.scrutiny(String(orders.scrutiny.requested), String(orders.scrutiny.annulled), String(orders.scrutiny.upheld))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.reinstated(byGround(ORDER_GROUNDS, orders.reinstated))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.own}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.terrorist(String(orders.terroristWithoutOrder))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.access(figure(orders.authorityAccess))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.referrals(String(orders.referralsClosed))}</Paragraph>
    </View>
  );
}

/** The tables of one version's figures, in W.2's order, then the order section, the standing sentence and the recipients. */
export function FiguresView({ year, figures }: { year: number; figures: TransparencyFigures }) {
  const r = figures.restrictions;
  const findings = labelled(figures.automated.findings, T.labels.findings, T.labels.other);
  const programs = [...findings, ...labelled(figures.automated.measures, T.labels.measures, T.labels.other)];
  const month = recipientsMonth(year);
  const recipients = figures.recipients;
  return (
    <View>
      <Table
        title={T.tables.byGround}
        rows={r.byGround.length === 0 ? [] : [...labelled(r.byGround, (key) => (key === "law" ? T.labels.law : T.labels.ground(key)), T.labels.otherGrounds), { label: T.labels.allRestrictions, count: r.total }]}
      />
      <Table title={T.tables.byMeasure} rows={labelled(r.byMeasure, T.labels.measure, T.labels.otherMeasures)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.noBreach} rows={[{ label: T.labels.noBreach, count: figures.noBreach }]} />
      <Table title={T.tables.intakes} rows={labelled(figures.intakes, (key) => T.labels.intakes[key] ?? key, T.labels.other)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.appeals} rows={labelled(figures.appeals, (key) => T.labels.appeals[key] ?? key, T.labels.other)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.reexaminations} rows={labelled(figures.reexaminations, (key) => T.labels.reexaminations[key] ?? key, T.labels.other)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.accountMeasures} rows={labelled(figures.accountMeasures, T.labels.measure, T.labels.otherMeasures)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.automated} rows={programs} />
      {figures.automated.r1 ? <Paragraph>{T.autoRate(figures.automated.r1.base, figures.automated.r1.restricted)}</Paragraph> : findings.length > 0 ? <Paragraph>{T.autoFew}</Paragraph> : null}
      {figures.uploads ? <Table title={T.tables.uploads} rows={labelled(figures.uploads, (key) => T.labels.uploads[key] ?? key, T.labels.other)} /> : null}
      {figures.orders ? <OrdersSection orders={figures.orders} /> : null}
      <Paragraph>{T.ordersHeld}</Paragraph>
      <Heading level={3}>{T.recipientsHeading}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>
        {recipients === "not recorded" ? T.recipientsNotYet : recipients.high === undefined ? T.recipientsOff(month, recipients.low) : T.recipients(month, recipients.low, recipients.high)}
      </Paragraph>
    </View>
  );
}

/** An older version of a year: its line, and its figures opened in place. */
function OlderVersion({ year, older }: { year: number; older: Edition["older"][number] }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <View>
      <Paragraph>{T.versionLine(older.version, older.publishedOn, older.replacedOn)}</Paragraph>
      <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" onPress={() => setOpen(!open)} className="mt-1 self-start">
        <Text className="text-sm text-sky-400 underline">{open ? T.hideVersion : T.showVersion}</Text>
      </Pressable>
      {open ? <FiguresView year={year} figures={older.figures} /> : null}
    </View>
  );
}

/** One year's section (9.3 item 2): its newest version, why that version was made, and its older versions. */
function EditionView({ edition, newest }: { edition: Edition; newest: boolean }) {
  return (
    <View>
      <Heading level={2}>{String(edition.year)}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>{T.edition(edition.year, edition.version, edition.publishedOn, edition.method)}</Paragraph>
      {edition.reason === "hold_ended" ? <Paragraph>{T.reason.hold_ended}</Paragraph> : null}
      {edition.reason === "correction" ? <Paragraph>{T.reason.correction(edition.publishedOn)}</Paragraph> : null}
      <FiguresView year={edition.year} figures={edition.figures} />
      {edition.older.length > 0 ? (
        <View>
          <Paragraph>{T.versions}</Paragraph>
          {edition.older.map((older) => (
            <OlderVersion key={older.version} year={edition.year} older={older} />
          ))}
        </View>
      ) : null}
      {newest ? <Paragraph>{T.method(edition.method)}</Paragraph> : null}
    </View>
  );
}

type HeadDay = PublicHead["days"][number];

/** A day before another, as the page prints a day. */
const dayBefore = (day: string) => new Date(Date.parse(`${day}T00:00:00.000Z`) - 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** One line of the head's section: a published row, or a day between two shown days that has no head value. */
type HeadLine = { kind: "row"; row: HeadDay } | { kind: "missing"; day: string };

/**
 * The section's lines (9.3 item 6): the rows newest first as the route gives them, and [tr.headMissing] for each day
 * between the newest and the oldest shown day that has no head value, after that day's restore row when it has one. A
 * day after the newest row is not shown as missing: its value may not be published yet.
 */
export function headLines(days: readonly HeadDay[]): HeadLine[] {
  const lines: HeadLine[] = [];
  const valued = new Set(days.filter((row) => row.kind === "head").map((row) => row.day));
  const newest = days[0]?.day;
  const oldest = days.at(-1)?.day;
  if (newest === undefined || oldest === undefined) return lines;
  for (let day = newest; day >= oldest; day = dayBefore(day)) {
    for (const row of days) if (row.day === day) lines.push({ kind: "row", row });
    if (!valued.has(day)) lines.push({ kind: "missing", day });
  }
  return lines;
}

/** A day's proof saved as <day>.tsr: the token as the authority sent it, the TimeStampResp that openssl reads. */
function saveProof(day: string, token: string) {
  const bytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(token), (char) => char.charCodeAt(0));
  saveBlob(new Blob([bytes], { type: "application/timestamp-reply" }), `${day}.tsr`);
}

/**
 * Section 6, the audit log's daily value (3d design, section 9.3 item 6; W.2; Task 5): [tr.head], then a row a day,
 * newest first, with its value and who witnessed it, a restore's row with [tr.restore], a retired value with
 * [tr.retired] and a day without a value with [tr.headMissing]; while a shown row has a proof, [tr.verify] with the newest
 * such day's value and file, and each day's proof to download on the web. When the route did not answer, this part alone
 * reads [page.down]. The place is in no answer and on no row.
 */
function HeadSection({ head }: { head: PublicHead | "loading" | "down" }) {
  const T = TRANSPARENCY_PAGE;
  const witnessed = head === "loading" || head === "down" ? undefined : head.days.find((row) => row.token !== null);
  return (
    <View>
      <Heading level={2}>{T.headHeading}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>{T.head}</Paragraph>
      {head === "loading" ? null : head === "down" ? (
        <Paragraph>{PAGE_DOWN}</Paragraph>
      ) : head.days.length === 0 ? (
        <Paragraph>{T.headNone}</Paragraph>
      ) : (
        <View role="list" aria-label={T.headHeading}>
          {headLines(head.days).map((line) =>
            line.kind === "missing" ? (
              <Text key={`${line.day}-missing`} role="listitem" className="mt-1 text-base leading-6 text-zinc-300">
                {T.headMissingRow(line.day)}
              </Text>
            ) : (
              <View key={`${line.row.day}-${line.row.kind}`} role="listitem" className="mt-1">
                <Text className="break-all text-base leading-6 text-zinc-300">
                  {line.row.kind === "restore"
                    ? T.restore(line.row.day, line.row.lastDay)
                    : line.row.retiredOn === null
                      ? T.headRow(line.row.day, line.row.value, line.row.witness)
                      : `${T.headRow(line.row.day, line.row.value, line.row.witness)} ${T.retired(line.row.retiredOn)}`}
                </Text>
                {line.row.token !== null && Platform.OS === "web" ? (
                  <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" onPress={() => saveProof(line.row.day, line.row.token!)} className="mt-1 self-start">
                    <Text className="text-sm text-sky-400 underline">{T.download(line.row.day)}</Text>
                  </Pressable>
                ) : null}
              </View>
            ),
          )}
        </View>
      )}
      {witnessed ? <Paragraph>{T.verify(witnessed.value, witnessed.day)}</Paragraph> : null}
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * The transparency page as it reads with the editions and the head's values it was given (3d design, section 9.3; W.2).
 * It shows what the stored editions hold and never a live count: no year section for the running year, and [tr.none]
 * while no edition exists. When a route did not answer, the fixed texts stand and that route's part alone reads
 * [page.down].
 */
export function TransparencyView({ answer, head = "loading" }: { answer: PublicTransparency | "loading" | "down"; head?: PublicHead | "loading" | "down" }) {
  return (
    <View>
      <Text accessibilityRole="header" className="text-3xl font-bold tracking-tight text-zinc-50">
        {T.title}
      </Text>
      <Paragraph>{T.lead}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.read}</Paragraph>
      {answer === "loading" ? null : answer === "down" ? (
        <Paragraph>{PAGE_DOWN}</Paragraph>
      ) : answer.editions.length === 0 ? (
        <Paragraph>{T.none}</Paragraph>
      ) : (
        answer.editions.map((edition, index) => <EditionView key={edition.year} edition={edition} newest={index === 0} />)
      )}
      <HeadSection head={head} />
      <Heading level={2}>{T.tdbHeading}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>{T.tdb}</Paragraph>
      <TextLink label={T.rulesLink} href="/rules" />
      <TextLink label={T.exploreLink} href="/explore/about" />
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * /transparency (3d design, sections 9.1 and 9.3), public, signed in or out: it reads no session for its content and
 * sends two GETs, /api/public/transparency and (Task 5) /api/public/head, each of which may be an hour old: nothing in
 * them changes within a day. Each fails alone: the other part still shows.
 */
export default function TransparencyPage() {
  const [answer, setAnswer] = useState<PublicTransparency | "loading" | "down">("loading");
  const [head, setHead] = useState<PublicHead | "loading" | "down">("loading");
  useEffect(() => {
    let live = true;
    api("/api/public/transparency", { schema: PublicTransparency })
      .then((read) => {
        if (live) setAnswer(read);
      })
      .catch(() => {
        if (live) setAnswer("down");
      });
    api("/api/public/head", { schema: PublicHead })
      .then((read) => {
        if (live) setHead(read);
      })
      .catch(() => {
        if (live) setHead("down");
      });
    return () => {
      live = false;
    };
  }, []);
  return (
    <AppShell>
      <ScrollView className="flex-1 bg-zinc-950" contentContainerClassName="px-4 pb-16 pt-6">
        <View className="w-full max-w-xl">
          <TransparencyView answer={answer} head={head} />
        </View>
      </ScrollView>
    </AppShell>
  );
}
```

```ts
/** What the facts route says of the R1 check's model, printed under its text while it is on. */
type R1Facts = Pick<PublicFacts["r1"], "model" | "digest" | "threshold" | "thresholdVersion" | "publisherClaim">;

/** "(test adapter)" after a tool's "on": a test adapter can run only while the app's site is closed (W.1). */
const testAdapter = (text: string) => text.replace(": on", ": on (test adapter)");

/** One tool's block on the rules page, as the facts give it: its paragraphs, in order. */
export interface ToolBlock {
  tool: "r1" | "match" | "edge" | "witness";
  on: boolean;
  paragraphs: string[];
}

/**
 * The automation section's four blocks, in the state the facts route gives each tool (9.2 item 4): a tool's text, its
 * model's facts while the R1 check is on, and inside the block of each of the two tools that rate or compare images,
 * while it is on, its own impact assessment's day and, while its measure is on, the day of the one that covers it. A date
 * is never printed over a tool it was not set for.
 */
export function toolBlocks(facts: PublicFacts): ToolBlock[] {
  const dates = (tool: { dpia: string | null; dpiaActs: string | null }, acts: boolean) => [
    ...(tool.dpia === null ? [] : [RULES_PAGE.dpia(tool.dpia)]),
    ...(acts && tool.dpiaActs !== null ? [RULES_PAGE.dpiaActs(tool.dpiaActs)] : []),
  ];
  const marked = (text: string, test: boolean) => (test ? testAdapter(text) : text);
  const { r1, match, edge, witness } = facts;
  const r1On = r1.state !== "off";
  const matchOn = match.state !== "off";
  const source = match.source ?? "its source";
  return [
    {
      tool: "r1",
      on: r1On,
      paragraphs: r1On
        ? [marked(TOOL_TEXTS.r1[r1.state === "withholds" ? "withholds" : "flags"], r1.test), ...(r1.model === null ? [] : [TOOL_TEXTS.r1.facts(r1)]), ...dates(r1, r1.state === "withholds")]
        : [TOOL_TEXTS.r1.off],
    },
    {
      tool: "match",
      on: matchOn,
      paragraphs: matchOn ? [marked(match.state === "seals" ? TOOL_TEXTS.match.seals(source) : TOOL_TEXTS.match.alerts(source), match.test), ...dates(match, match.state === "seals")] : [TOOL_TEXTS.match.off],
    },
    { tool: "edge", on: edge.on, paragraphs: [edge.on ? marked(TOOL_TEXTS.edge.on, edge.test) : TOOL_TEXTS.edge.off] },
    { tool: "witness", on: witness.on, paragraphs: [witness.on ? marked(TOOL_TEXTS.witness.on, witness.test) : TOOL_TEXTS.witness.off] },
  ];
}

/** The six full months before an edition's due day end with this month (yyyy-mm), the same in every version of the year. */
export function recipientsMonth(year: number): string {
  return new Date(Date.UTC(year + 1, TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueMonth - 1, 0)).toISOString().slice(0, 7);
}

const MONTHS = ["January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October", "November", "December"];
/** The day a year's edition is due, as a sentence names it: 1 March, from TRANSPARENCY_RULES. */
const DUE = `${TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueDay} ${MONTHS[TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueMonth - 1]}`;
/** The floor and the rounding of a banded count, as a sentence names them. */
const FLOOR = numberWord(TRANSPARENCY_RULES.floor);
const UNDER_FLOOR = `1 to ${TRANSPARENCY_RULES.floor - 1}`;
const ROUND_TO = numberWord(TRANSPARENCY_RULES.roundTo);

/** Who witnessed a day's value, as its row says it. */
const HEAD_WITNESS_WORDS: Record<HeadWitness, string> = {
  rfc3161: "with an outside timestamp",
  test: "with a test adapter's timestamp, which proves nothing",
  none: "without an outside timestamp",
};

/** The labels of a measure in the tables: the ledger's own. */
const measureLabel = (kind: string) => (kind in MEASURES ? MEASURES[kind as MeasureKind].label : kind);
/** A rule's title in force, for the table by ground. */
const ruleTitle = (id: string) => RULES.find((rule) => rule.id === id)?.title ?? id;

/** The transparency page's words (W.2). */
export const TRANSPARENCY_PAGE = {
  title: "Transparency",
  lead: "What korbat's moderators, its programs and authorities' orders did, in numbers. korbat publishes counts and never a decision: on a service this small, a list of decisions would point at people. Whoever a decision concerns gets its full reasons from korbat directly.",
  read: `How to read a figure. korbat prints 0, "${UNDER_FLOOR}", or a number rounded to the nearest ${ROUND_TO} ("about 60"). A line that would show fewer than ${FLOOR} is folded into "other". Each figure is rounded by itself, so the lines of a table need not add up to its total. The one exception is the section on authorities' orders: the law asks for those figures as numbers, so they are printed as numbers, small ones too. korbat publishes one edition for each calendar year, on or after ${DUE} of the next year, and never changes it: a correction is a new version beside it, marked and dated. The running year shows no figure, so nothing on this page moves when korbat takes one decision.`,
  edition: (year: number, version: number, publishedOn: string, method: number) =>
    `Edition ${year}, version ${version}, published ${publishedOn}. It counts what was decided, received or answered from 1 January to 31 December ${year}, UTC. Method ${method}.`,
  versions: "Earlier versions of this year, kept as they were published:",
  versionLine: (version: number, publishedOn: string, replacedOn: string) => `Version ${version}, published ${publishedOn}, replaced on ${replacedOn}.`,
  showVersion: "Show this version",
  hideVersion: "Hide this version",
  reason: {
    hold_ended: "This version adds an order that an authority's decision forbade korbat to disclose until now. Every other figure is the one first published: nothing else was counted again.",
    correction: (publishedOn: string) => `This version corrects the version before it. Every table of the year was counted again on ${publishedOn}, so a figure can differ for a reason other than the corrected one.`,
  },
  none: `korbat has published no edition yet. The first appears on or after ${DUE} of the year after korbat's first calendar year.`,
  /** A table with no row. */
  tableNone: "None in this year.",
  tables: {
    byGround: "Restrictions, by ground",
    byMeasure: "Restrictions, by kind of measure",
    noBreach: "Decisions that found no breach",
    intakes: "Reports and notices received",
    appeals: "Appeals answered in the year",
    reexaminations: "Re-examinations answered in the year",
    accountMeasures: "Measures on accounts",
    automated: "Programs",
    uploads: "Uploads not accepted",
  },
  labels: {
    ground: (id: string) => `Rule ${id}: ${ruleTitle(id)}`,
    law: "The law",
    otherGrounds: "Other grounds",
    allRestrictions: "All restrictions",
    measure: measureLabel,
    otherMeasures: "Other measures",
    other: "Other",
    noBreach: "Decisions that found no breach",
    intakes: {
      rules: "Reports under korbat's rules",
      illegal: "Notices of illegal content (Article 16 of the Digital Services Act)",
      finding: "Findings by korbat's moderators",
      automated: "Findings by a program",
    } as Record<string, string>,
    appeals: { kept: "Decision kept", partly_reversed: "Reversed in part", reversed: "Reversed" } as Record<string, string>,
    reexaminations: { action: "Action taken", no_action: "No action again" } as Record<string, string>,
    findings: (id: string) => `Findings by a program under rule ${id}`,
    measures: (id: string) => `Measures a program took under rule ${id}`,
    uploads: { refused: "Uploads refused on a match", report: "Held for a report", no_report: "Hold ended without a report" } as Record<string, string>,
  },
  autoRate: (base: string, restricted: string) => `Of ${base} findings by a program under rule R1, a person then restricted ${restricted}.`,
  autoFew: "Too few findings to say what became of them.",
  ordersHeading: "Authorities' orders",
  orders:
    "An order is not korbat's decision: korbat gives no reasons of its own for it, publishes no statement of reasons for it, and counts it in none of the tables above. These are the figures that Article 7 of Regulation (EU) 2021/784 asks for, as numbers.",
  /** The headings of the yearly report of authorities' orders (the 3f design's runbook), without the issuing state. */
  orderHeadings: {
    received: "Removal orders received",
    disabled: "Items disabled, and how fast",
    late: "Orders not carried out in time, with the ground",
    scrutiny: "Scrutiny and reinstatements",
    own: "The measures korbat takes against terrorist content",
  },
  orderLines: {
    received: (total: string, crossBorder: string) => `Removal orders received: ${total}, of which from another Member State: ${crossBorder}.`,
    itemsDisabled: (n: string) => `Items disabled following a removal order: ${n}.`,
    minutes: (list: string) => `Minutes from the clock's start to the disabling of an order's last item: ${list}.`,
    outside: (n: string) => `Orders whose last item was disabled outside the hour: ${n}.`,
    open: (n: string) => `Orders with an item still open: ${n}.`,
    annex3: (list: string) => `Annex III sent, by ground: ${list}.`,
    scrutiny: (requested: string, annulled: string, upheld: string) => `Scrutiny requested: ${requested}; annulled: ${annulled}; upheld: ${upheld}.`,
    reinstated: (list: string) => `Reinstated, by ground: ${list}.`,
    access: (n: string) => `Access to preserved content by an authority: ${n}.`,
    terrorist: (n: string) => `Restricted by korbat as terrorist content without an order (notices and its own findings; no automated tool): ${n}.`,
    referrals: (n: string) => `Messages at the contact point closed as a referral: ${n}.`,
  },
  /** Grounds as the page prints them. */
  grounds: {
    force_majeure: "force majeure",
    manifest_error: "manifest error",
    insufficient_information: "insufficient information",
    withdrawn: "withdrawn",
    annulled: "annulled",
    scrutiny: "after scrutiny",
    not_authentic: "not authentic",
    wrong_item: "wrong item",
  } as Record<string, string>,
  /** A figure the rows can no longer give, as tco-counts prints it: never 0. */
  notRecorded: "not recorded",
  ordersHeld: "Orders that an authority's decision forbids korbat to disclose are counted after that decision ends. A year can gain a second, marked version for that reason.",
  recipientsHeading: "Recipients",
  recipients: (month: string, low: string, high: string) =>
    `Average monthly active recipients of korbat (Article 24(2) of the Digital Services Act), over the six months to ${month}: between ${low} and ${high}.`,
  recipientsOff: (month: string, low: string) =>
    `Average monthly active recipients of korbat (Article 24(2) of the Digital Services Act), over the six months to ${month}: at least ${low}; korbat does not count readers without an account.`,
  recipientsNotYet: "korbat has not counted six full months yet.",
  method: (method: number) =>
    `How korbat counts (method ${method}). An account that was used while signed in during a month is counted once for that month. A reader without an account is counted once for each day they read korbat: korbat cannot tell whether Tuesday's reader is Monday's, because it keeps nothing that could tell. So the true number lies between the first figure, accounts alone, and the second, accounts plus the sum of each day's readers. To count, korbat feeds a counting sketch: a small summary that cannot list who was counted. For a reader without an account it is fed with a keyed digest of the network address and the browser's name, under a random key that exists for ${RECIPIENT_RULES.saltHours} hours in korbat's short-lived store and is written nowhere else. Until a month's sketch is deleted at the month's end, whoever runs korbat's server could still ask it whether one given account was probably counted in that month; after that korbat keeps two numbers and nothing else. A crawler is left out only when it names itself. korbat does not record where a reader is, so readers outside the European Union are counted too.`,
  // The audit log's daily value (3d Task 5; 9.3 item 6, W.2).
  headHeading: "The audit log's daily value",
  head: "Each day korbat publishes one value computed from the day and the newest entry of its staff audit log, the record of everything korbat's staff confirm with their keys. If an earlier entry were changed or removed later, the log would no longer lead to the values published since. A value shows neither how many entries the log has nor any entry, and it differs from one day to the next also when nothing was added to the log. A value on korbat's own page proves nothing against korbat's operator, who could change this page too: so the same value goes each day to a person who does not run the server, and, when the outside timestamp is on, to a timestamp authority.",
  /** A day's row: its value, and who witnessed it ("witness" reads none for a row without a token). */
  headRow: (day: string, value: string, witness: HeadWitness) => `${day}: ${value}, ${HEAD_WITNESS_WORDS[witness]}`,
  /** [tr.headMissing], in the row of a day between two shown days that has no value. */
  headMissingRow: (day: string) => `${day}: no value was published`,
  /** [tr.restore], a restore's row; the second sentence names the newest value above it that still fits, or says none does. */
  restore: (day: string, lastDay: string | null) =>
    `${day}: korbat restored its database from a backup. ${lastDay === null ? "No value above still fits the restored log." : `The newest value above that still fits the restored log is of ${lastDay}.`}`,
  /** [tr.retired], after a retired value. */
  retired: (day: string) => `retired by the restore of ${day}: true when published, and fits no log now`,
  /**
   * [tr.verify], while a shown row has a proof, with the newest such day's value and file: the command as it was run once
   * against a proof of a local test authority (OpenSSL 3.5.4), where it answered "Verification: OK" for the value and
   * failed for another value and for another authority's certificates.
   */
  verify: (value: string, day: string) =>
    `To check a day: download its proof, get the timestamp authority's certificates from the authority itself, and run: openssl ts -verify -digest ${value} -in ${day}.tsr -CAfile <certificates>. It answers "Verification: OK" when that authority signed this value at the time the proof states.`,
  download: (day: string) => `Download the proof of ${day} (${day}.tsr)`,
  headNone: "korbat has published no daily value yet.",
  tdbHeading: "The Transparency Database",
  tdb: "korbat does not send its statements of reasons to the European Commission's DSA Transparency Database. That duty (Article 24(5) of the Digital Services Act) does not apply to micro and small enterprises (Article 19(1)), which korbat is, and a statement sent there cannot be taken back. Should korbat outgrow the exemption, this page will say from which day it sends them.",
  rulesLink: "The rules",
  exploreLink: "How Explore works",
} as const;
```

### Replace `infra/.env.example` (whole file)

```text
# Copy to infra/.env and change every password. Never commit infra/.env.
POSTGRES_USER=postgres
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=change-me-superuser
POSTGRES_DB=korbat
KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD=change-me-migrate
KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD=change-me-api
KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD=change-me-auth
# The database role of the contact point's watcher, notify (3f). infra/postgres/init/01-roles.sh makes it on a new data
# directory; on one that exists the README's Upgrading makes it once. notify's own settings are below, under 3f.
KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD=change-me-notify
# Valkey (the session cache and rate-limit counters) refuses every command without it.
REDIS_PASSWORD=change-me-redis

# Images. The formats korbat accepts: remove one to refuse it and keep its decoder blocked, for
# example after a security advisory against that decoder, then restart api and worker.
MEDIA_FORMATS=jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif
# Uploads are refused while a media volume has less free space than this many bytes (2 GiB). The
# volumes share a disk with Postgres, and a full disk stops the database.
MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES=2147483648
# The sweeper's pass that deletes images without a database row: on refuses when there are many of
# them (a database restored from an older snapshot looks like that), off skips it during a restore,
# force deletes them once you have checked.
MEDIA_RECONCILE=on

API_LOG_LEVEL=info
# Comma-separated browser origins allowed to call the API cross-origin. Empty in prod (same origin via Caddy).
API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:8081

# Auth. `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` fills the keys with random values and shares them with apps/api/.env.
# Origin the web app is served from (Caddy). Production: https://<your domain>.
API_APP_ORIGIN=http://localhost:8080
# Which header names the client: cloudflare when the tunnel is the only way in (the API then trusts
# cf-connecting-ip), caddy when Caddy's port is reachable directly. Never none behind a proxy.
API_TRUST_PROXY=caddy
API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY=change-me-key-auth-hmac
API_IP_HASH_KEY=change-me-key-ip-hash
API_TOTP_ENC_KEY=v1:change-me-key-totp
# Earlier TOTP keys, comma-separated, kept only while secrets they encrypted are still stored; a secret
# read with one is re-encrypted with API_TOTP_ENC_KEY.
API_TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS=
# Encrypts what a signed-out notifier leaves to be told about their notice: a name, an address and the token of the
# mails' link. Keep it secret and backed up as API_TOTP_ENC_KEY is: without it korbat can neither mail a notifier nor
# say who sent a notice.
API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY=v1:change-me-key-notifier
# Earlier notifier keys, comma-separated. A contact is never encrypted again, so a key stays here while a contact it
# encrypted is still stored.
API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS=
# Cloudflare's documented always-pass test secret. Production uses the secret of your Turnstile widget.
API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY=1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA
# Mailpit from compose.dev.yml. Production: the EU relay, e.g. smtps://user:pass@smtp-relay.example:465
API_SMTP_URL=smtp://mailpit:1025
API_MAIL_FROM="korbat <no-reply@korbat.local>"
API_TERMS_VERSION=draft-2026-09
# Who checks the phone number behind the verified badge: off turns the badge off, dev accepts the code
# 000000 (development only; production refuses it), vonage texts a real code through Vonage Verify with the
# key and secret from the Vonage dashboard (the runbook in the 1b design says how).
API_VERIFY_PROVIDER=off
# Whether the web app's account settings show the verified badge section: on or off. Set it together with
# API_VERIFY_PROVIDER: off while that is off, on once it is dev or vonage (a section shown without a provider
# answers every Send code with "Verification is not available"). The web image reads it as EXPO_PUBLIC_BADGE,
# which Expo inlines at export time.
WEB_BADGE=off
API_VONAGE_API_KEY=
API_VONAGE_API_SECRET=
# The sender name of the verification text: 1 to 18 characters, none of / { } : $.
API_VERIFY_BRAND=korbat
# Passkeys. The RP ID every passkey is bound to: empty means the host of API_APP_ORIGIN. It may instead be a parent
# domain of that host (korbat.example for app.korbat.example). The staff console does not use it: staff keys have their
# own RP ID. Production refuses an IP address or localhost. Choose it before the first passkey is added: changing it
# later strands every passkey.
API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID=
# The site name password managers show next to a korbat passkey: 1 to 64 printable characters; empty means korbat.
API_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME=

# The staff console: the origin staff open it at, served by Caddy's second site (port 8090 in its container). Empty
# switches the console off: every /api/staff path then answers 404. It must differ from API_APP_ORIGIN and never appear
# in API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS. In development it is localhost on the port compose.dev.yml publishes the console on
# (DEV_CONSOLE_PORT below); open it there, never at 127.0.0.1. Production: https://<the console's own hostname>, a
# hostname apart from the app's.
API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN=http://localhost:8090
# The RP ID staff keys are bound to: empty means the hostname of API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN, which production requires. Choose
# the console's hostname before the first staff key is enrolled: moving the console later means enrolling every key
# again.
API_CONSOLE_RP_ID=

# Moderation. The hour of the UTC day, 0 to 23, at which the day's decisions on reports and notices are released to those
# who sent them, in one batch, so that nobody can tell from a mail's minute when a decision was made; empty means 7.
API_MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR=7

# after the others of their lane, never below a less severe lane. off, the default, orders by lane and age alone.
API_MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN=off
# The retention job, which erases what is due and deletes kept image rows that nothing retains any more: on unless set

# what is late. off only for a restore window: README, Restoring, step 5
API_MODERATION_RETENTION=on

# Authorities' orders and the alert channel (3f). Whether the API judges the alert channel's health: on mails "Phone
# alerts are down" when the watcher's beat or a push is late; off (the default outside production) only skips that
# check, and the console's home says that phone alerts are switched off on this server. Leave it off until the
# contact-point mailbox exists (README, Upgrading).
API_NOTIFY=off
# The operator's Member State, as an ISO code of a state whose facts the contracts hold (Germany's, DE, is the worked
# example), from which the console tells an order from another Member State; and the published contact point for
# authorities, an address. Leave the contact point empty until the owner's list is done (README, Before going public):
# the home state is required once it is set. The migrate service reads the home state too, for staff.js order-open.
API_HOME_STATE=DE
API_CONTACT_POINT=
# The report hold (3f): while a report of an account's sealed images to the authorities is owed, a deletion of the
# account keeps its email address, and nothing else of it, for at most seven days, and its deletion mail says so. on is
# the default; off restores the purge that overwrites the address at once, and then a report needs the address taken
# before the account is deleted (README, Notifications and hand-overs).
API_REPORT_HOLD=on
# The edge's purge (3d): when an image stops being public, the API asks the network provider to drop its copies at the
# edge, by prefix, several images a request. off (the default) asks nothing, and the image's header is then
# the only bound on a copy. test is for the suites and is refused while APP_SITE is open. cloudflare needs the zone's
# id, an API token with the one permission Zone, Cache Purge (a secret: keep it as the keys above are, and it is in no
# log line), and the public hostname images are served under, without a scheme or a path (README, The edge).
API_EDGE_PURGE=off
API_EDGE_ZONE_ID=
API_EDGE_API_TOKEN=
API_EDGE_HOST=
# The recipients' count (3d): the transparency page and staff.js recipients count the accounts used each month and,
# while this is on, the readers without an account each day, by a keyed digest of the network and the browser's name
# under a random key that lives 26 hours and is written nowhere else. on is the default; off leaves readers without an
# account out, and the pages then say "at least" (README, The yearly edition).
API_RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT=on
# The audit head's daily value (3d): once a day after the dispatch hour the API publishes it on /transparency and mails
# it, with its place and hash, to the keeper's address below, the staff member who does not run the server; empty sends
# no mail. Its outside timestamp: off (the default), test (for the suites, refused while APP_SITE is open), or rfc3161
# with the https address of a timestamp authority the owner has chosen, which is sent the day's value and nothing else
# (README, The yearly edition).
API_HEAD_WITNESS=off
API_HEAD_WITNESS_URL=
API_HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL=
# The watcher and the push server run under the Compose profile notify, switched on here once the mailbox and the phones
# exist: COMPOSE_PROFILES=notify. Nothing below is needed for the stack to start while it is off. The mailbox: IMAP over
# TLS on port 993, an application password that can only read, and the name of the junk folder as the mail host names it.
# The publisher's ntfy token is also in infra/ntfy/server.yml; production refuses the example's.
# COMPOSE_PROFILES=notify

# NOTIFY_IMAP_USER=
# NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD=

# The push network's fixed subnet, which the app's and the console's sites refuse; Caddy is on that network with

# PUSH_SUBNET=172.16.91.0/24

APP_SITE=open

# The development stack's host ports, read only by infra/compose.dev.yml. Set one when another container

# DEV_PG_PORT=55432
```
