```text
# The staff console's port: API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN must name the same port on localhost (http://localhost:<port>).
# DEV_CONSOLE_PORT=8090
# DEV_SMTP_PORT=51025
# DEV_MAILPIT_PORT=58025
# 3f, with the profile notify: the push site, which a test client subscribes through, and ntfy's own port, which only
# `pnpm --filter @korbat/api notify:dev` publishes to (NOTIFY_PUSH_URL in apps/api/.env).
# DEV_PUSH_PORT=8091
# DEV_NTFY_PORT=2586
```

### Replace `infra/compose.yml` (whole file)

```yaml
name: korbat

x-logging: &logging
  driver: json-file
  options: { max-size: "20m", max-file: "5" }

x-node-common: &node-common
  restart: unless-stopped
  read_only: true
  tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
  security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
  logging: *logging

services:
  postgres:
    # PostgreSQL 18. From 18 on the image keeps the cluster under /var/lib/postgresql/<major>/docker, so
    # the volume is mounted one level up and a later major can pg_upgrade inside it. A cluster from the
    # earlier pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 16) is moved over by scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs.
    image: postgres:18.6-alpine@sha256:77f585114c32fbca283dc835b0596f4e52b51b4c6662d7810b2f4084f60a1873
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 1g
    memswap_limit: 1g
    pids_limit: 256
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
      KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD}
      KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD}
      KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD}
      # The contact point's watcher's role (3f), which 01-roles.sh makes on a new data directory. Not required: a stack
      # without the watcher runs without it.
      KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD:-}
    volumes:
      - pgdata18:/var/lib/postgresql
      - ./postgres/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    # watch: the watcher's own network to the database, which holds nothing else.
    networks: [data, watch]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER} -d ${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  redis:
    # Valkey, the BSD-licensed fork of Redis, under the service name the URLs already use. A password
    # is required: nothing on the data network may read the session cache without it.
    image: valkey/valkey:9.1.2-alpine@sha256:48332870af354a799964c0012ae1194a0bf2bf894eb508f945810596dc2d8d11
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 384m
    memswap_limit: 384m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      REDIS_PASSWORD: ${REDIS_PASSWORD:?set REDIS_PASSWORD in infra/.env}
    command: ["sh", "-c", "exec valkey-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy noeviction --requirepass $$REDIS_PASSWORD"]
    volumes:
    # A fresh volume: Valkey 9 cannot read the RDB format 12 that Redis 7.4 wrote into `redisdata`, and that
    # volume held only transient state (limits, codes in flight, cached sessions, queued image jobs).
      - valkeydata:/data
    networks: [data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "VALKEYCLI_AUTH=$$REDIS_PASSWORD valkey-cli ping | grep -q PONG"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  migrate:
    <<: *node-common
    restart: "no"
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/api/Dockerfile
    command: ["node", "dist/migrate.js"]
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: postgres://korbat_migrate:${KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      MIGRATIONS_DIR: /app/migrations
      # `staff.js enroll` runs here, as the migrator, the one role the running API never holds, and records on each link
      # the console's origin and relying party ID it is issued for. Empty, the console is off and enroll refuses.
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}
      CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}
      # 3f: staff.js order-open runs here too, and reads the home state (whether an order is cross-border) and the app's
      # origin (how a link is read, as the console's route reads it). Neither is required: enroll and the migrations run
      # without them, and order-open refuses with one sentence while either is empty.
      HOME_STATE: ${API_HOME_STATE:-}
      APP_ORIGIN: ${API_APP_ORIGIN:-}
    networks: [data]
    depends_on:
      postgres: { condition: service_healthy }

  api:
    <<: *node-common
    # The image's name, the one Compose gives it by default, written out: notify (3f) runs the same image, so it is
    # built once.
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/api/Dockerfile
      args:
        KORBAT_VERSION: ${KORBAT_VERSION:-0.0.0}
    mem_limit: 512m
    memswap_limit: 512m
    pids_limit: 256
    environment:
      # development or production, from infra/.env; production turns on the guards against test keys, plain-http
      # origins and a relay without TLS. The worker below always runs as production.
      NODE_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:?set KORBAT_ENV to development or production in infra/.env}
      PORT: "3000"
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      DATABASE_URL_API: postgres://korbat_api:${KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      DATABASE_URL_AUTH: postgres://korbat_auth:${KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      REDIS_URL: redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis:6379
      TRUSTED_ORIGINS: ${API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS:-}
      # Which header names the client: the stack refuses to start without a choice.
      TRUST_PROXY: ${API_TRUST_PROXY:?set API_TRUST_PROXY in infra/.env}
      # Auth settings. The stack refuses to start while any of these is missing from infra/.env.
      APP_ORIGIN: ${API_APP_ORIGIN:?set API_APP_ORIGIN in infra/.env}
      AUTH_HMAC_KEY: ${API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY:?set API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY in infra/.env}
      IP_HASH_KEY: ${API_IP_HASH_KEY:?set API_IP_HASH_KEY in infra/.env}
      TOTP_ENC_KEY: ${API_TOTP_ENC_KEY:?set API_TOTP_ENC_KEY in infra/.env}
      TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: ${API_TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS:-}
      # Encrypts a signed-out notifier's name and address; earlier keys stay accepted for decryption.
      NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY: ${API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY:?set API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY in infra/.env}
      NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: ${API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS:-}
      TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY: ${API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY:?set API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY in infra/.env}
      SMTP_URL: ${API_SMTP_URL:?set API_SMTP_URL in infra/.env}
      MAIL_FROM: ${API_MAIL_FROM:?set API_MAIL_FROM in infra/.env}
      TERMS_VERSION: ${API_TERMS_VERSION:?set API_TERMS_VERSION in infra/.env}
      # The verified badge's phone check. off (the default) hides the badge; vonage needs the two credentials.
      VERIFY_PROVIDER: ${API_VERIFY_PROVIDER:-off}
      VONAGE_API_KEY: ${API_VONAGE_API_KEY:-}
      VONAGE_API_SECRET: ${API_VONAGE_API_SECRET:-}
      VERIFY_BRAND: ${API_VERIFY_BRAND:-korbat}
      # Passkeys. Empty values leave the API's defaults: the host of APP_ORIGIN as the RP ID and korbat as the name.
      WEBAUTHN_RP_ID: ${API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID:-}
      WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME: ${API_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME:-}
      # The staff console, served by Caddy's second site: the origin staff open it at, and the RP ID staff keys are bound
      # to (empty means the console's hostname). An empty origin switches the console off: every /api/staff path then
      # answers 404. The migrate service gets the same two values for `staff.js enroll`.
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}
      CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}
      # Moderation: the UTC hour of the daily release of decisions to those who reported, the queue's emergency switch, and
      # the retention job's switch, which is off only for a restore window (README, Restoring, step 5).
      MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR: ${API_MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR:-7}
      MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN: ${API_MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN:-off}
      MODERATION_RETENTION: ${API_MODERATION_RETENTION:-on}
      # Authorities' orders (3f): whether the alert tick judges the alert channel's health. Empty means on in production;
      # off until the contact point's mailbox exists (README, Upgrading).
      NOTIFY: ${API_NOTIFY:-}
      # The operator's Member State, a state whose facts the contracts hold (DE is filled in), and the published contact
      # point for authorities. Both empty until the owner's list is done; the home state is required once the contact
      # point is set.
      HOME_STATE: ${API_HOME_STATE:-}
      CONTACT_POINT: ${API_CONTACT_POINT:-}
      # 3f Task 5: whether a deletion keeps an account's address, at most seven days, while a report of its sealed images
      # to the authorities is owed. Empty means on; off restores the purge that overwrites the address at once.
      REPORT_HOLD: ${API_REPORT_HOLD:-}
      # 3d: the app's site switch, Caddy's (3f), handed to the API too, which refuses a test adapter while the site is open.
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
      # 3d Task 3: the purge of an image's copies at the edge once it stops being public: off (empty, the default), test
      # (refused while APP_SITE is open) or cloudflare, which needs the zone's id, the API token with the one permission
      # Zone, Cache Purge, and the public hostname images are served under (README, The edge).
      EDGE_PURGE: ${API_EDGE_PURGE:-}
      EDGE_ZONE_ID: ${API_EDGE_ZONE_ID:-}
      EDGE_API_TOKEN: ${API_EDGE_API_TOKEN:-}
      EDGE_HOST: ${API_EDGE_HOST:-}
      # 3d Task 4: whether readers without an account are counted among the recipients, each day's by a keyed digest of
      # the network and the browser's name under a salt that lives 26 hours; on unless set to off (README, The yearly edition).
      RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT: ${API_RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT:-}
      # 3d Task 5: the audit head's daily value. Its outside timestamp: off (empty, the default), test (refused while
      # APP_SITE is open) or rfc3161, which needs the timestamp authority's https address; and the one address the
      # keeper's daily mail goes to, empty for none (README, The yearly edition).
      HEAD_WITNESS: ${API_HEAD_WITNESS:-}
      HEAD_WITNESS_URL: ${API_HEAD_WITNESS_URL:-}
      HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL: ${API_HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL:-}
      # Images. The API writes uploads and only reads what the worker stored.
      MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: /media/uploads
      MEDIA_STORE_DIR: /media/store
      MEDIA_FORMATS: ${MEDIA_FORMATS:-jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif}
      MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES: ${MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES:-2147483648}
      MEDIA_RECONCILE: ${MEDIA_RECONCILE:-on}
    volumes:
      - media-uploads:/media/uploads
      - media-store:/media/store:ro
    networks: [app, data]
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      redis: { condition: service_healthy }
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  # The image worker runs the decoder, the most exploitable code in the stack. It has no network at
  # all, no credentials and no capabilities: it reads uploads and writes the store, and that is
  # everything it can reach. The memory limit was sized on worst-case images (2b design, Research).
  worker:
    <<: *node-common
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/worker/Dockerfile
    network_mode: none
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    mem_limit: 768m
    memswap_limit: 768m
    cpus: 1.0
    pids_limit: 64
    tmpfs: ["/tmp:size=64m"]
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: /media/uploads
      MEDIA_STORE_DIR: /media/store
      MEDIA_FORMATS: ${MEDIA_FORMATS:-jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif}
    volumes:
      - media-uploads:/media/uploads:ro
      - media-store:/media/store
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/media/store/heartbeat', 'utf8')).at < 60000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 4

  # The contact point's watcher (3f design, section 5): the API's image with dist/notify.js, under the profile notify. It
  # reads the contact-point mailbox over IMAP and publishes the alerts to ntfy. On the network watch it reaches PostgreSQL
  # as korbat_notify, whose grants are four tables, and nothing else; on push it reaches ntfy. It never joins data, where
  # the API listens and the limit store is. It exits rather than hang, and Docker starts it again. No setting of it is
  # required by Compose: the program names the one it is missing and exits.
  notify:
    <<: *node-common
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["notify"]
    command: ["node", "dist/notify.js"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    # Measured in this image (3f Task 1): about 82 MB resident idle, a peak of 93 MB during a first read of 10,000 old
    # messages, which took 21 seconds and fell back to 81 MB; under this limit the container's peak was 85 MB, with no
    # kill. 128 MB keeps more than a third above that peak.
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:-production}
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      DATABASE_URL_NOTIFY: postgres://korbat_notify:${KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD:-}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_USER: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_USER:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK:-}
      NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN: ${NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN:-}
    # A fixed address on push (3f's review, operations3), which infra/ntfy/server.yml exempts from ntfy's request limit
    # (visitor-request-limit-exempt-hosts): ntfy lets any one address publish 60 times and then once every 5 seconds (lab
    # L1), which would hold an order's alert behind a flood of contact mail. It lies inside PUSH_SUBNET, at the top of
    # the range, which Docker hands out last; change it, and the file's line, with the subnet.
    networks:
      watch: {}
      push:
        ipv4_address: ${NOTIFY_PUSH_IP:-172.16.91.254}
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      ntfy: { condition: service_started }
    # The watcher writes the time of every round it ends; two minutes without one is a hang.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - Number(require('fs').readFileSync('/tmp/korbat-notify-beat', 'utf8')) < 120000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # The hand-over of one seal's files (3f design, sections 5 and 7.14), under the profile handover, started by the operator
  # alone: docker compose --profile handover run --rm -T -v <directory>:/handover handover < list > digests. The API's
  # image with dist/handover.js, which opens no database and no socket: no network at all, no credential, no capability,
  # the image store and (3d) the quarantine read-only, the quarantine looked in first. It has no bind mount here: the
  # directory for the archive is an argument of the command (an empty source would stop every Compose command of the
  # stack), on an encrypted volume owned by uid 1000, the image's user node, the only place it can write. No setting of
  # it is required.
  handover:
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["handover"]
    command: ["node", "dist/handover.js"]
    restart: "no"
    network_mode: none
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
    stdin_open: true
    volumes:
      - media-store:/media/store:ro
      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine:ro

  # The quarantine's mover (3d design, sections 5 and 7.1), under the profile quarantine, started by the operator alone:
  # docker compose -f infra/compose.yml --profile quarantine run --rm -T quarantine < list > receipt, with the list that
  # staff.js quarantine-list printed, and the receipt then recorded by staff.js quarantine-record (the README,
  # Quarantine). The API's image with dist/quarantine.js, which opens no database and no socket: no network at all, no
  # environment, no credential, no capability and a read-only root; the image store and the quarantine read-write, and
  # nothing else. Its two roots are arguments of its entry point, and it refuses to start without both; what follows the
  # service's name on the command line (--lost, --inventory) is appended to them. It is the one service that writes the
  # quarantine; handover reads it, and the api, migrate and worker services never mount it.
  quarantine:
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["quarantine"]
    entrypoint: ["node", "dist/quarantine.js", "/media/store", "/media/quarantine"]
    restart: "no"
    network_mode: none
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    stdin_open: true
    volumes:
      - media-store:/media/store
      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine

  # The push server (3f design, section 5), under the profile notify, never linked into korbat's programs: ntfy at its
  # pinned release, reading its users, rights and tokens from infra/ntfy/server.yml (git-ignored, made from
  # server.yml.example), mounted read-only, since Compose would blank the $2a$10$ of a password hash in a variable. Only
  # on push, which is internal: it has no route out, so nothing is forwarded upstream. Its cache and auth files are on its
  # volume, at /var/tmp, the one directory of the image its user may write to.
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.28.0@sha256:6ef4b819f722fccdc036af611c4774cfdc2de821ab74fdd48bbf4c9d6f8973da
    profiles: ["notify"]
    command: ["serve", "--config", "/etc/ntfy/server.yml"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    user: "1000:1000"
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ntfy-data:/var/tmp
    networks: [push]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:2586/v1/health"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 4

  # Caddy serves the web app on port 8080, proxying /api, the staff console on port 8090, proxying only /api/staff, and
  # (3f) the phones' push site on port 8091, proxying only the two topics' subscriptions to ntfy. It runs as its own
  # user, sees only the API and ntfy, and is the only thing cloudflared can reach. A client from the push network (ntfy,
  # the watcher) is refused 403 on the app's and the console's sites.
  caddy:
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: infra/caddy/Dockerfile
      args:
        EXPO_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY: ${WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY:?set WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY in infra/.env}
        KORBAT_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:?set KORBAT_ENV to development or production in infra/.env}
        TUNNEL: ${TUNNEL:-off}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_BADGE: ${WEB_BADGE:-off}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_EMAIL: ${WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL:?set WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL in infra/.env}
        # 3f: the terms' contact point for authorities and korbat's Member State; neither is required (Before going public).
        EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT: ${WEB_CONTACT_POINT:-}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE: ${WEB_HOME_STATE:-}
    depends_on:
      api: { condition: service_healthy }
    environment:
      # The push network's subnet, which the app's and the console's sites refuse (3f).
      PUSH_SUBNET: ${PUSH_SUBNET:-172.16.91.0/24}
      # The app's site, open (the default) or closed: closed answers 503 to every path while a restore is checked (3f,
      # section 7.17). Caddy reads it when it starts and refuses to start on any other value.
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
    volumes:
      - caddy-data:/data
      - caddy-config:/config
    networks: [edge, app, push]

  cloudflared:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.9.1@sha256:b269e8abd07a5bf6f3f4be65d5050b2174eca89c56a0241a8ff32a16aec454e4
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    logging: *logging
    profiles: ["tunnel"]
    command: ["tunnel", "--no-autoupdate", "run"]
    environment:
      TUNNEL_TOKEN: ${TUNNEL_TOKEN}
    networks: [edge]
    depends_on:
      - caddy

# cloudflared reaches only Caddy, Caddy reaches only the API and ntfy, and the API alone reaches the data services, but
# for the watcher's own network to PostgreSQL (3f).
networks:
  edge:
  app:
  data:
  # The watcher and PostgreSQL, nothing else. Not internal: the mail host's port 993 is reached through its gateway.
  watch:
  # ntfy, the watcher and Caddy. Internal: no route out. Its fixed subnet is what the app's and the console's sites refuse.
  push:
    internal: true
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: ${PUSH_SUBNET:-172.16.91.0/24}

volumes:
  # PostgreSQL 18. The earlier pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 16) stays until scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs has
  # moved it and you remove it by hand.
  pgdata18:
  valkeydata:
  # Uploads wait here for the worker and are deleted once processed. Nothing in it needs a backup.
  media-uploads:
  # The images korbat serves. Back it up together with the database.
  media-store:
  # 3d: the files of images sealed for good, moved out of the store by the quarantine service, on the host's encrypted
  # disk. It is in no backup, by decision: a restore never brings a destroyed file back. Owned by uid 1000, mode 0700, the
  # path the API's image makes (the README, Quarantine and Backups).
  media-quarantine:
  # Caddy's state, owned by its own user; the earlier root-owned caddydata and caddyconfig volumes can go.
  caddy-data:
  caddy-config:
  # ntfy's message cache and its auth database (3f). The cache is how a phone gets an alert published while its
  # connection was down; the auth database is rebuilt from infra/ntfy/server.yml at every start.
  ntfy-data:
```

### Replace `packages/contracts/src/orders.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { hex, sha256, sortedJson } from "./canonical";
import { EDGE_WORDS, EdgePurgeView } from "./media";
import { FORBIDDEN_FORMAT } from "./text";

// Authorities' orders and the alert channel (3f design, sections 6.1, 6.2, 10.1, 10.2 and 18, W.1 and W.4). This module
// imports nothing from the other modules of the contracts but text.ts, which imports nothing, and (3d Task 3) media.ts,
// which imports only text.ts, for the edge's numbers and the purge line of an order's item: moderation.ts reads its
// constants for the staff overview, staff.ts its step-up params, and the watcher (apps/api/src/notify), which imports the
// contracts and nothing of the API, renders its pushes from it.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the numbers

/**
 * The numbers of 3f, the same as the SQL function order_rules() returns, which a database test compares member by
 * member: one constant mirrors one function, as STANDING_RULES mirrors standing_rules(). Every function and view of 3f
 * reads its numbers from there, and every word of the console, the pushes and the mails from here. Each is a cautious
 * default flagged for the owner (3f design, section 2): one line to change in each place.
 */
export const ORDER_RULES = {
  /** A removal order's hour (TCO Art. 3(3)); a restart of its clock is a fresh one; a message's deadline as an order. */
  hourMinutes: 60,
  /** The console's target. It stays with 3d's purge at the edge, which is unconfirmed and can fail (3d design, row 13). */
  targetMinutes: 55,
  /** The most items one "Disable for an order" confirms, and the most links one request names. */
  itemsPerAction: 10,
  /** Order decisions of one staff account in 24 hours. */
  decisionsPerDay: 50,
  /** Order records one staff account opens in 24 hours. */
  recordsPerDay: 20,
  /** A removal order's computed hold, and its one extension. */
  holdDays: 43,
  holdExtensionDays: 42,
  /** Every staff account is alerted this long before a held notice is released. */
  holdWarningDays: 7,
  /** No shorter hold for a tick the command line has not confirmed; a number here would cap it. */
  unconfirmedHoldHours: null,
  /** How long what a removal order disabled is preserved: months from the disabling, and a margin of days. */
  preserveMonths: 6,
  preserveMarginDays: 1,
  /** How long a deletion keeps the address while a report is owed, and when an owed report is alerted. */
  reportHoldDays: 7,
  reportAlertHours: 24,
  /** A message read more than this long after it arrived is stale and raises no push. */
  staleHours: 2,
  /** While an unhandled message's first push is this young, a further message raises no first push of its own; 0 switches the bound off. */
  quietMinutes: 15,
  /** When an unanswered message rings every phone, and the first reminder of its deadline. */
  escalateMinutes: 15,
  remindMinutes: 45,
  /** When the channel reads as down, and how long a row is still owed its push. */
  channelDownMinutes: 3,
  pushOwedMinutes: 60,
  /** When the copy of the audit log's tail is overdue, and when a hand-over archive not destroyed is alerted. */
  copyOverdueHours: 48,
  handoverAlertDays: 7,
  /** How long a handled message, an order's records and a closed restore gap are kept. */
  messageKeepDays: 30,
  recordKeepYears: 3,
  gapKeepMonths: 12,
} as const;
export type OrderRules = typeof ORDER_RULES;

/** What the database never reads: the watcher's round, the alert tick's, and how long the tick tries a row's mail. */
export const ALERT_RULES = {
  pollSeconds: 20,
  tickSeconds: 30,
  mailRetryHours: 24,
} as const;

/**
 * 3d (design, sections 6.1, 7.1 and 8.2; W.7): a move of sealed files into the quarantine, or back to the image store, is
 * alerted once it has been due this long, and then daily (quarantine_due), as alert_steps() judges it: F's daily
 * threshold, make_interval(days => 1), which a database test holds to this number. The words that state it print it from
 * here, as the words of 3f print ORDER_RULES.
 */
export const QUARANTINE_RULES = {
  dueHours: 24,
} as const;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the contact point

/** The two folders the watcher reads: the inbox, and the folder the mail host files junk in. */
export const CONTACT_FOLDERS = ["inbox", "junk"] as const;
export type ContactFolder = (typeof CONTACT_FOLDERS)[number];

/** What a message at the contact point turned out to be; `order` is set only by opening an order from it. */
export const CONTACT_DISPOSITIONS = ["order", "referral", "first_order_notice", "preservation_request", "scrutiny_decision", "clarification", "not_an_order"] as const;
export type ContactDisposition = (typeof CONTACT_DISPOSITIONS)[number];
/** What the close route takes: every disposition but `order`. */
export const CONTACT_CLOSE_DISPOSITIONS = ["referral", "first_order_notice", "preservation_request", "scrutiny_decision", "clarification", "not_an_order"] as const satisfies readonly Exclude<ContactDisposition, "order">[];

/** The words of the Contact point screen for each disposition (W.1). */
export const DISPOSITION_LABELS: Record<ContactDisposition, string> = {
  order: "An order",
  referral: "Referral",
  first_order_notice: "Notice before a first order",
  preservation_request: "Request to preserve longer",
  scrutiny_decision: "Scrutiny decision",
  clarification: "About an order korbat holds",
  not_an_order: "Not an order",
};

/** The eight words of notify_state.error: why the watcher's last round failed. */
export const NOTIFY_ERRORS = ["imap_connect", "imap_timeout", "imap_tls", "imap_login", "imap_folder", "imap_protocol", "push_connect", "push_refused"] as const;
export type NotifyError = (typeof NOTIFY_ERRORS)[number];

/** Messages a page of the Contact point screen. */
export const CONTACT_PAGE_SIZE = 50;

const Instant = z.iso.datetime();

/** One message at the contact point, as the console reads it: no sender, no subject and no content exist to show. */
export const ContactMessage = z.strictObject({
  id: z.uuid(),
  folder: z.enum(CONTACT_FOLDERS),
  receivedAt: Instant,
  seenAt: Instant,
  stale: z.boolean(),
  disposition: z.enum(CONTACT_DISPOSITIONS).nullable(),
  handledAt: Instant.nullable(),
  /** The staff handle of whoever closed it, or null. */
  handledBy: z.string().nullable(),
  /** The orders opened from it. */
  orders: z.array(z.uuid()),
});
export type ContactMessage = z.infer<typeof ContactMessage>;

/** GET /api/staff/contact: the messages newest first by receivedAt, a page at a time. */
export const ContactPage = z.strictObject({
  items: z.array(ContactMessage).max(CONTACT_PAGE_SIZE),
  nextCursor: z.string().nullable(),
});
export type ContactPage = z.infer<typeof ContactPage>;

/** The list's query: after the cursor the API handed out, and only the messages without a disposition with open=1. */
export const ContactQuery = z.strictObject({
  cursor: z.string().min(1).max(200).optional(),
  open: z.literal("1").optional(),
});
export type ContactQuery = z.infer<typeof ContactQuery>;

/** POST /api/staff/contact/:message/close. */
export const ContactCloseRequest = z.strictObject({ disposition: z.enum(CONTACT_CLOSE_DISPOSITIONS) });
export type ContactCloseRequest = z.infer<typeof ContactCloseRequest>;

/** The channel's state on the console's home: up, down, the mailbox unreadable, or switched off on this server. */
export const ALERT_CHANNEL_STATES = ["ok", "down", "mailbox", "off"] as const;
export type AlertChannelState = (typeof ALERT_CHANNEL_STATES)[number];

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the alerts

/**
 * The closed list of alerts, the CHECK of alert_outbox.kind written from it: 3f's kinds, then 3c's and 3e's six, whose
 * mails stay their own and which gain a push, then 3d's.
 */
export const ALERT_KIND_LIST = [
  "contact_mail",
  "contact_mail_escalated",
  "order_due",
  "order_opened",
  "order_corrected",
  "order_effected",
  "order_reinstated",
  "order_unverified",
  "hold_ending",
  "report_owed",
  "handover_undestroyed",
  "copy_overdue",
  "copy_taken",
  "alert_channel_down",
  "mailbox_unreachable",
  "alert_test",
  "moderation_urgent",
  "moderation_waiting",
  "moderation_burst",
  "moderation_reads",
  "moderation_reveal",
  "moderation_csam_lifted",
  // 3d (design, section 10.1): its kinds, each a sentence to every staff account. Task 1: a move of sealed files that is
  // due (alert_steps(), daily) and files the quarantine's record says are lost (staff.js quarantine-record).
  "quarantine_due",
  "quarantine_lost",
  // Task 2: a released file still recorded in the quarantine (alert_steps(), daily), and an admin's release of sealed
  // images (after the release's commit, to every staff account, the admin who released included).
  "release_undestroyed",
  "seal_released",
  // Task 3: the outbox's job gave up on purges at the edge (its own row, under F's daily rule).
  "edge_purge_failed",
  // Task 5: the transparency job published a day's value without an outside timestamp, or found the day before without
  // a published value (each its own row, under F's daily rule).
  "head_unwitnessed",
  "head_missed",
] as const;
export type AlertKind = (typeof ALERT_KIND_LIST)[number];

export type AlertLeg = "push" | "mail";
/** The ntfy topic of a push: the phone on call, or every staff phone. A mail goes to every staff account whatever the scope. */
export type AlertScope = "on_call" | "all";

/** One kind's entry: its priority and scope, its legs, who renders its mail, and the names of its facts. */
export interface AlertKindEntry {
  readonly priority: 3 | 5;
  readonly scope: AlertScope;
  readonly legs: readonly AlertLeg[];
  /**
   * `sentence`: the mail is the kind's own entry of ALERT_TEXTS, which the alert tick can mail again from the row's facts;
   * `own`: a mail of 3c or 3e that says more than the facts hold, which only staffAlert sends; null: pushed only.
   */
  readonly mail: "sentence" | "own" | null;
  /** The names of the row's facts: counts and times, at most six. */
  readonly facts: readonly string[];
}

const both: readonly AlertLeg[] = ["push", "mail"];
const sentenceKind = (priority: 3 | 5, scope: AlertScope, facts: readonly string[]): AlertKindEntry => ({ priority, scope, legs: both, mail: "sentence", facts });
const ownKind = (priority: 3 | 5, scope: AlertScope, facts: readonly string[]): AlertKindEntry => ({ priority, scope, legs: both, mail: "own", facts });

/**
 * Each kind's facts under the names the sentences print. `order_opened` carries `unknown` (1 for an order opened without
 * a time of receipt, else 0) beside its count and its deadline, so its sentence can tell "No deadline runs" from "Its
 * deadline is unknown"; `order_effected` carries `urgent` the same way.
 */
export const ALERT_KINDS: Record<AlertKind, AlertKindEntry> = {
  contact_mail: sentenceKind(5, "on_call", ["receivedAt", "dueAt"]),
  contact_mail_escalated: sentenceKind(5, "all", ["receivedAt", "dueAt"]),
  order_due: sentenceKind(5, "all", ["dueAt", "minutesLeft", "itemsOpen"]),
  order_opened: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["items", "dueAt", "unknown"]),
  order_corrected: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count", "at"]),
  order_effected: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["items", "at", "itemsOpen", "urgent"]),
  order_reinstated: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["at"]),
  order_unverified: sentenceKind(5, "all", ["count", "textsMissing", "holdsOpen", "oldestAt"]),
  hold_ending: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count", "at"]),
  report_owed: sentenceKind(5, "all", ["count", "oldestAt"]),
  handover_undestroyed: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count"]),
  copy_overdue: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["hours"]),
  copy_taken: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["at", "rows"]),
  alert_channel_down: { priority: 3, scope: "all", legs: ["mail"], mail: "sentence", facts: ["since"] },
  mailbox_unreachable: sentenceKind(5, "all", ["since"]),
  alert_test: { priority: 3, scope: "all", legs: ["push"], mail: null, facts: ["at"] },
  moderation_urgent: ownKind(5, "on_call", ["count", "oldestAt"]),
  moderation_waiting: ownKind(3, "all", ["count"]),
  moderation_burst: ownKind(3, "all", ["count"]),
  moderation_reads: ownKind(3, "all", ["limit"]),
  moderation_reveal: ownKind(3, "all", ["at"]),
  moderation_csam_lifted: ownKind(3, "all", ["at"]),
  quarantine_due: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count", "oldestAt"]),
  quarantine_lost: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count", "at"]),
  release_undestroyed: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count", "oldestAt"]),
  seal_released: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["at", "posts", "uploads"]),
  edge_purge_failed: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["count", "oldestAt"]),
  head_unwitnessed: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["day"]),
  head_missed: sentenceKind(3, "all", ["day"]),
};

/** The kinds the watcher publishes: every kind with a push leg. */
export const PUSH_KINDS: readonly AlertKind[] = ALERT_KIND_LIST.filter((kind) => ALERT_KINDS[kind].legs.includes("push"));
/** The kinds whose mail is their push's sentence, which the alert tick mails from the row. */
export const SENTENCE_MAIL_KINDS: readonly AlertKind[] = ALERT_KIND_LIST.filter((kind) => ALERT_KINDS[kind].mail === "sentence");

/** The facts of a row: counts, and instants as ISO strings in UTC. */
export type AlertFacts = Readonly<Record<string, number | string>>;

/**
 * A fact that is a day (3d Task 5's head alerts): the row holds the day's first instant, as it holds every time, and
 * renderAlert prints it as the day itself ("2026-10-16", rule 7 of the 3d design's section 18), never as a time of day.
 */
export const isDayFact = (name: string): boolean => name === "day";

/** A fact that is a time: `at`, `since`, a name that ends in At, or a day. Every other fact is a count. */
export const isTimeFact = (name: string): boolean => name === "at" || name === "since" || name.endsWith("At") || isDayFact(name);

/** What a part of a sentence is printed under: a fact present or missing, above zero, or equal to 1 or not. */
export interface AlertCondition {
  readonly fact: string;
  readonly is: "present" | "absent" | "positive" | "one" | "not_one";
}
/** A part of a sentence, printed when its condition holds; the parts printed are joined with a space. */
export interface AlertPart {
  readonly text: string;
  /** One condition, or several that must all hold. */
  readonly when?: AlertCondition | readonly AlertCondition[];
}
/** A kind's words: the title, the sentence in parts, and for a kind whose mail is its sentence the mail's line of what to do. */
export interface AlertText {
  readonly title: string;
  readonly sentence: readonly AlertPart[];
  readonly todo: string | null;
}

const NOT_LISTED = 'An order you find there is opened in the console under Orders, with "The message is not listed".';
const KEY_TOLD = "Every staff account gets this. If it was confirmed with your key and not by you, someone else holds your key: tell the operator at once.";
const one = (text: string): readonly AlertPart[] => [{ text }];

 * title and the sentence; a mail whose kind's mail is its sentence has the title as its subject after "korbat: ", and

/** A placeholder in braces: a fact's name, or a member of ORDER_RULES, of QUARANTINE_RULES or (3d Task 3) of EDGE_WORDS. */
const PLACEHOLDER = /[{]([a-zA-Z]+)[}]/g;

/** Every placeholder a kind's words name, each once. */
export function alertPlaceholders(kind: AlertKind): string[] {
  const text = ALERT_TEXTS[kind];
  const words = [text.title, ...text.sentence.map((part) => part.text), text.todo ?? ""].join(" ");
  return [...new Set([...words.matchAll(PLACEHOLDER)].map((found) => found[1]!))];
}

/** The form of a time in a row's facts: an instant in UTC with up to six decimals of a second. */
export const ALERT_TIME = /^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}([.][0-9]{1,6})?Z$/;

const two = (n: number) => String(n).padStart(2, "0");

/** An alert's time (rule 5 of section 18): "14:05 UTC", with the day before it when it is not the day of `now` in UTC. */
export function alertTime(iso: string, now: Date): string {
  const at = new Date(iso);
  const clock = `${two(at.getUTCHours())}:${two(at.getUTCMinutes())} UTC`;
  const day = `${at.getUTCFullYear()}-${two(at.getUTCMonth() + 1)}-${two(at.getUTCDate())}`;
  const today = `${now.getUTCFullYear()}-${two(now.getUTCMonth() + 1)}-${two(now.getUTCDate())}`;
  return day === today ? clock : `${day} ${clock}`;
}

/** Whether a part's condition, or every one of its conditions, holds for the facts. */
function holds(when: AlertPart["when"], facts: AlertFacts): boolean {
  if (when === undefined) return true;
  if (Array.isArray(when)) return when.every((condition: AlertCondition) => holds(condition, facts));
  const condition = when as AlertCondition;
  const value = facts[condition.fact];
  switch (condition.is) {
    case "present":
      return value !== undefined;
    case "absent":
      return value === undefined;
    case "positive":
      return typeof value === "number" && value > 0;
    case "one":
      return value === 1;
    case "not_one":
      return value !== 1;
  }
}

/** The facts held to the kind's names and kinds: a time where the name is a time's, a whole number elsewhere. */
function checkFacts(kind: AlertKind, facts: AlertFacts): void {
  const names = ALERT_KINDS[kind].facts;
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(facts)) {
    if (!names.includes(name)) throw new Error(`alert ${kind}: the fact ${name} is not one of its facts`);
    if (isTimeFact(name) ? typeof value !== "string" || !ALERT_TIME.test(value) : typeof value !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(value)) {
      throw new Error(`alert ${kind}: the fact ${name} is not ${isTimeFact(name) ? "a time" : "a count"}`);
    }
  }
}

/**
 * A kind's title, sentence and line of what to do, filled from the facts, ORDER_RULES, QUARANTINE_RULES and EDGE_WORDS. A time
 * prints as alertTime does at `now`, and a day as the date of its instant in UTC. A placeholder with nothing to fill it, a
 * fact of another kind and a fact of the wrong form throw: an alert never goes out with a hole or with anything but
 * counts and times in it.
 */
export function renderAlert(kind: AlertKind, facts: AlertFacts, now: Date): { title: string; sentence: string; todo: string | null } {
  checkFacts(kind, facts);
  const rules = { ...ORDER_RULES, ...QUARANTINE_RULES, ...EDGE_WORDS } as Record<string, number | null>;
  const fill = (text: string) =>
    text.replace(PLACEHOLDER, (_match, name: string) => {
      const value = facts[name];
      if (value !== undefined) return typeof value === "string" ? (isDayFact(name) ? value.slice(0, 10) : alertTime(value, now)) : String(value);
      const rule = Object.hasOwn(rules, name) ? rules[name] : undefined;
      if (typeof rule === "number") return String(rule);
      throw new Error(`alert ${kind}: nothing fills {${name}}`);
    });
  const text = ALERT_TEXTS[kind];
  return {
    title: fill(text.title),
    sentence: text.sentence
      .filter((part) => holds(part.when, facts))
      .map((part) => fill(part.text))
      .join(" "),
    todo: text.todo === null ? null : fill(text.todo),
  };
}

It holds IP addresses, and a phone number the account verified, only as keyed hashes that identify nobody outside korbat; a device's hash is deleted 30 days after the device was last seen. korbat also holds, and has not produced here, the times and device types of the account's sign-ins.",
} as const;

/**
 * The digest that a later step of a notification record (its answer, an event) and every step of a production hold in
 * their audit row in place of the facts (10.5): the SHA-256, in hex, of the record's row at that step in the canonical
 * JSON (canonical.ts), as the database printed it. The chain proves the record existed and was not changed afterwards,
 * and `staff.js records --verify` recomputes it from the row, without the audit log ever naming the person.
 */
export async function recordDigestOf(row: unknown): Promise<string> {
  return hex(await sha256(sortedJson(row)));
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the requests (10.2, 10.3)

/** A uuid in the lower case PostgreSQL writes: the one spelling a hashed param may take. */
const LowerUuid = z.uuid().regex(/^[0-9a-f-]+$/, { message: "a uuid in lower case" });

/** Whether a text holds a control character: C0, DEL or C1. */
const hasControl = (text: string) =>
  [...text].some((char) => {
    const code = char.codePointAt(0)!;
    return code < 32 || (code >= 127 && code < 160);
  });
/** Whether a string is whole text, with no half of a surrogate pair. */
const isWellFormed = (text: string) => (text as string & { isWellFormed(): boolean }).isWellFormed();

/**
 * One line typed from an order's document: an authority's name, a reference, a link. Stored as written or refused: well
 * formed, no control character, none of the invisible direction and spacing characters, some text, at most `max`
 * characters as PostgreSQL counts them. It is an outsider's text, and the console draws it as such.
 */
const orderLine = (max: number) =>
  z
    .string()
    // A character outside the basic plane is two UTF-16 units, so this bound never refuses what the count below accepts.
    .max(2 * max)
    .refine(isWellFormed, { message: "half of a surrogate pair is not text" })
    .refine((text) => !hasControl(text), { message: "control characters are not allowed" })
    .refine((text) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(text), { message: "invisible direction and spacing characters are not allowed" })
    .refine((text) => text.trim().length > 0, { message: "some text is needed" })
    .refine((text) => Array.from(text).length <= max, { message: `at most ${max} characters` });
export const OrderAuthority = orderLine(ORDER_TEXT_LIMITS.name);
export const OrderReference = orderLine(ORDER_TEXT_LIMITS.name);
export const OrderLinkText = orderLine(ORDER_TEXT_LIMITS.link);

const distinct = (values: readonly string[]) => new Set(values).size === values.length;
const orderLinks = (min: number) => z.array(OrderLinkText).min(min).max(ORDER_RULES.itemsPerAction).refine(distinct, { message: "a link is named once" });

/**
 * POST /api/staff/orders (7.4). sectionC is required and has no default: the form's third choice, "I cannot tell", is
 * sent as true. A named message comes with the channel mailbox, which the database forces too. The withholding is true
 * for a removal order and whenever Section C is set, so no request can hold a notice on a post its author sees; an order
 * to provide information names no post, so it does not withhold unless Section C forces it. It takes no link; the other
 * two kinds take one to itemsPerAction.
 */

  .strictObject({
    messageId: z.uuid().nullable(),
    channel: z.enum(ORDER_CHANNELS),
    kind: z.enum(ORDER_KINDS),
    memberState: MemberStateCode,
    authority: OrderAuthority,
    reference: OrderReference,
    links: orderLinks(0),
    sectionC: z.boolean(),
    emergency: z.boolean(),
    withholdFromAuthor: z.boolean(),
  })
  .superRefine((request, ctx) => {
    if (request.messageId !== null && request.channel !== "mailbox") ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["channel"], message: "an order opened from a message arrived in the mailbox" });
    if ((request.kind === "tco_removal" || request.sectionC) && !request.withholdFromAuthor) {
      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["withholdFromAuthor"], message: "a removal order, and an order whose author must not be told, keeps the post from its author" });
    }
    if (request.kind === "dsa_art10" && !request.sectionC && request.withholdFromAuthor) {
      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["withholdFromAuthor"], message: "an order to provide information names no post to withhold" });
    }
    if (request.kind === "dsa_art10" ? request.links.length > 0 : request.links.length === 0) {
      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["links"], message: "an order to provide information takes no link; the other kinds take at least one" });
    }
  });

/** POST /api/staff/orders/:order/items: one to itemsPerAction more links, up to ORDER_ITEMS_MAX in all. */
export const OrderItemsRequest = z.strictObject({ links: orderLinks(1) });
export type OrderItemsRequest = z.infer<typeof OrderItemsRequest>;

/**
 * What a correction changes (7.4): only the members to change, at least one. crossBorder is the API's, set with
 * memberState. closeItems closes open items, each with one reason, no item twice. Section C set never comes with the
 * withholding unset.
 */
export const OrderCorrectFacts = z
  .strictObject({
    kind: z.enum(ORDER_KINDS).optional(),
    memberState: MemberStateCode.optional(),
    authority: OrderAuthority.optional(),
    reference: OrderReference.optional(),
    channel: z.enum(ORDER_CHANNELS).optional(),
    sectionC: z.boolean().optional(),
    emergency: z.boolean().optional(),
    withholdFromAuthor: z.boolean().optional(),

      .array(z.strictObject({ itemId: LowerUuid, reason: z.enum(ORDER_ITEM_CLOSE_REASONS) }))
      .min(1)
      .max(ORDER_RULES.itemsPerAction)
      .refine((items) => distinct(items.map((item) => item.itemId)), { message: "an item is closed once" })
      .optional(),
  })
  .refine((facts) => Object.keys(facts).length > 0, { message: "a correction changes something" })
  .refine((facts) => !(facts.sectionC === true && facts.withholdFromAuthor === false), { message: "an order whose author must not be told keeps the post from its author", path: ["withholdFromAuthor"] });
export type OrderCorrectFacts = z.infer<typeof OrderCorrectFacts>;

/** The step-up params of order_corrected, asked only under the rule admin: the request's facts (10.3). */
export const OrderCorrectedParams = z.strictObject({ facts: OrderCorrectFacts });
export type OrderCorrectedParams = z.infer<typeof OrderCorrectedParams>;

/** Every ground a console event takes: an Annex III's and a closing's, each once. A param is never a free string. */
const CONSOLE_EVENT_GROUNDS = [...ANNEX3_GROUNDS, ...ORDER_CLOSE_GROUNDS] as const;

/**
 * The step-up params of order_event_recorded (10.3): the kind, its ground (one of its kind's list, or null for a kind

 * takes.

export const OrderEventRecordedParams = z
  .strictObject({ kind: z.enum(ORDER_CONSOLE_EVENTS), ground: z.enum(CONSOLE_EVENT_GROUNDS).nullable(), messageId: LowerUuid.nullable() })
  .superRefine((params, ctx) => {
    const grounds = orderEventGrounds(params.kind);
    if (grounds === null ? params.ground !== null : params.ground === null || !grounds.includes(params.ground)) {
      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["ground"], message: grounds === null ? "this event has no ground" : "a ground of this event's list" });
    }
    const needs = params.kind === "clarification_received" || params.kind === "hold_extended";
    const may = needs || params.kind === "grounds_ceased";
    if ((needs && params.messageId === null) || (!may && params.messageId !== null)) {
      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["messageId"], message: needs ? "this event names the message it came in" : "this event names no message" });
    }
  });

      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["withholdFromAuthor"], message: "a removal order, and an order whose author must not be told, keeps the post from its author" });
    }
    if (params.kind === "tco_removal" && params.urgent) ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["urgent"], message: "a removal order is given effect without a check first: urgent means nothing for it" });

    if (posts.some((post, i) => i > 0 && posts[i - 1]! >= post)) ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["items"], message: "the items are sorted by post, without repeats" });
```

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { MEASURE_KINDS, RULE_IDS } from "./moderation";
import { ANNEX3_GROUNDS, ORDER_GROUNDS } from "./orders";

// The public figures (3d design, sections 2 rows 1 to 3 and 8, 6.4, 7.5, 7.6, 10.1 and 10.6; Task 4) and the audit head's
// daily value (sections 2 row 9, 6.5 and 7.7; Task 5). This module
// imports moderation.ts and orders.ts for closed lists alone, and nothing imports it but the index, so it loads last.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the numbers

/**
 * The mirror of the SQL function transparency_rules(), which a database test holds member for column: the floor under
 * which a count prints as "1 to 9" and a row is folded into "other", the rounding of every other count, the day on which
 * a year's edition is due (1 March of the next year, in UTC) and the method's version. Each is the owner's to change
 * (section 2, rows 2 and 3), in that function and here.
 */
export const TRANSPARENCY_RULES = {
  floor: 10,
  roundTo: 10,
  dueMonth: 3,
  dueDay: 1,
  method: 1,
} as const;

/**
 * A count as the public reads it, exactly as the SQL function band() prints it (a table test holds the two equal over 0
 * to 200): 0 for zero, "1 to 9" under the floor, otherwise "about" and the count rounded to the nearest ten, halves
 * upward. It is the only place a count becomes public text.
 */
export function band(n: number): string {
  if (!Number.isInteger(n) || n < 0) throw new Error(`band takes a count, not ${n}`);
  if (n === 0) return "0";
  if (n < TRANSPARENCY_RULES.floor) return "1 to 9";
  const step = TRANSPARENCY_RULES.roundTo;
  return `about ${Math.floor((n + step / 2) / step) * step}`;
}

/**
 * The recipients' count (7.5), method 1: a month's sketch of signed-in accounts and a day's sketch of signed-out readers,
 * the day's salt living `saltHours`, every sketch dying `sketchDays` after its first write if the month's close never
 * took it, the user agent cut at `userAgentBytes` before it is digested, and the figure the average of `months` full
 * months. A crawler is left out only by its own words: one pattern on the agent, nothing guessed about a reader.
 */
export const RECIPIENT_RULES = {
  method: 1,
  months: 6,
  saltHours: 26,
  sketchDays: 70,
  userAgentBytes: 256,
  crawler: /bot|crawl|spider|slurp/i,
} as const;

/**
 * The seven routes of the social module that answer without a session (7.5): a post, its thread, the two public
 * timelines, a profile, its posts and its replies. A signed-out GET of one of them feeds the day's sketch. The image
 * route and the page status are not counted. A route-table test fails when the social module gains a signed-out read
 * that is neither here nor refused by name in that test.
 */
export const RECIPIENT_READ_ROUTES = [
  "GET /api/posts/:id",
  "GET /api/posts/:id/thread",
  "GET /api/timeline/latest",
  "GET /api/timeline/explore",
  "GET /api/profiles/:handle",
  "GET /api/profiles/:handle/posts",
  "GET /api/profiles/:handle/replies",
] as const;

/** Why a version of a year's edition was stored (the CHECK of transparency_editions.reason): version 1 alone is `first`. */
export const EDITION_REASONS = ["first", "hold_ended", "correction"] as const;
export type EditionReason = (typeof EDITION_REASONS)[number];

/**
 * The audit head's daily value (3d design, sections 2 row 9, 6.5, 7.7 and 10.1; Task 5): the tag its digest begins with
 * (head_value(), "korbat.head.v2", then the day, the place and the hash, each after a line feed), the days the public
 * route and the page show, how long the witness is waited for, and the largest token kept. What only the API reads.
 */
export const HEAD_RULES = {
  tag: "korbat.head.v2",
  shownDays: 30,
  witnessTimeoutMs: 10_000,
  tokenMaxBytes: 16_384,
} as const;

/** A row of head_publications (the CHECK of its kind): the day's value, or the public mark of a restore. */
export const HEAD_KINDS = ["head", "restore"] as const;
export type HeadKind = (typeof HEAD_KINDS)[number];

/** Who was asked to witness a value (the CHECK of its witness): nobody while HEAD_WITNESS is off, else the adapter's name. */
export const HEAD_WITNESSES = ["none", "rfc3161", "test"] as const;
export type HeadWitness = (typeof HEAD_WITNESSES)[number];

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the public answers

/** A banded count, as band() prints it: never a number under ten, never an exact one. */
const Band = z.string().regex(/^(0|1 to 9|about [1-9][0-9]*0)$/);
/** A day, as the public pages print one: 2026-03-01. */
const Day = z.string().regex(/^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$/);

/** One row of a table split by a label from a closed list: what is folded under the floor is the row `other`. */
const rows = <const L extends readonly [string, ...string[]]>(labels: L) => z.array(z.strictObject({ label: z.enum([...labels, "other"]), count: Band }));

/**
 * The labels of each table (6.4): a rule's id or `law` for the ground; a measure's kind; an intake's kind, a user's
 * report under the rules and a notice of illegality apart; an appeal's result; a re-examination's answer; one of 3e's six
 * account measures; an upload's end (from Task 7).
 */
export const FIGURE_LABELS = {
  grounds: [...RULE_IDS, "law"],
  measures: MEASURE_KINDS,
  intakes: ["rules", "illegal", "finding", "automated"],
  appeals: ["kept", "partly_reversed", "reversed"],
  reexaminations: ["action", "no_action"],
  accountMeasures: ["strike", "suspend", "terminate", "retire_handle", "warn_reporting", "restrict_reporting"],
} as const;

/**
 * The order section (6.4 step 5): the figures F 7.18 lists for tco-counts, as numbers and without the issuing state,
 * since the Regulation asks for numbers (section 2, row 4). A figure the rows can no longer give is null, which the page
 * prints as "not recorded", as tco-counts does, and never as 0.
 */
export const OrderFigures = z.strictObject({
  received: z.strictObject({ total: z.number().int().min(0), crossBorder: z.number().int().min(0) }).nullable(),
  itemsDisabled: z.number().int().min(0).nullable(),
  minutes: z
    .strictObject({
      list: z.array(z.number().int().nullable()),
      outside: z.number().int().min(0),
      withoutReceipt: z.number().int().min(0),
      open: z.number().int().min(0),
    })
    .nullable(),
  annex3: z.strictObject(Object.fromEntries(ANNEX3_GROUNDS.map((ground) => [ground, z.number().int().min(0)])) as Record<(typeof ANNEX3_GROUNDS)[number], z.ZodNumber>).nullable(),
  scrutiny: z.strictObject({ requested: z.number().int().min(0), annulled: z.number().int().min(0), upheld: z.number().int().min(0) }).nullable(),
  reinstated: z.strictObject(Object.fromEntries(ORDER_GROUNDS.map((ground) => [ground, z.number().int().min(0)])) as Record<(typeof ORDER_GROUNDS)[number], z.ZodNumber>).nullable(),
  authorityAccess: z.number().int().min(0).nullable(),
  terroristWithoutOrder: z.number().int().min(0),
  referralsClosed: z.number().int().min(0),
});
export type OrderFigures = z.infer<typeof OrderFigures>;

/**
 * A stored edition's figures, as transparency_figures() computes them (6.4): banded strings only, but the order section's
 * numbers. `uploads` comes with Task 7 and stays optional for good: an edition stored before it never changes, so it
 * never gains the member. `orders` is absent when no countable order exists, and nothing says whether one was left out.
 * `recipients` is two bounds, one while signed-out readers are not counted, or "not recorded" before six months are.
 */
export const TransparencyFigures = z.strictObject({
  restrictions: z.strictObject({ byGround: rows(FIGURE_LABELS.grounds), byMeasure: rows(FIGURE_LABELS.measures), total: Band }),
  noBreach: Band,
  intakes: rows(FIGURE_LABELS.intakes),
  appeals: rows(FIGURE_LABELS.appeals),
  reexaminations: rows(FIGURE_LABELS.reexaminations),
  accountMeasures: rows(FIGURE_LABELS.accountMeasures),
  automated: z.strictObject({
    findings: rows(RULE_IDS),
    measures: rows(RULE_IDS),
    /** Of the findings under R1, how many a person's final decision had restricted by the due day: only on a base of ten or more. */
    r1: z.strictObject({ base: Band, restricted: Band }).optional(),
  }),
  uploads: rows(["refused", "report", "no_report", "open"]).optional(),
  orders: OrderFigures.optional(),
  recipients: z.union([z.literal("not recorded"), z.strictObject({ low: Band, high: Band.optional() })]),
});
export type TransparencyFigures = z.infer<typeof TransparencyFigures>;

/** One stored version of a year's edition, as GET /api/public/transparency answers it. */
const EditionVersion = z.strictObject({
  version: z.number().int().min(1),
  publishedOn: Day,
  /** The day the next version was published, which replaced this one. */
  replacedOn: Day,
  reason: z.enum(EDITION_REASONS),
  figures: TransparencyFigures,
});

/**
 * GET /api/public/transparency (10.6): every year's newest version, newest year first, with its older versions. It reads
 * transparency_editions alone (the recipients' bounds are inside the figures) and nothing of a person.
 */
export const PublicTransparency = z.strictObject({
  editions: z.array(
    z.strictObject({
      year: z.number().int(),
      version: z.number().int().min(1),
      publishedOn: Day,
      method: z.number().int(),
      reason: z.enum(EDITION_REASONS),
      figures: TransparencyFigures,
      older: z.array(EditionVersion),
    }),
  ),
});
export type PublicTransparency = z.infer<typeof PublicTransparency>;

/**
 * GET /api/public/facts (10.6): what is switched on now, read from the API's settings: booleans, names, days and numbers,
 * never a token, a zone, a host or an address. Until the tasks that build them, the R1 check and the comparison with known
 * material print off; the edge prints its adapter (Task 3) and the head's witness its own (Task 5, HEAD_WITNESS). `dpia` and `dpiaActs` are each a
 * tool's own impact assessment and the one that covers its measure, so no date of one tool stands over another.
 */
export const PublicFacts = z.strictObject({
  r1: z.strictObject({
    state: z.enum(["off", "flags", "withholds"]),
    test: z.boolean(),
    model: z.string().nullable(),
    digest: z.string().nullable(),
    threshold: z.number().nullable(),
    thresholdVersion: z.number().int().nullable(),
    publisherClaim: z.string().nullable(),
    dpia: Day.nullable(),
    dpiaActs: Day.nullable(),
  }),
  match: z.strictObject({
    state: z.enum(["off", "alerts", "seals"]),
    test: z.boolean(),
    source: z.string().nullable(),
    dpia: Day.nullable(),
    dpiaActs: Day.nullable(),
  }),
  edge: z.strictObject({ on: z.boolean(), test: z.boolean() }),
  witness: z.strictObject({ on: z.boolean(), test: z.boolean() }),
  /** Whether signed-out readers are counted (RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT). */
  recipientsSignedOut: z.boolean(),
});
export type PublicFacts = z.infer<typeof PublicFacts>;

/** A head's value: the hex SHA-256 of the tag, the day, the place and the hash, which shows neither of the last two. */
const HeadValue = z.string().regex(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
/** The outside witness's token as base64, at most HEAD_RULES.tokenMaxBytes bytes before it was encoded. */
const HeadToken = z
  .string()
  .max(Math.ceil(HEAD_RULES.tokenMaxBytes / 3) * 4)
  .regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9+/]+={0,2}$/);

/**
 * GET /api/public/head (10.6): the published rows of the last HEAD_RULES.shownDays days, newest first, each a day's value or
 * a restore's mark. `witness` reads `none` for a row without a token, whatever was asked; `retiredOn` is the day a restore
 * retired the value; `lastDay`, on a restore's row alone, is the day of the newest published value that still fits the
 * restored log ([tr.restore]), null on every other row. Never the place, the hash or a time of day.
 */
export const PublicHead = z.strictObject({
  days: z.array(
    z.strictObject({
      day: Day,
      kind: z.enum(HEAD_KINDS),
      value: HeadValue,
      witness: z.enum(HEAD_WITNESSES),
      token: HeadToken.nullable(),
      retiredOn: Day.nullable(),
      lastDay: Day.nullable(),
    }),
  ),
});
export type PublicHead = z.infer<typeof PublicHead>;
```
